items.title: [Feature] Support per-model Hugging Face and ModelScope sources
items.body:
## Overview

Some deployments use a main model from ModelScope and a draft model from Hugging Face. The global `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` switch cannot express this combination. This PR adds explicit, per-model Hub selection.

## Claims

- Support `hf://owner/model` and `modelscope://owner/model` for the model, tokenizer, and speculative draft model.
- Preserve existing bare `owner/model` IDs and local paths; explicit prefixes override the global Hub setting without cross-Hub fallback.
- Resolve cross-repository `auto_map` code through the selected Hub, respecting `code_revision` and `trust_remote_code`.

```sh
vllm serve modelscope://Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"hf://RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

## Validation

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/transformers_utils/test_model_hub.py -q
```

33 tests passed, also with `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True`. Tests cover mixed sources, revisions, custom code, caching, and download failures. Ruff, Markdown lint, and `git diff --check` passed.

GPU end-to-end regressions are included but have not been run locally. Model evaluation is pending.

## Details

Explicit references resolve to local SDK snapshots before loading. Custom code uses a local overlay without modifying Hub caches. No new source-selection flags or environment variables are introduced.

Open-PR searches found no direct match for per-model HF/ModelScope selection; final duplicate review remains pending.

items.title: [Multimodal][Model Runner V2] Support encoder-decoder plugins whose encoder reads the prompt (T5Gemma 2)
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Three small framework changes let encoder-decoder models whose encoder reads the prompt tokens (T5-style text encoders) run as vLLM plugins. This follows the guidance to add new encoder-decoder models as plugins, from the [V1 guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/usage/v1_guide/#encoder-decoder-models) and the review on vllm-project/vllm#32617. The motivating plugin is [vllm-t5gemma2-plugin](https://github.com/Chen-afk-art/vllm-t5gemma2-plugin) for T5Gemma 2. The PR also fixes the tower LoRA mapping order of encoder-decoder models in Model Runner V2.

## Claims

- **`EncDecMultiModalProcessor.process_text_only_encoder_prompt`** (default `False`): when a processor sets it, the renderer sends encoder prompts without multimodal data through the processor too. Plugins can then accept plain text prompts; bart-plugin, for example, takes the encoder text as `multi_modal_data` instead.
- **`CrossAttention(underlying_attn_backend=...)`** (default: selected as before), like `Attention(attn_backend=...)`. It is for models that read the KV caches of a self-attention and a cross-attention layer directly, so both must use one known layout.
- **Model Runner V2 fix**: the tower LoRA mapping of encoder-decoder models now follows the batch order in which the encoder runs. It followed the scheduler order, so when requests with different decoder prompt lengths started in the same step, one request's encoder tokens could run with another request's adapter.
- **Docs**: list the T5Gemma 2 plugin, and document the processor flag for plugin authors.
- **No change for in-tree models**: the flag and the parameter default to the current behavior, and the Model Runner V2 change only affects encoder-decoder models with tower LoRA, of which none are in-tree.

## Validation

| Check | Setup | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `pre-commit run` | changed files | passed |
| `pytest tests/renderers` | CPU | 339 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `test_cohere.py::test_async_cohere_renderer_does_not_block_event_loop`, also fails on `main` (`a91a1d0`) in the same environment. |
| vllm-t5gemma2-plugin tests on this branch | CPU, tiny random T5Gemma 2 checkpoint, float32 | 5 passed (details below) |
| Same plugin on `main` without this PR | CPU | Engine startup fails with "This vLLM version lacks features that T5Gemma2 needs: `EncDecMultiModalProcessor.process_text_only_encoder_prompt`, `CrossAttention(underlying_attn_backend=...)`" |
| vllm-t5gemma2-plugin tests on this branch | NVIDIA A40 (Model Runner V2, FlashAttention), tiny checkpoint, float16 | 5 passed |
| Same, `google/t5gemma-2-270m-270m` | NVIDIA A40, bfloat16 | 5 passed: 4 in a full run, and the LoRA test in a rerun after lowering the plugin's random LoRA scale to 0.01 (0.03 turned the output into noise, where vLLM and HF diverge at near-ties) |

The 5 plugin tests cover:
- **Generation vs HF transformers**: greedy output matches for text, one image, two images and an explicit decoder prompt, all in one batch.
- **LoRA vs HF + PEFT**: requests with two different adapters and without one share a batch, and the output matches.
- **Text-only mode**: works, and image inputs are rejected.

**Model Runner V2 fix, before and after.** Run the plugin's `tests/test_text_only_lora.py` on the A40 with this branch, then with the commit "Build the tower LoRA mapping of encoder-decoder models in batch order" reverted:

| Checkpoint | With the fix | Without the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Tiny, float16 | passed | `test_lora_matches_peft` fails at token 0: vLLM `[57, 101, 107, …]` vs HF `[55, 55, …]` |
| `google/t5gemma-2-270m-270m`, bfloat16 | passed | `test_lora_matches_peft` fails: the request without an adapter repeats `[236828, 236761, 236770, 236761, …]` |

How the test triggers the bug:
- Its batch starts with a request whose decoder prompt has several tokens, followed by one-token requests. Model Runner V2 runs the one-token requests first, so the batch order differs from the scheduling order.
- The plugin's tests run the engine in-process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`), so all requests are scheduled in the same first step.
- Without the fix, the request with no adapter runs its encoder with another request's LoRA.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Chen-afk-art/vllm-t5gemma2-plugin && cd vllm-t5gemma2-plugin
pip install -e ".[test]"
pytest tests -v
T5GEMMA2_TEST_MODEL=google/t5gemma-2-270m-270m pytest tests -v  # real checkpoint
git -C <vllm checkout> revert --no-commit <commit of the Model Runner V2 fix>
pytest tests/test_text_only_lora.py -v  # fails without the fix
```

**CI**: no in-tree model sets the new flag or passes the new parameter, so vLLM CI covers only their defaults (existing renderer and attention tests). The new paths, and the Model Runner V2 fix, are exercised by the plugin's test suite, run above on CPU and on GPU.

**Model evaluation**: not applicable, since no in-tree model's output changes.

## Details

**Why the processor flag.** vLLM V1 runs the encoder of an encoder-decoder model through the multimodal encoder path, so the encoder only sees what the processor packs into multimodal items. Encoder prompts without multimodal data skipped the processor, which left a text encoder with no input.
- With the flag, `_process_singleton(force_mm_processing=True)` calls `_process_multimodal(prompt_token_ids, {}, ...)` and copies `prompt` and `cache_salt`, as `_process_tokens` does.
- It lives in `_process_singleton` rather than `_process_tokens` because `HfRenderer` overrides `_process_tokens`.
- `_process_enc_dec(_async)` enables it for the encoder prompt only.

**Why the backend parameter.** T5Gemma 2's decoder uses one softmax over its own keys and the encoder keys. The plugin computes two partial attentions with their LSE, one per KV cache, and merges them with `merge_attn_states`. For that, both caches must be in FlashAttention's layout, or both must be read by its own PyTorch path.

**Root cause of the Model Runner V2 fix.**
- `EncoderDecoderModelState.prepare_inputs_embeds` reorders the scheduled encoder inputs by `input_batch.req_ids` before running the encoder.
- `set_active_mm_loras` was called with `scheduler_output.scheduled_encoder_inputs` in scheduler order.
- Model Runner V2 sorts the batch by token count (`sort_batch_req_ids`), so the two orders differ when new requests have different decoder prompt lengths.
- The runner now passes the encoder inputs in batch order to both, for encoder-decoder models only.

**Duplicate check.**
- Open PRs matching "T5Gemma", "CrossAttention" and "encoder-decoder plugin" show nothing that overlaps.
- vllm-project/vllm#32617 (T5Gemma 2 in-tree) was closed after the review asked for a plugin. This PR follows that guidance and keeps the model out of tree.

**AI assistance.** This PR and the plugin were written with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

items.title: [Model] Add Unlimited-OCR-2 DASH attention support
items.body:
## Overview

Add native [Unlimited-OCR-2](https://huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2) support with DASH sparse attention and page-aware RoPE.

## Claims

- FlashAttention and FlashInfer for prefill and decode; Model Runner V2 support.
- Reuse R-SWA to retain input KV and bound output KV to a 128-token window.
- Full decode CUDA Graphs and opt-in segmented prefill graphs.
- Optional page-count guard with GPU incremental state and no token-history host reads.

## Validation

MPDocBench, 420 documents / 3,135 pages, optimized source with V2 (measured before this cleanup; FA/FI math is unchanged):

| Output budget | Overall |
| --- | ---: |
| Published-client fallback | 84.7407 |
| Available context, rerun all four length stops | 84.8430 |
| Paper reference | 84.5900 |

The available-context run has no length stops or page-count mismatches. This uses the public dataset and a local evaluation adapter; it does not reproduce the unpublished per-PDF budgets or identical paper deployment. MarathonDocBench was cancelled.

Page-guard optimization on one GB200, Runner V2, FA/decode Graphs, B=4, 418 output tokens/request: three warm runs improved median end-to-end throughput from 573.3 to 760.2 tokens/s (+32.6%). OCR text matched excluding bounding-box variation also seen between baseline repeats; forced-stop tokens matched exactly. This synthetic workload does not establish long-document speedup.

## Details

Prefill requires complete prompts. Dummy-run state reuses existing forward-context kwargs. Segmented graphs leave dynamic DASH routing, attention and KV writes eager; no prefill speedup is claimed. Chunked prefill, prefix caching, quantization, PP/CP, LoRA, speculative decoding and KV transfer are unsupported.

Validated on GB200/BF16 using prebuilt extensions; clean-build validation remains pending. Strict GPU-sync checking currently fails in the unchanged shared vision encoder before decode.

AI-assisted implementation. No duplicate model-support PR found; #57540 concerns generic n-gram sampling, not this model. Draft pending human review.

items.title: [Model] Support ViT full CUDA graph for Qwen3-Omni
items.body:
## Overview Add ViT full CUDA graph support for the Qwen3-Omni thinker (`Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration`, for example `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct`), part of #38175. Only the vision encoder is captured; the audio encoder stays eager. The thinker has its own `Qwen3Omni_VisionTransformer`, so this follows the Qwen3-VL integration (#35963, video in #38061) rather than reusing the Qwen3-VL code. This is a draft because I have not run it on a GPU. I would like a design review now. The GPU checks it still needs are listed under Limitations, and help from anyone who can run them is welcome. ## Claims - Qwen3-Omni implements `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for images and videos, with the same buffer keys as Qwen3-VL. - The eager vision encoder and the graph path build their attention metadata through one new `prepare_encoder_metadata`, as in Qwen3-VL. - **This also changes the eager encoder for every Qwen3-Omni user, with or without the graph flag.** On FlashInfer and with FP8 encoder attention, the eager path now gets the same `cu_seqlens` and `max_seqlen` as Qwen3-VL. On main, the Omni encoder computed `max_seqlen` only for FA, ROCm AITER FA and Triton, and passed raw `cu_seqlens` to every backend. The RDNA3 fallback for `torch.repeat_interleave` is removed because that call is gone. I have only run the `TORCH_SDPA` backend on CPU, where the output is bit-identical to main. - Not measured: anything on a GPU, including graph replay, encoder latency and TTFT. ## Validation **Tests.** `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py` gets a `qwen3_omni` entry for the image and video E2E tests. It uses `load_format="dummy"` with `dummy_hf_overrides` to shrink the 30B thinker, since the test only checks that capture and replay run. I have not run it, because it needs CUDA. **Eager encoder, main compared with this branch (CPU, `TORCH_SDPA`, fp32).** A tiny random `Qwen3Omni_VisionTransformer` (hidden 64, 4 heads, depth 3, deepstack at layers 0 and 1) with the same weights in main's class and this branch's class gives a max abs diff of 0.0 for single and mixed image and video grids, with `grid_thw` as a tensor or a list. **Capture/replay logic through `EncoderCudaGraphManager` (CPU).** The real manager and this PR's protocol methods ran on the same tiny encoder with budgets `[32, 64, 128]`, 4 items per batch and 8 attention sequences (frames, counted as the grid's `t`) per batch. This is an emulation, not a GPU run: - `torch.cuda.graph` was replaced by a no-op, and each captured graph by a replayer that reruns `encoder_cudagraph_forward` on the captured fixed-size buffers after the manager copies and pads the replay values into them. - The CPU `TORCH_SDPA` wrapper requires the sequences to cover every token, which padded buffers never do. I wrapped it so that tokens past the last `cu_seqlens` offset form one extra sequence whose output is discarded. That is my assumption about varlen kernels, not something tested on FA or FlashInfer. Each output was compared with the eager encoder on that item alone: | Case | Graph hits / eager | max abs diff | |---|---|---| | 3 images in one batch | 3 / 0 | 0.0 | | 2 images + 1 image over the largest budget | 2 / 1 | 0.0 | | 5 images, split across two batches | 5 / 0 | 0.0 | | 2 videos (grid `t` = 2 and 4) | 2 / 0 | 0.0 | The image cases give the same results with video disabled (buffers sized for images). All cases give the same results with the absolute position embedding off. **Lint and types.** `ruff` check and format pass. `mypy` on `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py` adds no errors over main's version of the file in the same environment. ## Details Differences from the Qwen3-VL integration: - **Absolute position embedding is optional.** When `apply_vit_abs_pos_embed` is off, `pos_embeds` is `None` in both the captured inputs and the replay values. The existing manager already skips `None` values when it copies replay values (`_run_budget_graph`), and this PR does not change the manager. The encoder then adds no position embedding. - **Deepstack features come after the main merger** (`merger_list`). The output is `[main, deepstack...]` along the hidden dimension, so `out_hidden_size` is `visual_dim + multiscale_dim`, where `multiscale_dim` is `visual_dim` times the number of deepstack layers. - **`rot_pos_emb` takes a list** of `[t, h, w]` instead of a tensor, so all metadata is built from Python lists, as in Qwen3-VL. - **Eager metadata comes from the shared `MMEncoderAttention` helpers**, as in Qwen3-VL: `cu_seqlens` is built with NumPy, `max_seqlen` comes from `compute_max_seqlen`, and `cu_seqlens` goes through `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, for which the encoder now records `tp_size` and `fp8_padded_hidden_size`. Eager and graph share this path so that the graph replays the same metadata the eager encoder uses, as in Qwen3-VL. If you would rather review the eager change on its own first, I can split it into a separate PR. **Limitations (not run, needs a GPU):** - The E2E test above: `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k qwen3_omni`. - Graph replay compared with eager, with the real weights on FA and FlashInfer. - Eager main compared with this branch on FlashInfer, FP8 encoder attention and ROCm. - Encoder latency and TTFT with and without `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'`. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

items.title: [Docs] Add GLM-5.3-Flash to supported models
items.body:
## Overview

Adds the missing GLM-5.3-Flash entry to the multimodal supported-models table.

Context: #54062 was closed after GLM-5.3-Flash support landed in v0.30.0, but the supported-models table was not updated.

## Claims

- `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` is registered in
  `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` and has been supported since
  v0.30.0, but it was absent from `docs/models/supported_models.md`.
- The new row lists the checkpoint and its image/video modalities, following
  the adjacent GLM-4.1V / GLM-4.5V rows.

## Validation

Docs-only change; no code paths are touched.

```text
pre-commit run --files docs/models/supported_models.md
# typos, markdownlint-cli2 and the remaining applicable hooks passed
```

The model code supports image and video through the inherited Glm4v
multimodal path (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` registers
`Glm5NextMultiModalProcessor` and accepts `{"image", "video"}` in its tower
model). The sibling docs change in #63643 confirms the same model's
image/video support in the encoder CUDA-graph matrix.

## Details

- LoRA is left blank because general GLM-5.3-Flash LoRA support is still in
  #56327; PP is marked supported via the inherited `SupportsPP` implementation.
- The text-only `Glm5NextForCausalLM` entry is not listed separately, matching
  the Qwen3.5 hybrid rows in this table; text-only mode is available through
  the documented `--language-model-only` path.
- No new CI test: this is a documentation row for an already-registered
  architecture.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (opencode/DeepSeek) was used to prepare this docs change. The
human submitter is responsible for the final review.

items.title: [Docs] Add GLM-5.3-Flash to encoder CUDA graph supported models
items.body:
## Purpose

`docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md` maintains the support matrix for multimodal encoder CUDA graphs. 

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) already supports them on main — it inherits the full `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` implementation from `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration` — but is missing from the matrix. 

This PR adds the row (image ✅ / video ✅); no code changes.

Duplicate-work check (per AGENTS.md): no open PR covers GLM-5.3-Flash in this matrix. No new CI test: the capability is inherited, not new code, and the shared parent implementation already carries coverage; same reasoning as the docs-only precedent in #44720.

## Commands

- Server (stock main @ v0.32.0, 8×H200):

  ```bash
  vllm serve /models/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'
  ```

- Image request: OpenAI chat completion with a base64 PNG (448×448 solid blue), `max_tokens: 64`
- Video request: OpenAI chat completion with a base64 MP4 (4 frames solid red), `max_tokens: 200`

## Test Result

- Startup log (all 8 TP ranks): `Encoder CUDA graph capture complete. Captured 8 graphs across 1 paths.`
- Image request: HTTP 200 — `The image appears to be entirely blue - a solid blue color throughout...` (usage: prompt 281, completion 43)
- Video request: HTTP 200 — `...Frame 00:00 is solid red...Red` (usage: prompt 55, completion 68)
- No ERROR / Traceback in the server log during either request.

items.body:
## Overview Add native support for [inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny). vLLM-Omni will be updated to use cls/func from upstream vLLM (after next release) to support models incorporating Ming-3-asr as a component (e.g., `inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash`) ## Claims - Support native `inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny` model - Online serving, offline inference - Transcription of multiple languages and dialects; features such as full-history no-repeat n-gram blocking - Benchmarking and validating ## Validation 1. Unit tests added or modified; related ut cmds: ```bash pytest -s \ tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_ming_v3_asr.py \ tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_bailing_moe_v3_vl.py \ tests/models/test_ming_v3_asr_logits_processor.py \ tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_qwen3_asr_sanitize_prompt.py \ tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing.py -q VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_ming_v3_asr.py -q ``` 2. offline inference example ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ python examples/speech_to_text/ming_v3_asr.py \ --model /path/to/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny \ --audio /path/to/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr/examples/cases/audio/english_common_voice.wav \ --language en ``` out: `same way you did` 3. online serving Launch server: ```bash vllm serve inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny --trust-remote-code # with optional full-history no-repeat n-gram blocking vllm serve inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny \ --trust-remote-code \ --logits-processors \ vllm.model_executor.models.ming_v3_asr_logits_processor:NoRepeatNGramLogitsProcessor ``` Send a request: ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F model=inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny \ -F file=@audio.wav \ -F temperature=0 \ -F max_completion_tokens=256 \ -F 'vllm_xargs={"no_repeat_ngram_size":10}' ``` ### Benchmark summary: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false \ vllm serve inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8190 \ --revision ac95e7b1678c08ea6f4a2581a051e432ed63e9b7 \ --trust-remote-code \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-num-seqs 64 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --mm-encoder-attn-backend TORCH_SDPA \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \ --disable-log-requests \ --logits-processors \ vllm.model_executor.models.ming_v3_asr_logits_processor:NoRepeatNGramLogitsProcessor ``` Seed-TTS | Execution | English req/s | Chinese req/s | English WER | Chinese CER | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Eager | 27.85 | 34.71 | 1.0896% | 0.5574% | | Compile + CUDA Graph | 53.46 | 56.51 | 1.1199% | 0.5364% | *single H200, BF16, TORCH_SDPA encoder, concurrency 32, max_num_seqs=64, greedy decoding, no-repeat disabled, prefix/MM processor caches disabled. Each condition used a full warmup followed by one timed pass over SeedTTS prompt audio (1,088 English and 2,020 Chinese clips) *For this one, used Seed-TTS ref recordings (`prompt-wavs/`) and prompt transcripts, with Whisper English normalization. Different from `wavs/` used in the next table. Accuracy (for other benchmarks) | Dataset / Metric | #Items | vLLM | Model Vendor | Err / Refs | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Seed-TTS target EN WER | 1,088 | 2.659890% | - | 314 / 11,805 | | Seed-TTS target ZH CER | 2,020 | 0.889604% | - | 376 / 42,266 | | AISHELL-1 CER | 7,176 | 1.049969% | 1.07% | 1,100 / 104,765 | | LibriSpeech clean WER | 2,620 | 1.197503% | 1.29% | 635 / 53,027 | | LibriSpeech other WER | 2,939 | 2.397791% | 2.56% | 1,268 / 52,882 | *For Seed-TTS, used Seed-TTS target recordings (`wavs/`) and target transcripts, scored with the vendor’s general normalization rules to track accuracy across implementation changes. *Accuracy Reference from official model vendor: https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr/blob/6141e8c552815db724d8df0f72c9d865c547a1ea/figures/open-asr.png ## Details ASR model should be supported in vLLM rather than vLLM-Omni, while vLLM-Omni could use an ASR model from upstream vLLM as a component in another model (I'll update in vLLM-Omni after next releasing). items.title: [Model][LoRA] LoRA support for MiniMax M3
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

LoRA support for MiniMax M3 (`MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM` and `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration`). Adapters on attention (q/k/v/o and the indexer's index_q/index_k), the dense MLP, shared experts and routed experts are served without changing the base kernels. Follows the pattern of the Step5 LoRA support (#62498): model-specific LoRA layers live in `vllm/lora/layers/custom_layer.py`.

## Claims

- Both entry points implement `SupportsLoRA`; the VL wrapper targets its `language_model` (`get_mm_mapping`). LoRA is marked supported in `docs/models/supported_models.md`.
- Sparse attention layers fuse q, k, v, index_q and index_k into one `MinimaxM3QKVParallelLinearWithIndexer`, so for LoRA `qkv_proj` packs five modules. This five-entry mapping is set on the model instance, which is what the LoRA manager reads; the class-level `packed_modules_mapping`, which quantization configs use for exclusion lists, keeps q/k/v as on main, so a quantized checkpoint that excludes q/k/v of a dense attention layer (no indexer) still loads. `MiniMaxM3QKVIndexerWithLoRA` gives it five LoRA slices that shard like the base weight: q, k, v as in `MergedQKVParallelLinearWithLoRA`, index_q like k/v (one indexer head per KV head, including KV-head replication), index_k replicated on every rank.
- Dense attention layers (layers 0-2 in the default config) keep a plain 3-way `QKVParallelLinear` under the same five-entry LoRA packing; `MiniMaxM3DenseQKVWithLoRA` applies q/k/v there and drops the two always-empty indexer entries.
- Weight reload under LoRA: wrapped parameters live under `base_layer`, while a checkpoint-format reload (`reload_weights` calls `load_weights`) sends unwrapped names. On main these weights are skipped silently, including routed experts (`fused_moe_make_expert_params_mapping` adds `base_layer.` to the checkpoint side too, so no checkpoint name matches). `load_weights` now resolves wrapped parameters by their unwrapped names.
- `fully_sharded_loras` is rejected at startup; without the check the fused qkv projection would silently stay unwrapped.
- Routed-expert LoRA uses the existing MoE LoRA path (e.g. BF16/FP8 experts, Marlin). NVFP4 experts on the FlashInfer TRTLLM backend additionally need #63024.

## Validation

Environment: NVIDIA GB300, `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly arm64 image built from `8e2beaa3b`. `vllm/lora/` and `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py` were copied from this PR's base (old) or head (new) over the image; tests ran from this PR's `tests/`.

New tests:

Old is this PR's base (main) for the first commit's tests; the quantization test compares against this PR's first commit.

| test | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_lora.py::test_lora_packs_indexer_and_quant_checks_real_projections` (text/vl x LoRA off/on) | 4 failed on the first commit: `Detected some but not all shards of model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj are quantized` | 4 passed |
| `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_lora.py::test_load_weights_resolves_lora_wrapped_params[lora-wrapped]` | failed on main (q/index_k and expert weights not loaded) | passed |
| `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_lora.py::test_load_weights_resolves_lora_wrapped_params[plain]` | passed | passed |
| `tests/lora/test_layers.py -k minimax_m3` (5 tests) | collection error on main (classes missing) | 5 passed |

- `test_lora_packs_indexer_and_quant_checks_real_projections`: builds both entry points (inner modules stubbed) with LoRA off and on. The mapping the LoRA manager reads packs five modules into `qkv_proj`. A MiniMax-style MXFP8 config (`ignored_layers`) that excludes q/k/v of dense layer 0 and all five projections of sparse layer 3 marks both fused `qkv_proj` layers as excluded and layer 1 as quantized.
- `test_minimax_m3_qkv_lora[sparse|dense]`: `from_layer` with the five-entry packing picks the new class for each layer type, and the LoRA output matches the base output plus per-slice `x @ A.T @ B.T`.
- `test_minimax_m3_qkv_indexer_lora_b_shards_like_weight`: for TP 2/4/8 with 4/2/2 KV heads (sharded and replicated), the per-rank slices of a full-size lora_B equal the rows the base weight loader puts on that rank.

Regression, `pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_utils.py`: main 131 passed, 72 skipped; this PR 136 passed, 74 skipped.

CI: the LoRA job (`.buildkite/test_areas/lora.yaml`) now also runs `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_lora.py` and triggers on `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py`.

After the second commit, the end-to-end check below was rerun with #59941 applied: both architectures still wrap layer 0 with `MiniMaxM3DenseQKVWithLoRA` and layers 1-3 with `MiniMaxM3QKVIndexerWithLoRA`, and outputs with and without the adapter are unchanged from the first commit.

End-to-end, single GB300, CUDA graphs on: a 4-layer MiniMax M3 config (layer 0 dense attention + dense MLP, layers 1-3 sparse attention + MoE with 16 experts, BF16), dummy weights re-initialized to N(0, 0.02), rank-8 adapters on q/k/v/o/index_q/index_k and the dense/shared-expert MLPs, `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration`:

- layer 0 `qkv_proj` is `MiniMaxM3DenseQKVWithLoRA`, layers 1-3 are `MiniMaxM3QKVIndexerWithLoRA`;
- an adapter with B = 0 gives greedy output identical to no adapter (2 prompts x 24 tokens);
- a random adapter changes the first generated token for both prompts; prompt logprobs move by up to 3.56;
- in a batch of [no adapter, random adapter], prompt logprobs of each row equal the single-adapter runs exactly (max abs diff 0.0), so the delta does not leak into the no-LoRA row.

Not verified:

- Real checkpoints, TP > 1, and routed-expert adapters were not served end to end; routed-expert LoRA goes through the unchanged `FusedMoEWithLoRA` path.

NaN seen during validation, root-caused (not from this PR): the image above predates #59941. There, `eager_break_during_capture` is resolved at import time, but `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` is auto-enabled later during config setup, so whether MiniMax M3's sparse attention gets its eager break depends on import order. In that image the same tiny model (dummy weights, no LoRA, default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` with breakable CUDA graphs) gives different greedy output for two identical requests with either architecture. In some runs every logit is NaN, e.g. `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration` with LoRA disabled. Which architecture and which LoRA setting hits NaN changed between runs. `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and `enforce_eager=True` were deterministic. With the one-file fix from #59941 (already on main) applied to the image:

- both architectures, with LoRA disabled and enabled (plus `PIECEWISE` for the text architecture with LoRA), give finite logprobs and the same greedy tokens across repeated requests;
- with the same MoE backend (`moe_backend="triton"`, which LoRA selects), prompt logprobs of LoRA-disabled, LoRA-enabled (no adapter), text and VL architectures are bitwise equal (max abs diff 0.0);
- an adapter changes the output, and the output with the adapter is identical across repeats and between the two architectures.

## Details

- Quantization configs receive the class-level `packed_modules_mapping` by reference before the model is built, while the LoRA manager reads the mapping from the model instance. Keeping the five-entry packing on the instance only leaves quantization exclusion checks exactly as on main: every attention `qkv_proj` is checked against q/k/v, which are the only projections of a dense layer; a sparse layer's index_q/index_k are not part of the check, as on main.

## Overview

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 is the MiniCPM-V 4.6 stack with a different `model_type`, so
this adds `MiniCPMOcrForConditionalGeneration` as a subclass of
`MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration` and registers it in the model registry and
the chat-template fallback.

image processor returns instead of being recomputed from the image size, because
the small-image upsize tier is decided from the pixels. This also covers

Requires a transformers build that ships `minicpm_ocr` (`MiniCPMOcrConfig`,
`MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor`, `MiniCPMOcrProcessor`).

`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` is needed for plain

items.title: [Model] dots.ocr: support encoder CUDA graph

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests

items.body:
## Overview

Add encoder CUDA graph support (`SupportsEncoderCudaGraph`) for dots.ocr, so its ViT can be captured and replayed by the existing `EncoderCudaGraphManager`. Part of #38175.

## Claims

- dots.ocr implements `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph`; with `compilation_config={"cudagraph_mm_encoder": True}` its vision encoder runs through captured graphs.
- Graph outputs are **bit-identical** to eager on the same padded inputs; end-to-end OCR text is identical to eager.
- Images up to 512 tokens get faster when kernel launch is the bottleneck: single-request latency for a 224×224 image is **3.0× (A100) / 4.4× (RTX 4090)** faster; on an RTX 3090 with a fast CPU the gain is small (1.07×).
- The default budget range is capped at 512 tokens. Larger images fall back to eager, so typical document pages are not slower than eager.

## Validation

**Correctness** (RTX 3090 and RTX 4090; bf16):
- Graph vs eager on the *same padded input* (same budget, same zero padding, same `cu_seqlens` padding), 5 batching cases (single page, two pages in one batch, a tiny image that the manager puts in its own batch, an oversize image that falls back to eager, mixed graph/eager): **bit-identical** in all cases.
- Comparing against *unpadded* eager differs by up to ~5% relative. This is not specific to graphs: running the same page in eager with a different batch composition changes its output by ~6% as well, because the bf16 GEMMs pick different kernels for different row counts.
- End-to-end greedy OCR on 3 rendered pages (256 tokens each): identical text to eager on RTX 3090, RTX 4090 and A100.
- Test: added `dots_ocr` to `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py` (image modality, single 4096 budget so both test images — 1426 and 2646 tokens — replay through the encoder graph rather than falling back to eager). Passes locally on RTX 3090: `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k "dots_ocr and image"`.

**Performance**, default config after this PR (budgets 64–512, `max_batch_size` = 8). Encoder only, p50 of 50 runs, graph and eager interleaved:

| Single image | RTX 3090 + i5-12400 (4.4 GHz) | RTX 4090 + Xeon 6133 (2.5 GHz) | A100 + Xeon 8380 (2.3 GHz) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 tokens | 1.41× | 6.22× | 4.47× |
| 128 tokens | 0.99× | 4.14× | 2.86× |
| 256 tokens | 1.02× | 2.47× | 1.83× |
| 384 tokens (padded to 512) | **0.71×** | 1.35× | 1.09× |
| 512 tokens | 1.01× | 1.29× | 1.05× |
| ≥ 513 tokens / 1000×800 page | 1.00× (eager) | 1.00× (eager) | 1.00× (eager) |

End-to-end (`LLM.generate`, `max_tokens=1` latency ≈ TTFT, p50 of 20 requests, each with a new image; throughput = 32 pages / 64 small images with `max_tokens=128`):

| | RTX 3090 | RTX 4090 | A100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 224×224 latency | 37 → 34 ms | 92 → 21 ms | 55 → 18 ms |
| 448×448 latency | 99 → 98 ms | 106 → 45 ms | 62 → 37 ms |
| 1000×800 latency | 381 → 380 ms | 179 → 179 ms | 137 → 136 ms |
| 32 pages throughput | 0.96× | 1.02× | 0.96× |
| 64 small images throughput | 0.89× | 1.07× | 0.98× |
| KV cache memory | −0.23 GiB | −0.23 GiB | −0.23 GiB |

Why cap at 512: with the manager's default range (up to `max_num_batched_tokens`, 4096 here), a 1000×800 page (1044 tokens) is padded to the 2048 budget and runs at **0.56–0.61×** of eager on all three GPUs; 513–1023-token images run at 0.67–0.84×. In no tested GPU did a budget above 512 beat eager. The cap also reduces graph memory from 1.43 GiB to 0.23 GiB and removes ~12–19 s of startup capture time.

How measured: encoder numbers call `EncoderCudaGraphManager.execute` (graph) and `vision_tower(pixel_values, grid_thw)` (eager) on the same inputs in one process, interleaved, CUDA events with synchronize, 10 warmup + 50 timed runs. Budget caps other than the default were simulated by overriding `get_encoder_cudagraph_budget_range`. Happy to share the scripts.

## Details

- `DotsVisionTransformer.forward` is split into `prepare_encoder_metadata()` (outside the graph: rotary embeddings, `cu_seqlens` computed on CPU and padded to `max_batch_size + 1` with the last offset, `max_seqlen` kept on CPU) and in-graph compute, shared by the graph and eager paths. `max_seqlen` is captured as `budget × 4` (spatial merge 2×2) because the attention call bakes it into the graph via `.item()`.
- dots.ocr is image-only and each image is one attention sequence, so `cu_seqlens` is padded to `max_batch_size` only (no frames axis).
- `min_budget = 64` (same as Qwen2-VL/Qwen3-VL): the smallest dots.ocr image is 4 tokens, but a smaller minimum would shrink the inferred `max_batch_size` (`min(max // min, min)`).

**Limitations**
- The benefit depends on the GPU/CPU speed ratio: when the CPU is fast relative to the GPU (e.g. RTX 3090 + 4.4 GHz desktop CPU), eager is GPU-bound and the graph gains little; padding to the next power-of-two budget can then make 257–511-token images slower (0.71× at 384 tokens on RTX 3090).
- Batched throughput is roughly neutral (0.89–1.07×): in batched mode eager runs many images in one large call, while the graph path splits them into budget-sized batches.
- Run-to-run variation: on the dual-socket 4090 host, eager latency varied by ~15% between processes (launch-bound, sensitive to CPU placement); graph latency was stable. Numbers above are from a single process per configuration.
- Not measured: online serving under concurrency; H100.

**AI assistance:** The model code was written by the author; an AI assistant (Claude) reviewed it, wrote the local acceptance/benchmark scripts, ran some of the measurements, and helped draft this description. The author reviewed all changed lines and validated the results.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Judge draft KV groups with the draft model's config for CUDA-graph support
items.body:
## Overview

This PR builds on #55593 by @he-yufeng and completes it, so a speculative drafter whose attention heads differ from the target's keeps full CUDA graphs on both model runners. His two commits come first with his authorship and messages. On top of them, one commit applies his rule to Model Runner V2 and one tags the draft KV cache group early enough for his V1 check to take effect on current `main`. Fixes #55581.

## Claims

- Model Runner V2 keeps `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` with a drafter of its own head count, where `main` drops to `PIECEWISE` for every layer, the target's included.
- The V1 runner keeps `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` with an EAGLE-style drafter of its own head count.
- Only KV groups holding draft layers take the draft model's config, so runs without a drafter resolve the same graph mode as before.

## Validation

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed below.

I ran the engine on one B300 with FlashInfer attention, TP1, the Qwen3.8-27B target (24 query and 4 KV heads per rank) with dummy weights, and a dummy-weight drafter with 40 query and 40 KV heads, head size 128 and 2 speculative tokens. Model Runner V2 used a 2-layer Qwen3 `draft_model` drafter and V1 a 1-layer EAGLE3 drafter. Every run generated 32 tokens for each of 4 prompts.

| Runner | Tree | Resolved `cudagraph_mode` | FULL graphs captured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model Runner V2 | `main` | `PIECEWISE` | none |
| Model Runner V2 | this PR | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 8 batch shapes |
| V1 | `main` | `PIECEWISE` | none |
| V1 | #55593's commits on `main` (with the Model Runner V2 commit) | `PIECEWISE` | none |
| V1 | this PR | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 6 decode batch shapes |

On `main` both runners log `CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE is not supported with spec-decode for attention backend FlashInferBackend (support: AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE); setting cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`.

Each new test fails on the tree without its fix and passes with it. His V1 test fails on `main`, the Model Runner V2 test (`test_draft_layers_cudagraph_support_uses_draft_model_config`) fails on his commits alone, and the grouping test (`test_groups_from_builder_tag_eagle_groups`) fails without the last commit. On CPU, `test_attn_utils.py`, `test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`, `test_gpu_model_runner.py`, `test_kv_cache_utils.py`, `test_kv_cache_planning.py` and `test_kv_cache_config_builder.py` give the same results on `main` and this PR apart from the three new tests. Seven tests in `test_gpu_model_runner.py` fail on both trees because they need a GPU. `pre-commit run --from-ref main --to-ref HEAD` passes, mypy included.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```python
# drafter: a config with num_attention_heads=40, num_key_value_heads=40,
# head_dim=128 and the target's vocab (dummy weights are enough), e.g. a
# 2-layer Qwen3ForCausalLM for draft_model or LlamaForCausalLMEagle3 for eagle3.
# VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 selects Model Runner V2, 0 selects V1.
from vllm import LLM

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B",
    load_format="dummy",
    speculative_config={"method": "draft_model", "model": "<drafter dir>",
                        "num_speculative_tokens": 2},
    attention_backend="FLASHINFER",
    max_model_len=4096,
    language_model_only=True,
)
print(llm.llm_engine.vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode)
```

</details>

## Details

FlashInfer reports full CUDA-graph support for a KV cache spec when trtllm-gen decode can serve it, and it takes the query-head count for that check from `model_config`, which is the target's. A draft layer with 40 KV heads under a target with 24 query heads per rank fails `24 % 40 == 0`, the check reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`, and with speculative decoding the runner drops to `PIECEWISE` for all layers. #55593 fixes this on V1 by judging draft-side KV groups (`is_eagle_group`) with `speculative_config.draft_model_config`.

Model Runner V2 asks each attention group's builder with the runner's `vllm_config` in `get_attn_cg_support` and in the varlen check used by adaptive verification, so it needs the same rule. It already tags draft layers (`is_draft_layer`, set by its EAGLE-style and `draft_model` speculators). `init_attn_backend` copies that tag onto the group's KV cache spec, because merged group specs drop it, and both checks pick the draft config from it. The tag is a `compare=False` field, so KV cache grouping and layouts stay the same.

On current `main` the V1 runner resolves its graph mode twice, first for the minimal KV cache config of the CUDA-graph memory profiling pass and then for the real one. Only `get_kv_cache_configs` set `is_eagle_group`, so the profiling pass saw an untagged draft group, judged it with the target's config and dropped the mode to `PIECEWISE`, which the second pass keeps. The last commit moves the tagging into `get_kv_cache_groups_from_builder`, which both configs are built from. The warning about an untagged EAGLE group with Mamba layers stays in `get_kv_cache_configs`, so it is logged once.

V1 tags draft groups only for methods that use EAGLE block dropping, so a V1 `draft_model` drafter is judged with the target's config as before. On `main` that setup also stops at the first prefill with `assert is_strictly_contiguous(block_tables_prefill)` in FlashInfer, a separate issue this PR does not touch. Model Runner V2 covers `draft_model`. I measured on B300 only (SM103, trtllm-gen decode).

### Not a duplicate

I searched open and closed PRs for `get_cudagraph_support` with FlashInfer, drafters with a different head count, `can_use_trtllm_attention`, and `55581 in:body`. #55593 is the open fix for #55581 on V1, and this PR keeps it whole and adds the Model Runner V2 side and the profiling-pass tagging it needs on current `main`. Maintainers can take this PR in place of #55593 or merge #55593 first, after which this PR reduces to the last two commits. #56289 by @XFDG (closed) read the head count from the group's own layers inside FlashInfer. This PR uses none of its code.

## Credits

@he-yufeng wrote the V1 runner fix and its test in #55593, and this PR carries his two commits unchanged. Thank you. @XFDG's #56289 was an earlier approach to the same bug.

## Overview

## Claims



## Validation

Test inference using the official H-Spec checkpoint released in the paper for Qwen3-8B ([weifanjiang/qwen3-8b.speculators.hspec](https://huggingface.co/weifanjiang/qwen3-8b.speculators.hspec)):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
    --speculative-config '{"model": PATH_TO_HSPEC-CHECKPOINT, "method": "mamba_attn_hybrid", "num_speculative_tokens": 7}'
```

| task | Paper MAL | reproduced MAL | diff |
|---|---|---|---|

items.title: [Model][Quantization] Add BitNet b1.58 support
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds native support for BitNet b1.58 ternary checkpoints (`quant_method: "bitnet"`): a `bitnet` quantization method plus the `BitNetForCausalLM` architecture ([BitNet b1.58 2B4T](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.12285)). Addresses #17279, #18213 and the BitNet part of #33142.

## Claims

- `vllm serve microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T` works out of the box (no `--quantization` flag), with torch.compile + CUDA graphs.
- `quant_method: "bitnet"` checkpoints on existing architectures also load, e.g. `tiiuae/Falcon3-*-1.58bit` and `HF1BitLLM/Llama3-8B-1.58-100B-tokens` (`LlamaForCausalLM`).
- No new kernels: ternary weights are unpacked to int8 at load and run through the existing int8 W8A8 scaled-mm kernels (CUTLASS on CUDA; Triton/CPU via the existing kernel selection) with dynamic per-token int8 activations — the same math BitNet uses.
- Weight memory is ~2x smaller than bf16 (2B4T: 2.57 GiB).

## Validation

All on 1x A100-SXM4-40GB, torch 2.14 / CUDA 13.0.

**HF parity** — `pytest tests/models/quantization/test_bitnet.py -v` → 3 passed. Greedy logprobs (16 tokens, top-5) match the Transformers reference for both scale conventions:

| Checkpoint | Arch / linear class | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T` | `BitNetForCausalLM` / `AutoBitLinear` | pass |
| `tiiuae/Falcon3-1B-Instruct-1.58bit` | `LlamaForCausalLM` / `BitLinear` | pass |

Plus a CPU unit test that `unpack_ternary_weight` inverts `transformers.integrations.bitnet.pack_weights`.

**GSM8K** (`vllm serve <model>` then `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000`, 5-shot, 1319 questions):

| Model | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| `microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T` | 0.648 | 0.001 |
| `tiiuae/Falcon3-1B-Instruct-1.58bit` | 0.269 | 0.001 |

**Throughput** — `vllm bench throughput --model microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T --input-len 512 --output-len 256 --num-prompts 500`: 32.92 req/s, 37,922 total tok/s, 4,214 output tok/s.

**Serving smoke test** — chat completions return coherent answers (e.g. "What is 17 * 23?" → `391`).

**`HF1BitLLM/Llama3-8B-1.58-100B-tokens`** — serves (8.46 GiB weights); layer-5 qkv / gate_up / down outputs match HF at cosine ≥ 0.99999 and first-token top-5 candidates agree, but greedy continuations drift after a few tokens: the model's next-token distribution is very flat (top-1 ≈ 13%) and HF's `BitLinear` does the int8 × ternary matmul in bf16, so it is not added as a parity test.

**No host syncs** — `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` generation on bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T completes cleanly.

**Regression** — `tests/models/test_registry.py` + `tests/quantization/test_register_quantization_config.py`: 427 passed, 1 failed (`test_custom_quant[meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct]`: gated-repo 401 on the test box, fails identically on the base commit). `tests/models/test_initialization.py -k BitNet`: passed. `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD --hook-stage manual` passes.

New tests run in the existing "Quantized Models" Buildkite step (`pytest -v -s models/quantization`).

## Details

- **Packing:** HF packs 4 ternary values per uint8 along the *output* dim in blocks (`packed[r]` holds rows `r, r+N/4, r+N/2, r+3N/4`), so packed rows can't be TP-sliced directly. The weight loader unpacks the full tensor first, then hands it to the normal (merged/QKV/row-parallel) loader.
- **Scales:** `BitLinear` stores `1/mean|W|` (output divided), `AutoBitLinear` stores `mean|W|` (output multiplied); the per-tensor scale is inverted at load for `BitLinear`, and fused QKV / gate-up scales become per-channel via the existing kernel path.
- **Model:** Llama + ReLU² gated MLP + SubLN (`attn_sub_norm` before `o_proj`, `ffn_sub_norm` before `down_proj`). Reuses `LlamaAttention` / `LlamaForCausalLM`; the decoder layer is re-declared because `LlamaDecoderLayer` hard-codes the SiLU `LlamaMLP`. Sub-norms use the existing `TPAwareRMSNorm` (all-gather under TP>1).
- The MLP computes `relu(gate)**2 * up` natively (fused by torch.compile) rather than via `ReLUSquaredActivation`: its CUDA op silently returns wrong results on non-contiguous input such as `gate_up.chunk(2)[0]` (found while validating; existing callers pass contiguous tensors, so it is not fixed here).
- **Limitations:** only pre-quantized (`quantization_mode: "offline"`) checkpoints; online mode (bf16 master weights) raises a clear error. TP>1 and ROCm were not validated (single A100 available); `bitnet` is not added to ROCm's `supported_quantization`. The bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T `config.json` has a stale `auto_map` to non-existent remote code — load it without `--trust-remote-code` (Transformers supports `bitnet` natively).
- Weights are stored as int8 (2 bits/value would need a dedicated kernel, e.g. a follow-up via humming's `BitnetWeightSchema`, already usable with `--quantization humming`).
- **Not a duplicate:** #52195 is a CPU-only reference backend that ternarizes non-BitNet models online; #40088 is a stale draft (merge conflicts since June, includes scratch files, review notes its quantization path is broken). This PR serves the actual released BitNet checkpoints on GPU via existing kernels.

items.title: [Model] Support Decision 3.0 prefix_bidir attention (vllm-sr/d3-turbo)
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Serve [`vllm-sr/d3-turbo`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-turbo) (27B) with `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-turbo` and no other flags, and ask it typed questions on `/v1/systemone`. Today it stops at start-up with `ValueError: unsupported decision_config.json attention_mode 'prefix_bidir'`: its checkpoint declares an attention mode that `D3ForSequenceClassification` does not take yet. Follow-up to #61565 and #61778, which added Decision 3.0 and its other sizes.

## Claims

- **`prefix_bidir` gets the checkpoint's own mask.** A prompt is a state block (the system turn, the media, `State:` and the state) followed by a question block. Each request's two blocks become the PrefixLM ranges of the full attention layers, the mask vLLM already applies to multimodal prefix-LM models (causal, or both ways within a range): the state reads itself both ways, the question reads the state and itself both ways, and the state never sees a question. The linear-attention layers stay causal.
- **`/v1/systemone` gives the checkpoint runtime's answers** on one AMD Instinct MI325X: 1 of 260 decisions changed (a near-tie: the reference's two best answers are 0.0056 apart), median |dp| 0.0007, max 0.026, over text, JSON, one image, several images, a video and a 24K-token state. At long context (64K to 117K-token states, `--max-model-len 131072`) 0 of 6 changed, max |dp| 0.014.
- **No flags needed.** The checkpoint declares the length it was validated at (`validated_length`, 32,768 tokens per question), and it becomes the default `max-model-len` when none is given; `--max-model-len 131072` serves long contexts. The other Decision 3.0 checkpoints declare none and are unaffected.
- **`D3Strategy` sends each prompt's state block size**, counted with the runtime's own rule: the lead tokens that end by the end of the state text, so a token joining the state's last character to the question block belongs to the question.
- The other Decision 3.0 models are unchanged (their GPU tests pass). The docs list d3-turbo and its long-context limit, the test registry lists it, and a new GPU test runs `prefix_bidir` in CI on a small checkpoint against d3-turbo's own runtime.

## Validation

**Setup**: one AMD Instinct MI325X per side. vLLM is the ROCm nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-e68efc685ab1e6f1eda004ced7157e3ca411da2f` (PyTorch 2.13, ROCm 7.2) with this branch's Python tree (main `59a51259c` plus this PR; rebased onto `1a74cc7bb` before opening, with no changes to these files) copied over the installed one; no kernels were built. It ran `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-turbo` (32,768 tokens per question, the new default; `--max-model-len 131072` for long context) with no other flags: Model Runner V2 and the Triton attention backend, which vLLM selects for the PrefixLM ranges. The reference is the checkpoint's own runtime, `AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)`, with the versions its `requirements.txt` pins (transformers 5.17.0, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2) in the same image, on its default path: the state block once per request, then the questions on it, through its fused ROCm kernels. Checkpoint `vllm-sr/d3-turbo` @ `689b3af1` (tag v1.1).

**Answers vs the reference** (`model.system_one(...)` in process): a seeded set of 32 requests and 260 questions. Text: six states with 1, 4 and 16 questions each, a 16-question JSON state, a 64-question request, a 40-option and a 255-option choice, and an empty state. Media: three photos with 8 questions each, a one-question photo request, requests with 3 and with 2 images, an 11 s video with 6 questions, and a video with an image. Then a 24K-token state with 4 questions, and for long context 64K, 96K and 117K-token states with 2 questions each (reference: `long_context=True`). The decision is the top choice, `noul >= 0.5`, or a score's most likely level; |dp| is the largest absolute probability difference over a question's options.

| Set | Questions | Decisions changed | Median abs dp | p90 | Max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| text and JSON | 212 | 1 (reference margin 0.0056) | 0.0007 | 0.0072 | 0.019 |
| one image | 25 | 0 | 0.0001 | 0.0057 | 0.025 |
| several images | 10 | 0 | 0.0001 | 0.013 | 0.013 |
| video | 9 | 0 | 0.0010 | 0.026 | 0.026 |
| 24K-token state | 4 | 0 | 0.0023 | 0.0027 | 0.0027 |
| 64K, 96K, 117K-token states | 6 | 0 | 0.0024 | 0.014 | 0.014 |

**Latency**, one request at a time, p50 over 3 runs after a warm-up (1 run for the 64K to 117K states), ms. The runtime runs in process; vLLM is measured over HTTP.

| Request | Runtime | vLLM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 text question | 60 to 61 | 30 to 35 |
| 4 text questions | 77 to 107 | 58 to 85 |
| 16 text questions | 176 to 242 | 225 to 271 |
| 16 questions, JSON state | 218 | 376 |
| 64 text questions | 756 | 810 |
| 255-option choice | 398 | 370 |
| 1 photo, 1 question | 303 | 191 |
| 1 photo, 8 questions | 254 to 360 | 909 to 1,310 |
| 3 photos, 6 questions | 682 | 2,489 |
| 11 s video, 6 questions | 447 | 1,456 |
| 24K-token state, 4 questions | 3,579 | 24,862 |
| 64K-token state, 2 questions | 10,574 | 55,449 |
| 117K-token state, 2 questions | 26,275 | 168,277 |

**Start-up**: `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-turbo` with no flags and an empty Hugging Face cache answered its first request 270 s after launch, the 52 GB download included.

**Throughput**, closed loop over the same requests (the 23 text requests, or the 8 image and video requests), 30 to 60 s per level: vLLM serves the text mix at 5.95 req/s with 1 client, 7.56 with 8 and 7.89 with 64 (55.5, 69.6 and 73.2 questions/s), and the media mix at 0.87 and 0.95 req/s with 1 and 8 clients (5.0 and 5.3 questions/s). The runtime's mean latency on the same requests corresponds to 6.15 req/s (56.7 questions/s) on text and 2.45 req/s (13.5 questions/s) on media, one request at a time.

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py` (MI325X): 3 passed in 234 s: d3-edge and d3-nano as before, and the new `test_d3_prefix_bidir_matches_the_checkpoint_runtime`. Without the state block sizes in the pooling params the new test fails (0.035 > 0.02).
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py`: 62 passed, including the new state block test.
- `pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k decision_config`: 8 passed; `pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k D3`: 1 passed.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, typos, markdownlint and the repository checks).
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on the server: 62 requests (text, one and several images, video) with no synchronization error.

## Details

- **The mask**: the Triton, FlexAttention and FlashAttention 4 backends already OR per-request bidirectional ranges into the causal mask for multimodal prefix-LM models. Two ranges per request, `[0, s)` for the state block and `[s, n)` for the question block, give exactly the runtime's `prefix_bidir` mask, so no kernel changes are needed.
- **Where the ranges come from**: `D3Strategy` counts each prompt's state block (images and videos included, since they come first) and sends it as `PoolingParams.extra_kwargs["d3_state_tokens"]`. `D3PrefixBidirModelState`, the model's Model Runner V2 state, turns it into the request's two ranges. The only change outside the model is a `DefaultModelState.get_mm_prefix_ranges` hook that `prepare_attn` calls; its default is the previous inline code.
- **Detection and config**: the arch config convertor already detects Decision 3.0 checkpoints by their `decision_config.json`; for `prefix_bidir` it also sets `is_mm_prefix_lm`, so attention backends that take the ranges are selected. The config hook keeps the text layers causal (decoder attention that reads the ranges) and marks the model non-causal, so chunked prefill and prefix caching stay off as for the other Decision 3.0 models. A declared `validated_length` sets `max_model_len` only when the user gives none.
- **Tradeoffs and limits**
  - State per question: the runtime reads a request's state once and answers every question from it. vLLM reads it again for each question, one engine request per question as for the other Decision 3.0 models, so many questions about a large state (several images, long text) cost more than in the runtime (latency table). The media themselves are processed once per request and the vision encoder output is cached.
  - Long prompts: at 64K tokens one question takes about 28 s in vLLM and the runtime's state pass about 10 s; most of the gap is the attention kernel with ranges, which is slower than the runtime's SDPA at that length on this GPU.
  - Model Runner V2 on CUDA or ROCm GPUs only: Model Runner V1 does not give the ranges to the attention, so loading a `prefix_bidir` checkpoint there raises a clear error. FlexAttention does not take this model's hybrid KV cache layout (784-token blocks), so on ROCm the Triton backend serves it.
  - `/classify` and `/pooling` cannot carry the state block size, so a `prefix_bidir` prompt sent there reads as a single block; `LLM.classify` takes it through `PoolingParams`, as the new test does.
  - Not in this PR: Box and Track questions and images inside questions or options, which `/v1/systemone` does not offer; NVIDIA measurements beyond CI (no NVIDIA GPU was available to me); tensor parallelism; LoRA.
- **CI**: the new test runs in the optional "Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling)" step on d3-edge's weights (already downloaded there) plus six small runtime files from d3-turbo at a pinned revision. d3-turbo's own 52 GB checkpoint is covered by the measurements above, not CI.
- **Not a duplicate**: no open or closed PR or issue covers d3-turbo or `prefix_bidir` (searched for d3-turbo, `prefix_bidir`, Decision 3.0, `D3ForSequenceClassification`). #61251 changes how `/v1/systemone` tokenizes a shared state and also edits `D3Strategy.read()`; whichever lands second rebases, and the state block size here is computed on the same prompt either way.
- **AI assistance** was used for the code, tests, measurements and this description. The PR stays a draft until the submitter has reviewed every line.

## Follow-ups

- **State once**: answer all of a request's questions from one pass over its state, either as one engine request per state or with prefix caching restricted to KV blocks that lie entirely inside the state block (the question block reads itself both ways, so blocks that cross into it cannot be shared).
- **A faster attention path for long `prefix_bidir` prompts on ROCm.**
- **Box and Track questions** and images inside questions and options on `/v1/systemone`.

items.body:
## Overview

Add support for Domyn Edge (`DomynEdgeForCausalLM`), a ~4B dense decoder released by Domyn: [`domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base`](https://huggingface.co/domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base) and [`domyn/Domyn-Edge-SFT`](https://huggingface.co/domyn/Domyn-Edge-SFT).

## Changes

- New architecture `DomynEdgeForCausalLM` with interleaved RoPE/NoPE attention layers, per-layer sliding windows (1024 tokens or full attention), QK-norm, pre/post sandwich RMSNorms (as in Gemma2), and tied embeddings.
- Outputs match the HF reference implementation, including beyond the 1024-token sliding window.
- GSM8K accuracy matches the scores published on the model cards (Base 71.8 vs 71.6; SFT 91.2 vs 94.6) using the provided script in the vLLM codebase.

## Validation

**Tests** (1x A100 64GB, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0, Python 3.12.11, pytest 9.1.0):


`pre-commit` passes on all changed files.

**GSM8K** (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot):

|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Domyn-Edge-Base | `/v1/completions` | greedy | 256 | **71.8** | 71.6 |
| Domyn-Edge-SFT | `/v1/chat/completions`, thinking on | model defaults (T=1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20) | 8192 | **91.2** | 94.6 |

```bash

vllm serve domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 4096
```

## Details

Architecture highlights:

- **Interleaved RoPE / NoPE layers** (`position_layers`): NoPE layers skip the rotary embedding.

items.title: [Model] Support hotwords for Qwen3-ASR
items.body:
## Overview

`Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration.get_generation_prompt` never reads `stt_params.hotwords`, so `hotwords` sent to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` is silently dropped for Qwen3-ASR, while Fun-ASR and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize (#62329) consume it. This PR renders the hotwords into the system-turn context, which is the official SDK's `context` channel and already carries `prompt` since #35415. The hotwords go first, then the prompt, one per line.

**Why not just `prompt`?** #43430 tried this before and was closed as stale. On it, @DarkLight1337 noted that it is "more like supporting a custom system prompt rather than having actual hotwords". That is fair for Qwen3-ASR: unlike MOSS, its model card has no hotword template, so the list goes into the context as-is (adding a prefix made no difference, see Details). The value is that `hotwords` then means the same thing across Fun-ASR, MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize and Qwen3-ASR, which `prompt` cannot provide, because its meaning differs per model:
- Qwen3-ASR: context.
- Whisper: preceding text (`<|prev|>`).
- MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize: replaces the default instruction.
- Kimi-Audio: an instruction before the audio.

A client that sends a hotword list today gets it applied on Fun-ASR and MOSS, and silently dropped on Qwen3-ASR. Unlike #43430, this PR keeps the request `prompt` instead of replacing it. The `system_prompt` / `user_prompt` split suggested there touches every STT model and is left out; I'm happy to follow up on it.

Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "hotwords"` only returns #62398 (VibeVoice-ASR, its own model file). #36018 (`response_prefix`, last updated 08-25) edits the same function; `git merge-tree` shows no conflict.

## Claims

- `hotwords` now takes effect for Qwen3-ASR, alone or together with `prompt`.
- Requests without hotwords are unchanged token for token. The one exception: a whitespace-only `prompt` or `hotwords` no longer emits a system turn that holds only spaces.
- `hotwords=X` renders the same tokens as the existing `prompt=X` path, so it inherits that path's behavior; end to end, the two agree as closely as two identical runs do.
- With a short relevant list, B-WER drops by 20-30% on LibriSpeech and hard-hotword misses more than halve on Aishell1-NE (tables below).

## Validation

Setup: RTX 6000 Ada, nightly wheel 953fa44 plus this patch (its Qwen3-ASR prompt and sanitizer code match the current base), `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-{0.6B,1.7B}`, `temperature=0`.

**Unit tests**: `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_asr.py -k generation_prompt_context`. Before the patch, 5 failed (`blank`, `hotwords`, `prompt-and-hotwords`, `sanitized-hotwords`, `hotwords-forced-language`) and 2 passed (`none`, `prompt`); after, 7 passed. The tests decode the real prompt token ids.

**E2E reproducer** (Aishell-1 `BAC009S0764W0413`, reference 许玮甯最近到法国工作):

| request | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| no extra fields | 徐伟宁最近到法国工作。 | 徐伟宁最近到法国工作。 |
| `-F hotwords=许玮甯` | 徐伟宁最近到法国工作。 | **许玮甯**最近到法国工作。 |
| `-F prompt=许玮甯` | - | 许玮甯最近到法国工作。 |
| `-F hotwords=许玮甯 -F prompt=这是一段娱乐新闻。` | - | **许玮甯**最近到法国工作。 |

**Equivalence**: across 6367 utterances, `hotwords=list` vs `prompt=list` gives identical text for 97.1% (1.7B) and 96.0% (0.6B) of them. Re-running the same no-context requests gives 97.0% and 96.1%, which is batch-order noise.

**Public biasing benchmarks**, sent through the `hotwords` field:

| model | benchmark | metric | no hotwords | `hotwords` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.7B | Aishell1-NE, 808 utts, true hotwords + 20 distractors | CER / hard-hotword recall | 4.34% / 31.2% | **2.57% / 71.6%** |
| 1.7B | LibriSpeech test-clean, N=100 | WER / B-WER | 1.91% / 7.92% | **1.65% / 5.55%** |
| 1.7B | LibriSpeech test-other, N=100 | WER / B-WER | 3.64% / 16.84% | **3.24% / 12.21%** |
| 0.6B | Aishell1-NE, same lists | CER / hard-hotword recall | 5.29% / 25.6% | **3.54% / 63.2%** |
| 0.6B | LibriSpeech test-clean, N=100 | WER / B-WER | 2.28% / 10.43% | **2.03% / 8.18%** |
| 0.6B | LibriSpeech test-other, N=100 | WER / B-WER | 4.72% / 21.16% | **4.34% / 16.88%** |

## Details

- **Root cause**: #39674 added `TranscriptionRequest.hotwords` / `SpeechToTextParams.hotwords`, but each model has to map the field into its own prompt, and the Qwen3-ASR implementation never read it.
- **Rendering**: the list is passed through verbatim (sanitized like `prompt`), with no label. Adding `热词：` or `Hotwords: ` in front made no difference: CER and B-WER moved by ≤0.3 points on both models. The SDK examples also pass bare context.
- **Hotwords before the prompt**: this was measured with 5 prompts per language (generic, domain, instruction, long background, cross-language), 0/20/100 distractors on Aishell and N=100 on test-other, both models, compared with paired sign tests.
  - Aishell: hotwords-first wins on hard-hotword hits, 276:84 (p=5e-25) on 0.6B and 252:122 (p=2e-11) on 1.7B, which is +3 to +5 points of recall with short lists.
  - English: on par. 0.6B B-WER is 16.67% vs 16.84%; 1.7B is 12.25% vs 11.99%, i.e. prompt-first is slightly better there.
- **Order is per model**: #62398 (VibeVoice-ASR, open) puts the prompt before the hotwords for its own model. The order here is what measured best for Qwen3-ASR.
- **Scope**: `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, plus `/v1/audio/translations`, which shares the code path (only transcriptions was benchmarked). `/v1/realtime` keeps its own fixed prompt (#61031 wires `prompt` / `language` into it). With #61031 merged, a realtime request has no `hotwords`, so its prompt stays the same.
- **Docstring**: it claimed that the SDK's `_build_messages` omits the system role without context. It always emits one (`{"role": "system", "content": context or ""}`). The docstring now says so; the no-context prompt is kept as before.

<details>
<summary>Limitations (model behavior, not this patch)</summary>

- **The benefit decays with list length.** Same lists plus n distractors:

| distractors (Aishell / test-other) | 0 / 0 | 20 / 100 | 100 / 1000 | no hotwords |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.7B Aishell hard-hotword recall | 79.5% | 72.2% | 55.6% | 31.7% |
| 1.7B test-other B-WER | 7.85% | 12.62% | 16.58% | 16.86% |

  1000 English hotwords are ~3500 tokens against ~90 audio tokens per utterance. The docs already advise keeping lists short.
- **1.7B occasionally recites the list.** With ≥20 Mandarin distractors, 0-2 of 808 utterances per list size append the hotword list after the transcript. These runs sent the list through `prompt`, so this predates the patch; callers can bound it with `max_completion_tokens`.
- **Eval caveats**: greedy decoding only; English normalization is lowercasing and punctuation stripping, with no number normalization; distractors are drawn at random from the benchmark lists.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the patch, tests, and evaluation scripts, and to run the validation above on my machine.

items.title: [Model] Support GLM-5.3 MLA DSpark drafts on CUDA
items.body:
## Overview

Add CUDA serving support for a GLM-5.3 MLA DSpark draft exported in the speculators format, without checkpoint-side Python runtime files or startup monkey patches.

Related: [speculators#1052](https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/issues/1052), [vllm-ascend#14535](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14535). The former covers training/export and the latter is an Ascend implementation; this change targets the CUDA model, latent cache, and anchor-relative mixed-window attention. Searches for open GLM/DSpark and `GlmDSparkMLA` PRs found no matching CUDA implementation. This is distinct from K3-specific MLA refactoring and generic draft-context limits.

## Claims

- Register `GlmDSparkMLAForCausalLM` and preserve its architecture and MLA geometry through speculators config conversion.
- Reuse the Qwen3 DSpark scaffold, Markov/confidence heads, MLP, and weight loading, with an MLA decoder and compressed `512 + 64` latent/RoPE cache.
- Resolve layer count, sliding/full layout, window size, and causality from configuration, preserving the tested draft's block-anchor-relative window semantics.
- Keep this PR separate from sampling-RNG changes. Existing model routes remain the defaults.

## Validation

### Serving environment and results

The serving validation was performed on the local **vLLM 0.31.0 integration**, not the current `main` checkout. The checkpoint tensors were unchanged.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Software | vLLM `0.31.0+glmmla.20261019`, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130` |
| Target / draft | GLM-5.3 MG43 NVFP4 W4A4C8 / MLA-distilled DSpark step1750 |
| Execution | V2 GPU model runner, single-node TP4, PP1, DCP1, eager |
| Precision | BF16 draft weights and target/draft KV caches |
| Speculation | 8 draft tokens, probabilistic drafting, standard rejection, adaptive verification off |
| Workload | Fixed internal 300-request corpus, concurrency 8, original per-request sampling |
| Length limits | Context 196608, output cap 1024, respecting EOS |

| Implementation | Mean accepted length, including one target token |
|---|---:|
| Historical checkpoint-side runtime | 3.396830 |
| Same-node checkpoint-side runtime reference | 3.341220 |
| Installed vLLM 0.31.0 integration | 3.368620 |

Both same-node runs completed 300/300 requests with zero errors. Ten fixed-input comparisons (five layers, prefix lengths 257 and 2305, real checkpoint TP-rank-0 head slices) had bitwise-identical attention outputs and latent cache entries against the old runtime. A dense-reference mask check covered causal sliding and noncausal full attention around the 2048 window boundary.

These are single stochastic runs, not confidence intervals or throughput benchmarks. The evaluated 0.31.0 build retained historical draft/verifier RNG isolation; that sampler change is intentionally **not included** here. Accordingly, the figures describe the validated integration environment, not an exact end-to-end measurement of this current-main source branch. Current main declares PyTorch 2.14.0.

### Source checks on this branch

Passed `git diff --check`, AST parsing of all seven changed Python files, and Ruff checks. The checkout is sparse, so Ruff was invoked with `vllm` explicitly classified as first-party and `INP001` excluded:

```bash
git diff --check
git diff --name-only HEAD^ HEAD -- '*.py' | xargs ruff check \
  --config 'lint.isort.known-first-party = ["vllm"]' --ignore INP001
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/glm_dspark_mla.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/dspark.py vllm/config/speculative.py
```

The GPU checkpoint and request corpus are internal and are not uploaded in this PR. No automated GPU CI coverage or full pre-commit pass is claimed; the serving results above are the external-to-CI validation evidence.

## Details

### Scope and compatibility

The supported MLA geometry is deliberately restricted to Q rank 2048, KV rank 512, NoPE head dimension 192, RoPE dimension 64, and V head dimension 256. Hidden size and head count are read from configuration, subject to compatible tensor-parallel shapes.

The implementation does **not** hardcode five decoder layers or a four-sliding/one-full ordering. It resolves each layer through the existing DFlash attention configuration helper. The measured checkpoint uses four causal sliding layers with a 2048 window and one noncausal full layer; other layouts have not been evaluated. The sliding window starts relative to the draft block's anchor, not each individual query position. Default NeoX-style RoPE was evaluated; this does not claim arbitrary RoPE-scaling compatibility.

This initial path requires BF16 draft weights, eager execution, PP1 and DCP1. Graph support is explicitly disabled. The current paged kernel handles at most 16 query rows per request per call; the evaluated speculative width is 8. Cache insertion currently uses PyTorch indexed assignments; async-performance and graph-capture improvements are not claimed.

The dedicated kernel is retained because the draft's mixed causal/noncausal and anchor-relative window semantics must match training. This is not a claim that every GLM/K3 MLA checkpoint, weight layout, or backend is interchangeable. Future shared-backend work should preserve those semantics.

### Usage

The draft export declares `architectures: ["GlmDSparkMLAForCausalLM"]`; its `transformer_layer_config` declares `model_type: "glm_dspark_mla"` and the MLA dimensions. Matching weights and config are sufficient; no checkpoint-side runtime code is required.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve /path/to/target \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 196608 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/path/to/draft","num_speculative_tokens":8}'
```

The human submitter has confirmed source review and authorized submission. AI assistance was used to develop and prepare this PR.
