items.title: [Model][Frontend] Add native VibeVoice-ASR with transcription API support
items.body:
## Overview

Adds a native VibeVoice-ASR implementation (`microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF`) with `/v1/audio/transcriptions` support, including `diarized_json` (#48543). Previously the model only ran through the Transformers backend, which has no transcription endpoint. `--model-impl transformers` still selects that path. No open PR covers VibeVoice.

## Claims

- `json`, `text` and `diarized_json` responses; `prompt`/`hotwords` map to the model's context slot.
- Single-pass long-form audio (no server-side chunking), clean up to 40 min (see the 60 min row).
- Deterministic: no VAE sampling noise, unlike HF (see Details).
- Matches HF with its noise disabled: identical transcripts on 500/500 LibriSpeech, 300/300 VoxPopuli-de and 19/20 multi-speaker clips.

## Validation

fp16 on Quadro RTX 6000 24 GB (Turing). HF reference: Transformers 5.18, same prompts and inputs. All tests pass; pre-commit is clean.

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_vibevoice_asr.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_diarized.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vibevoice_asr.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_transcribe_diarize.py
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py tests/models/test_initialization.py -k VibeVoice
```

| WER (cpWER) | native | HF, noise off | HF, default noise |
|---|---|---|---|
| LibriSpeech test-clean, 500 utts | 2.14 % | 2.14 % | 2.11 % |
| VoxPopuli-de, 300 utts¹ | 12.97 % | 12.97 % | 13.15 % |
| 20 conversations, 2-3 speakers² | 1.98 (4.25) % | 1.98 (4.25) % | 1.98 (4.30) % |
| 40 min, 8 speakers², one request | 1.56 (7.9) % | OOM | — |
| 60 min, 8 speakers², one request³ | 19.0 (28.4) % | OOM | — |

| `vllm bench serve`⁴, concurrency | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Requests/s | 0.59 | 2.28 | 3.74 | 5.44 | 6.74 |
| RTFx | 4.8 | 16.2 | 26.7 | 38.8 | 48.0 |

- **Parallelism:** TP=2 and PP=2 match single-GPU transcripts (48/48 and 47/48).
- **Sync check:** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passes.
- **Single stream:** native and the Transformers backend take 198 s and 201 s for the same 100 utterances.

<details>
<summary>Notes and reproduction</summary>

¹ Excludes 10 broken items (empty reference, or non-German audio) for every system; raw WER is 17.2 % for all.
² Synthetic: LibriSpeech speakers concatenated with pauses, disjoint from the WER set.
³ Clean for the first ~35 min, then repetition loops. The cause is not the audio (minutes 30–50 alone: 2 % WER), not the encoder (latents bit-identical full-pass vs. standalone) and not fp16 (fp32 loops at the same point). The loops start once the total context exceeds ~40k tokens.
⁴ LibriSpeech, 200 requests, caches disabled; c=4/8/16 were repeated 3x with < 1 % variation.

```
vllm serve microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF --dtype float16 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --mm-processor-cache-gb 0
vllm bench serve --backend openai-audio --endpoint /v1/audio/transcriptions \
  --model microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openslr/librispeech_asr \
  --hf-subset clean --hf-split test --num-prompts 200 --max-concurrency 16
```
</details>

## Details

- **Determinism:** HF samples VAE noise at inference; here the latent mean is used. vLLM's processor, encoder and prefix caches assume deterministic embeddings, and the noise changes 3–20 % of transcripts with no accuracy gain. Reviewers, please confirm this divergence.
- **Serving change:** `parse_diarized_transcript` now receives the raw output, not the `post_process_output` result, mirroring `verbose_json`. VibeVoice needs plain text for `json` and structure for `diarized_json`. MOSS parses identically either way.
- **Transformers backend:** it caps audio at ~60 s (via the config's `max_position_embeddings=450`), OOMs on 24 GB with default settings, and crashes when batching audio of different lengths. This PR doesn't fix those issues; it avoids that path.

**Limitations**
- No native LoRA, which the fallback had. Most of the ~10 Hub adapters target the original checkpoint format; they can be merged offline. Decoder LoRA can follow (`glmasr.py` pattern).
- Validated in fp16 only. **Could a reviewer with an Ampere+ GPU please run the generation test in bf16, ideally plus a ~60 min request?**
- Beyond ~40 min, split recordings client-side. The default output cap (32,768 tokens, from `generation_config.json`) is also tight for an hour.
- Long-form serving needs the `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_*` limits and `--max-model-len` raised (documented).
- Streaming returns raw JSON.
- Speaker labels are passed through as generated (`"0"`, `"1"`, ...).
- Chat prompts don't get `<|AUDIO_DURATION|>` filled in (pre-existing).
- Startup profiling adds ~1.5 min.

Related: #32823

items.title: [Feature] Support batch invariance for ShortConv (LFM2) models
items.body:
## Overview

Fix #61319. LFM2 models (`Lfm2ForCausalLM`, `Lfm2MoeForCausalLM`) can't use batch-invariant mode: with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the engine refuses to start with `RuntimeError: VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for SHORT_CONV_ATTN.` That leaves them without the documented way to get reproducible greedy outputs. This PR lets `SHORT_CONV_ATTN` declare batch invariance. `PLE_SHORT_CONV_ATTN` stays opted out.

## Claims

- LFM2 models start and are batch-invariant under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` passes the full `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` suite (22/22) on an A40.
- The symptom in #61319 (round 0 of repeated `generate()` calls differs from later rounds) goes away in batch-invariant mode, with prefix caching on.
- No change when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is unset.

## Validation

A40 (SM86), official image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-39983a5e` (no upstream changes to the touched files between that commit and this branch's base). Probe: 8 prompts × 128 greedy tokens, 4 `generate()` rounds on one engine, then each prompt alone. Counts are prompts (out of 8) whose token ids differ. The `enforce_eager` / no-prefix-cache rows and the 22-test suite ran with an env-gated copy of the same one-line opt-in. The rest ran with this branch's file installed.

| model | config | round 0 vs rounds 1–3 | rounds 1–3 | batched vs alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LFM2-8B-A1B | main, default | 8 | 0 | 8 |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | main, `enable_prefix_caching=False` | 0 | 0 | 6 |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | main, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | engine fails to start | | |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | this PR, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | this PR, BI + `enforce_eager` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | this PR, BI + `enable_prefix_caching=False` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| LFM2-1.2B | main, default | 2 | 0 | 3 |
| LFM2-1.2B | this PR, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | **0** | **0** | **0** |

Upstream BI suite with this change:

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py
# 22 passed in 1057s (FLASH_ATTN / FLEX_ATTENTION / TRITON_ATTN)
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=LiquidAI/LFM2-1.2B pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN]"
# 1 passed in 35s
```

## Details

**Why #61319 happens.** LFM2 runs with prefix caching on by default (`mamba_cache_mode=align`, block size 16). From round 1 on, any prompt with a full block gets a cache hit, so the first prefill step shrinks (92 → 76 tokens in my probe, where only the 17-token prompt hits). Without batch invariance, kernel selection depends on batch shape. Every sequence in that step then moves by a few ULPs, and near-tied argmaxes flip later. In my runs, two warm rounds never disagreed. With prefix caching on but no prompt long enough to hit, all rounds match. This is the documented "no bitwise reproducibility by default" behavior, and the documented fix is batch-invariant mode, which LFM2 couldn't use. Setting `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:16:8 CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=1`, as #61440 does, still leaves 2/8 prompts differing, because this isn't run-to-run atomics.

**Why ShortConv qualifies.** `causal_conv1d_fn` (prefill) and `causal_conv1d_update` (decode) compute each output token from that sequence's own `L_cache` window plus its conv-state slot. There is no reduction across sequences and no split depending on batch size. The rest of the layer is `in_proj`/`out_proj`, which already go through the batch-invariant linear path, plus elementwise gating.

**Scope and limitations.**
- `PLE_SHORT_CONV_ATTN` (Qwen4Exp's dilated conv) inherits from `ShortConvAttentionBackend`. It is explicitly kept at `False`: it uses its own packing path, and I couldn't validate it.
- All runs used Model Runner V2 (the default). The check is shared with V1 through `get_mamba_attn_backend`, but V1 wasn't run.
- Spec decoding under batch invariance and LFM2-VL weren't tested.
- Only Ampere (SM86) was tested.
- I didn't add an end-to-end LFM2 line to CI. If you want one, `VLLM_TEST_MODEL=LiquidAI/LFM2-1.2B ... -k FLASH_ATTN` on the needle test costs ~35 s per variant, and I'm happy to add it.

**Not a duplicate.** The only PR linked to #61319 is #61440. It forces deterministic cuBLAS/cuDNN settings globally, which doesn't address this (see above), and its diff currently spans 891 files. I searched open PRs for `supports_batch_invariance`, `SHORT_CONV_ATTN`/ShortConv, and LFM2 batch invariance. #45819 (GDN) and the Mamba2 BI PRs touch other backends only.

items.title: [Model] Support hotwords for MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Overview

`MossTranscribeDiarizeForConditionalGeneration.get_generation_prompt` ignores `stt_params.hotwords`, so `hotwords` sent to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` is silently dropped for MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize (only Fun-ASR consumes it today). This PR appends the hotwords to the prompt using the [model card's hotword recipe](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize) (`<instruction>热词提示：w1, w2`).

Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue touches MOSS hotwords (`gh pr list --state open --search "hotwords"` / `"MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize"`). #50362 (verbose_json) edits the same model file in a different function and does not conflict.

## Claims

- `hotwords` now takes effect for MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize, with or without a custom `prompt`. Blank `hotwords` keeps the old prompt byte-for-byte.
- With a short relevant list, error rates on hotwords roughly halve on public biasing benchmarks (tables below); overall WER/CER also drops.
- Documents `hotwords` (previously undocumented) in the speech-to-text guide, including a note that long or unrelated lists can hurt accuracy.

## Validation

Setup: RTX 6000 Ada, nightly wheel at the base commit plus this patch, `vllm serve OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize --trust-remote-code`, `temperature=0`.

**Unit tests**: `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_transcribe_diarize.py`: before the patch 2 failed (`hotwords`, `custom-prompt-hotwords`); after, 14 passed.

**E2E reproducer**: `curl localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions -F model=moss -F file=@clip.wav -F temperature=0 -F hotwords="珞珈数科, 钛动科技"`. Before the patch the output was identical to sending no hotwords; after, it is identical to writing the model card recipe into `prompt` by hand (洛嘉数科 -> 珞珈数科). Outputs without hotwords are unchanged.

**Public biasing benchmarks** (real speech, short relevant lists):

| benchmark | metric | no hotwords | `hotwords` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aishell1-NE, 808 utts | CER / hard-hotword recall | 6.46% / 18.3% | **2.54% / 93.8%** |
| LibriSpeech test-clean, N=100 | WER / B-WER | 2.23% / 9.45% | **2.02% / 5.05%** |
| LibriSpeech test-other, N=100 | WER / B-WER | 4.93% / 21.54% | **3.83% / 10.39%** |

<details>
<summary>Full tables (distractors, long lists, English recipe)</summary>

Aishell1-NE (from [SeACo-Paraformer](https://github.com/R1ckShi/SeACo-Paraformer); R1 = hard hotwords):

| hotwords | CER | hotword recall | R1 recall |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | 6.46% | 58.7% | 18.3% |
| hotwords in the utterance | 2.54% | 96.8% | 93.8% |
| + 20 distractors | 3.18% | 92.3% | 84.3% |
| full 400-word list | 9.83%* | 72.2% | 49.2% |

\* Excludes 8 runaway utterances; 95.33% with them.

LibriSpeech rare-word biasing ([Le et al. 2021](https://github.com/facebookresearch/fbai-speech/tree/master/is21_deep_bias), official `score.py`), scored on utterances where no condition ran away (output > 2x reference + 5 words): 2465/2620 test-clean, 2770/2939 test-other. Runaways are counted over the full set.

| set | condition | WER | B-WER | runaways |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| test-clean | none | 2.23% | 9.45% | 0 |
| test-clean | `hotwords`, N=100 | 2.02% | 5.05% | 3 |
| test-clean | model card English recipe via `prompt`, N=100 | 2.46% | 6.16% | 23 |
| test-clean | `hotwords`, N=1000 | 12.67% | 17.39% | 134 |
| test-other | none | 4.93% | 21.54% | 1 |
| test-other | `hotwords`, N=100 | 3.83% | 10.39% | 1 |
| test-other | model card English recipe via `prompt`, N=100 | 4.45% | 12.43% | 17 |
| test-other | `hotwords`, N=1000 | 14.04% | 27.27% | 151 |

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause**: #39674 added `TranscriptionRequest.hotwords` and `SpeechToTextParams.hotwords`, but each model must map it into its own prompt format; the MOSS implementation (#47729) never read the field.
- **One hint for all languages**: the model card has a Chinese default instruction with `热词提示：` and an English variant with `Hotwords:`. On English audio, the Chinese default with `热词提示：` beat the English recipe on both LibriSpeech sets (B-WER 5.05% vs 6.16% and 10.39% vs 12.43%) and had far fewer runaways (3 vs 23 and 1 vs 17), so there is no per-language switch.
- **The list is passed through verbatim** (stripped) rather than re-joined, matching how Fun-ASR treats the same field.
- **Limitation (model behavior, not this patch)**: long lists (400 zh / 1000 en terms) cause repetition loops or leak list terms after the transcript, and accuracy drops below the no-hotword baseline even after excluding runaways. The docs now advise keeping the list short; callers can bound runaways with `max_completion_tokens`.
- **Eval caveats**: English normalization was lowercasing and punctuation stripping only, with no number normalization, so absolute numbers are not comparable to papers, but conditions are comparable to each other. Runaway filtering favors the N=1000 rows. Greedy decoding only.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the patch, tests, and evaluation scripts, and to run the validation above on my machine.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Support unequal P/D TP for hybrid Mamba models
items.body:
## Overview

Enables PD disaggregation with the Mooncake connector when prefill and decode engines use different tensor-parallel sizes (e.g. P=TP1, D=TP2) for hybrid Mamba models (Mamba1, GDN). Before this change, unequal TP either failed validation or silently registered the wrong byte ranges for packed Mamba cache pages, corrupting the transferred state.

Duplicate-work check: open PRs were searched for Mooncake, Mamba/GDN, and unequal/heterogeneous TP overlap; none address unequal P/D TP for hybrid Mamba models with the Mooncake connector.

## Claims

- Fixes silent Mamba/GDN state corruption on unequal P/D TP: each decode rank now transfers exactly the conv sub-projections and SSM state slice it owns.
- Supports both TP ratio directions (P_TP > D_TP and P_TP < D_TP) for GDN and Mamba1 in the Mooncake connector.
- Adds a `mamba_transfer_geometry` handshake (shapes, dtypes, conv layout, Mamba type, replication) so the receiving side validates the peer's state geometry before transfer. Equal-TP deployments neither send nor require it, so the wire format stays backward compatible.
- Reuses the shared `ssm_conv_transfer_utils` decomposition (previously used by NIXL/MORIIO) instead of duplicating it, and extends it to the SD `(state_len, dim)` conv layout.
- Restores region coalescing for equal TP and for replicated producer caches without Mamba regions.

## Validation

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
                 tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py -q
```

New and updated coverage:

- `test_gdn_rawpages_reshard_states_and_preserve_canaries`: GDN end to end for (P_TP, D_TP) in (1,2), (2,1), (4,2), (2,2); asserts exact payload bytes and canary preservation.
- `test_mamba1_rawpages_reshard_states_and_preserve_canaries`: Mamba1 end to end for (1,2) and (2,1) in both SD and DS conv layouts.
- `test_equal_tp_mamba_merge_needs_no_peer_geometry`: equal TP requires no geometry and still coalesces Mamba sub-regions.
- `test_unequal_tp_rejects_unsupported_mamba_states`: clear error for unsupported state types.
- `test_prepared_regions_revalidate_changed_peer_geometry`: peer geometry mismatch is rejected at prepare time.
- `test_region_length_validation_preserves_replicated_mla`: replicated MLA regions still validate.

Unit tests pass locally: `python3 -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py -q`.

End-to-end (author): PD disaggregation with the Mooncake connector, P=TP1 / D=TP2, GDN hybrid model: validated.

## Details

Root cause: a Mamba cache page is packed (conv state followed by SSM state, and for GDN the conv state itself packs Q|K|V sub-projections), so its per-rank layout under unequal TP is not a contiguous slice of the whole page. Slicing by the TP ratio passed the length check but wrote garbage state.

The fix decomposes the page: the conv dimension is split into per-rank sub-projections derived from `MambaSpec` (shared, layout-aware helper), registered as separate transfer regions alongside the SSM state, and the sender-side plan maps each sub-region to the peer offset for both ratio directions. Attention regions keep head-clamped TP planning while Mamba regions use raw TP, matching how each cache is actually sharded.

Minimal flow for the changed path (hybrid Mamba model, P_TP=1, D_TP=2):

1. Prefill registers one transfer region per Mamba sub-piece (each conv sub-projection slice plus the SSM state slice) instead of one whole page per layer.
2. The handshake metadata carries `mamba_transfer_geometry` (per-layer shapes, dtypes, conv layout, Mamba type, replication).
3. Before planning any transfer, the peer's geometry is validated against the local one; mismatches fail fast with a clear error.
4. Per request, the sender emits one copy per sub-region: the conv/SSM slice the decode rank owns, at the peer offset determined by the TP ratio direction.
5. Each decode rank receives exactly the slice it owns; no whole-page slicing by TP ratio remains.

Limitations: Mamba2 is still rejected for unequal TP with a clear error (follow-up). The geometry handshake is only exercised when TP sizes differ.

items.title: [Model] Support box and ground decisions with GUI-Actor
items.body:
## Overview Adds `box` and `ground` as structured-decision primitives, answered by GUI-Actor's pointer head, and the `GuiActorForConditionalGeneration` architecture that serves it. `/v1/systemone` gains two question types that locate a target in an image instead of picking an option. The primitives follow the TypeSafe "System One" contract, so a request written for the reference serving layer answers here the same way. Closes #62247, which carries the API design write-up. No other PR covers this: searched `box ground`, `gui-actor`, `pointer head`, `bounding box question`, `ground question` and `systemone` for open PRs — the `systemone` hits are unrelated frontend fixes, none adds a spatial question type or a pointer-head model. ## Claims - `/v1/systemone` accepts `{"type": "box"}` and `{"type": "ground"}` questions: a box returns four normalised edges, a ground returns a 0–999 click point, each with a confidence. - `microsoft/GUI-Actor-{3B,7B}-Qwen2.5-VL` serve through vLLM, detected from their weights with no config change. - Answers are decoded from the pointer head's per-patch distribution using the reference implementation's arithmetic, byte-identical on 600 randomised grids. - Scores **90.49 / 95.12 / 84.87** (All / text / icon) `hit_top1` on ScreenSpot, against **79.09 / 83.79 / 73.39** for the Jev reference `box`. - A model that cannot answer a question type returns 501, not 400. ## Validation **Test results** (this host, CUDA 12.8, 4×A40): | Scope | Result | |---|---| | `test_spatial.py` + `test_question_types.py` + `test_gui_actor_pointer_head.py` | 58 passed | | `test_strategies.py` + `test_decisions.py` | 99 passed | | Full structured-decisions + config suite | 219 passed, 2 failed¹ | | **GPU e2e** (`test_gui_actor.py`, 3B, 17.8 GiB budget) | **3 passed / 71 s** | | `ruff check` / `ruff format` | clean | ¹ `meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct` and the EAGLE3 draft model are gated-repo failures on an unauthenticated host; unrelated to this change and failing identically on the base commit. **Decode arithmetic is the reference arithmetic.** The same 600-grid comparison behind the claim above returned bit-identical `box` edges, `ground` points and confidences against the reference serving layer. **ScreenSpot** (1272 samples, `hit_top1`, identical harness): | | text | icon | All | median latency | |---|---|---|---|---| | Jev reference `box` | 83.79 | 73.39 | 79.09 | 1256 ms | | **this PR** | **95.12** | **84.87** | **90.49** | **700 ms** | **End-to-end**, on an 18 GiB budget (matching the CI MIG slice): ``` BOX : {"box": {"bottom": 0.821444, "left": 0.0, "right": 0.848678, "top": 0.072072}, "confidence": 0.830029} GROUND: {"point": [657, 467], "confidence": 0.016932, "topk_points": [[657, 467], [512, 489], [207, 428], ...]} ``` **Reproduce:** ```bash pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/ -q pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_gui_actor_pointer_head.py -q pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_gui_actor.py -q # needs a GPU ``` ## Details ### Why the pooler returns raw logits `GuiActorPooler` returns the head's raw `proj_dec @ proj_enc.T / sqrt(d)` scores. Softmaxing them in the pooler would give a row that already sums to one, and the decode softmaxes again at the checkpoint's temperature — a second softmax over a normalised row flattens the distribution and moves every decoded edge. ### Why the temperature never moves the geometry The checkpoint ships a fitted `pointer_temperature`. It scales the confidence only: the region or box is extracted from the raw distribution first, and the temperature is applied to the probability mass afterwards. This matches the reference, and `test_spatial.py` pins it. ### Why the embed-layer capture is cloned The head's encoder side reads the embed layer's output, the vision features as they were scattered into the placeholders. `embed_input_ids` clones it because the runner writes the result into a preallocated buffer it reuses every step; holding a reference would read the next step's tokens at pooling time. ### Why chunked prefill and prefix caching are off The answer is read from the image patches of the prompt's own prefill. A chunked prompt leaves the capture without them, and a cached image prefix skips the embed forward entirely. Both are disabled in `GuiActorForConditionalGenerationConfig`. The reference layer hit a related bug by keying its image prefix cache on token ids — Qwen2.5-VL renders an image as a fixed run of `<|image_pad|>` whose length depends only on the image size, so two equal-size screenshots collided. ### Why detection keys on tensor names `is_gui_actor_checkpoint` accepts either a `...WithPointer` architecture name or the `multi_patch_pointer_head.` tensor prefix. The tensors are authoritative: a config can declare the pointer token ids without a trained head, and such a model would serve a random grounding score. The architecture name is checked first because it costs no download. The weight check is gated on the config still naming a Qwen2.5-VL architecture. Without that gate the class rewrites its own `text_config` and constructs itself from inside its own `__init__` — 34 levels deep, allocating a model per level, until the device runs out of memory. ### Why other backbones are rejected `MODEL_ARCH_CONFIG_CONVERTORS` dispatches on `model_type`, and only `qwen2_5_vl` has a GUI-Actor convertor. A pointer checkpoint over another backbone would otherwise load as a plain backbone with its pointer tensors silently unmatched. `assert_no_foreign_gui_actor`, called from the base convertor, rejects a `...WithPointer` architecture on any other model type at load. ### Scope and follow-ups - **Only Qwen2.5-VL backbones.** The head's projection is square, which needs the vision tower's output width to equal the language model's. Qwen3-VL and Qwen3.5 are a follow-up. - **`/v1/decisions` does not accept the new types.** It keeps OpenAI's schema; a box or ground question there is a 422, unchanged. ### Complexity Production diff is **+1434/−29**. Of that, 382 lines are `spatial.py`, a straight port of the reference decoder whose correctness is established by comparison rather than design; 344 are the new model architecture, comparable to `d3.py` plus its pooler; the rest extends the existing question-type and strategy contracts rather than adding parallel implementations. New primitives and a new architecture account for the size.
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Touches no core component (model runner, scheduler, `v1/core`); reuses the `clef_flash` / `d3` patterns for pooling models, `WeightsMapper`, and the multimodal processor registry. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Unit, contract and GPU e2e tests added; the e2e runs inside the CI shard's 18 GiB budget using the 3B checkpoint. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Single-call-site helpers inlined, comments limited to non-obvious invariants, docs updated. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Claims carry reproduction commands; root causes and tradeoffs are in Details.

items.title: [ROCm][Model] Add Beam 1.0 support on ROCm
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview


ROCm follow-up to [#61978](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61978), which adds day-0 support for Reflection's [Beam 1.0](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B) and its [DFlash2 drafter](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2).


EDIT: Since #61978 has been split into smaller PRs (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62042, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62052, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62074), I've updated against main and now the PR diff isn't swamped by the changes from #61978.

This PR adds AMD-owned implementations under `vllm/models/beam/amd/` for both `BeamForCausalLM` and `DFlash2BeamDraftModel`. The NVIDIA implementation from #61978 is unchanged in the relative diff. Shared package dispatch selects the AMD classes on ROCm and the NVIDIA classes elsewhere.

## Claims

- Beam 1.0 BF16 loads and serves on 8x MI350X with TP8 and expert parallelism through the AMD model path.
- Beam's required FP32 activation, normalization, Q/K preprocessing, attention-output gate, and logit-softcap arithmetic is retained in AMD-local Triton kernels.
- The AMD target uses standard vLLM ROCm attention and KV-cache updates, linear layers, finalized MoE output, and RCCL collectives rather than NVIDIA direct-cache, CuTe/FlashInfer, or MNNVL fast paths.
- The AMD DFlash2 implementation loads the released 1.93B drafter, generates successfully, and delegates cache writes and cache-format handling to the selected ROCm attention backend.
- The change adds no HIP/C++ kernels and does not modify the scheduler, KV-cache manager, model runner, attention backends, or NVIDIA Beam implementation.
- Added recipe in line with https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/issues/1107

### Serving commands

Target only:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --reasoning-parser beam \
  --tool-call-parser beam \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

With DFlash2:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --speculative-config '{
    "method": "dflash",
    "model": "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 8
  }'
```

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 10.1, PyTorch 2.13, TP8 with expert parallelism, Beam 1.0 BF16 and the BF16 DFlash2 drafter.

| Check | Target only | DFlash2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ruff checks and formatting | Passed | Passed |
| Current-source ROCm build | Passed | Passed |
| Full 501B checkpoint and drafter load | Passed | Passed |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, strict extraction | 1,202/1,319 (91.13% ± 0.78%) | 1,200/1,319 (90.98% ± 0.79%) |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, flexible extraction | 1,212/1,319 (91.89% ± 0.75%) | 1,212/1,319 (91.89% ± 0.75%) |

The GSM8K used 5-shot chat, greedy decoding, `max_gen_toks=1024`, TP8, and expert parallelism.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B,tensor_parallel_size=8,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=16384,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enable_expert_parallel=True \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size auto \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024
```

The lm-eval vLLM wrapper also accepts the top-level speculative aliases:

```text
spec_method=dflash,spec_model=/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2,spec_tokens=8
```

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model beam \
  --tokenizer /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dataset-name random \
  --num-prompts 10 \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 10 \
  --max-concurrency 10 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 42
```

</details>

### Short concurrency sweep
On NVIDIA SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` / `low_entropy`, with a fixed 1,024-token output, greedy decoding, 16 warmup requests per point, and `10 * concurrency` measured requests:

| Concurrency | Prompts | Target tok/s | DFlash2 tok/s | Speedup | Target TTFT | DFlash2 TTFT | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10 | 117.40 | 168.47 | 1.44x | 234.66 ms | 241.48 ms | 3.41 |
| 4 | 40 | 331.88 | 443.00 | 1.33x | 657.87 ms | 297.50 ms | 3.51 |
| 8 | 80 | 492.26 | 769.78 | 1.56x | 634.83 ms | 240.43 ms | 3.63 |
| 16 | 160 | 803.81 | 1,263.22 | 1.57x | 788.46 ms | 265.18 ms | 3.57 |

All 580 measured requests across both modes succeeded. DFlash2 token acceptance ranged from 30.13% to 32.83%. These are single runs without variability estimates.

<details>
<summary>SPEED-Bench run configuration</summary>

Both servers used the same target configuration:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --served-model-name beam \
  --disable-log-requests
```

The DFlash2 server added:

```bash
--speculative-config '{
  "method": "dflash",
  "model": "/path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 8
}'
```

Each server was reused across all four concurrency points. `vllm bench serve` issued its initial probe and 16 warmup requests before the measured requests at each point:

```bash
for concurrency in 1 4 8 16; do
  num_prompts=$((10 * concurrency))
  vllm bench serve \
    --backend vllm \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --model beam \
    --tokenizer /path/to/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
    --dataset-name speed_bench \
    --dataset-path /path/to/prepared/speed-bench \
    --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_8k \
    --speed-bench-category low_entropy \
    --speed-bench-output-len 1024 \
    --num-prompts "${num_prompts}" \
    --num-warmups 16 \
    --max-concurrency "${concurrency}" \
    --request-rate inf \
    --ignore-eos \
    --temperature 0 \
    --seed 42
done
```

</details>

### Remaining validation

- [x] Accuracy benchmarks (with and without dflash2)
  - [X] GSM8k 
  - [x] GPQA-diamond
  - [x] AIME2025
- [X] Performance baseline using NVIDIA [speedbench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) 8k with low entropy and 1k fixed OSL
- [x] Same checks for gfx942

## Details

- **Vendor ownership:** All ROCm target and DFlash2 implementation code lives under `vllm/models/beam/amd/`. The relative diff does not modify `vllm/models/beam/nvidia/`.
- **Platform dispatch:** `vllm.models.beam` exports AMD target and draft classes on ROCm and NVIDIA classes on other platforms.
- **Target execution:** AMD attention uses ordinary backend-owned K/V cache updates. AMD projections use standard vLLM linear layers, MoE returns finalized output normally, and distributed reductions use standard RCCL paths.
- **DFlash2 cache handling:** AMD-local Triton computes context K normalization and RoPE. Cache layout, slot scattering, optional shuffling, and quantization are delegated to each ROCm attention backend's native cache-update API rather than hard-coded pointer arithmetic.
- **Numerics:** AMD-local Triton kernels retain Beam's required FP32 operations and intermediate BF16 rounding boundaries.
- **HIP launch compatibility:** AMD kernels omit CUDA-only Triton launch options such as `enable_reflect_ftz` and `launch_pdl`.
- **Footprint:** 1,968 additions and 2 deletions across 12 Beam model files; no core execution or NVIDIA implementation changes.

AI assistance was used. The submitter should review every changed line and this description before converting the PR from draft.

items.title: [Docs][Model] Sync supported-model tables with the registry and add a consistency test
items.body:
## Overview

Syncs the supported-model docs tables with the model registry (36 undocumented architectures, 5 stale rows, 1 removed-architecture row, 2 missing `<sup>C</sup>` markers) and adds three consistency tests to `tests/models/test_registry.py` that pin the docs to the registry in both directions. Docs-only change plus tests; no runtime code touched.

## Claims

- Every architecture in the documented registry dicts (`_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS`, `_EMBEDDING_MODELS`, `_LATE_INTERACTION_MODELS`, `_REWARD_MODELS`, `_TOKEN_CLASSIFICATION_MODELS`, `_SEQUENCE_CLASSIFICATION_MODELS`, `_MULTIMODAL_MODELS`) now has a row in the model docs tables.
- Every architecture token in the docs tables is now either a registry architecture, a converted model (row marked `<sup>C</sup>`), or a documented non-registry architecture (out-of-tree plugin / Transformers fallback / speculative decoding); pooling-mode enum tokens (`ALL`, `CLS`, `LAST`, ...) are allowlisted as non-architectures.
- Removed architectures (`_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS`) no longer appear in the docs tables.
- Three deterministic CPU-only tests enforce all three invariants going forward, red/green-verified against the pre-fix docs.

## Validation

Red/green, CPU-only (macOS arm64, `.venv`, torch 2.14.1 + repo requirements). The tests are from this PR in both runs; only the docs differ.

**Red** — docs at upstream `main` (`0c2584929`), tests added:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "are_registered or are_documented or are_absent" -v
```

- `test_docs_architectures_are_registered` **FAILED** — 9 stale tokens: `KimiAudioForConditionalGeneration`, `MiniMaxVL01ForConditionalGeneration`, `NVLM_D_Model`, `Qwen2_5OmniThinkerForConditionalGeneration`, `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration` (×2, main + transcription tables), `GemmaForSequenceClassification`, `JinaVLForSequenceClassification`, `Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification`
- `test_registry_architectures_are_documented` **FAILED** — 36 missing architectures (BertForMaskedLM, CohereCompassForConditionalGeneration, DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel, DeepseekV41ForCausalLM, Dots3NoteForCausalLM, EmbeddingGemma2Model, ExaoneMoEForCausalLM, FunAudioChatForConditionalGeneration, Glm5NextForCausalLM, Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration, HfMoondream, InklingForCausalLM, InklingForConditionalGeneration, JinaVLForRanking, LLaMAForCausalLM, LagunaForCausalLM, Llama4ForCausalLM, LongcatFlashNgramForCausalLM, MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration, MiniCPMV4_7ForConditionalGeneration, Ministral3ForCausalLM, MoonshotKimiaForCausalLM, NVLM_D, NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM, NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3, NemotronH_Super_Omni_Reasoning_V3, NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration, Qwen2_5OmniForConditionalGeneration, Qwen2_5OmniModel, Qwen3OmniMoeForConditionalGeneration, Qwen3_5ForCausalLM, Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM, Qwen4ExpForCausalLM, Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration, Step3TextForCausalLM, Terratorch)
- `test_removed_architectures_are_absent_from_docs` **FAILED** — `MiniMaxVL01ForConditionalGeneration` (in supported_models.md)

**Green** — with this PR's docs changes, same command: **3 passed**.

`pre-commit run --files <4 changed files>` — all hooks passed (incl. forbidden-imports, ruff, typos).

## Details

The worklist was generated mechanically (AST parse of `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py`, resolving the `**{...}` merge of `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS` aliases into `_EMBEDDING_MODELS`, diffed against first-column tokens of every model docs table), not by hand. Per-row facts come from source: LoRA/PP flags from the module class bases, example models from `tests/models/registry.py` (`TBA` where the test registry has none).

Fix classes:

1. **New rows** for recent registry additions, in the table their dict dictates (text vs multimodal vs pooling page): Qwen3.5 text-only pair, Qwen4-Exp pair, GLM-5.3 pair, Laguna, Llama 4 text-only, Step3 text-only, Inkling pair, DeepSeek-V4.1, Cohere Compass, Dots3Note, FunAudioChat, Nemotron-Parse, EmbeddingGemma 2, Terratorch, DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel.
2. **Alias merges** into existing rows where the registry key is an alias of a documented arch: `LLaMAForCausalLM`, `Ministral3ForCausalLM`, `ExaoneMoEForCausalLM`, `NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM`, `LongcatFlashNgramForCausalLM`, `HfMoondream`, `MiniCPMV4_6/4_7ForConditionalGeneration`, `NemotronH_(Super_)Omni_Reasoning_V3`, `BertForMaskedLM`.
3. **Stale renames** to current registry keys (listed in Validation). `D3ForSequenceClassification`, `ClefFlashForJointSchema` and `ClefOmniForJointSchema` were left as-is: they are already documented in `structured_decisions_models.md`, which the tests scan.
4. **Removals/markers**: the `MiniMaxVL01ForConditionalGeneration` row (arch removed in v0.23, docs keep no previously-supported section), and the `<sup>C</sup>` converted-model marker added to the two scoring rows missing it — both are served by the same online `seq_cls_model_loader` conversion as their marked siblings (bge-reranker-v2-gemma via `no_post_processing`, Qwen3-VL-Reranker).

Test design: deterministic file parsing (no network, no GPU, no model loading), skips when `docs/` is absent (installed-package runs), and carries `skip_global_cleanup` since it creates no global vLLM state. The `<sup>C</sup>` marker is the docs' own convention for converted models, so the exemption is structural rather than a name allowlist.

Not duplicating existing work: #47271 also touches `supported_models.md` but only adds the OpenPangu V2 row together with its registry entries (a consistent pair — these tests stay green under it in either merge order). No other open PR syncs the tables.

AI assistance was used to generate the worklist, the docs edits, and the tests; every changed line was reviewed and the red/green validation above was run by the human submitter's side.

items.title: [Perf][Model] Support torch.compile for the PaddleOCR-VL vision encoder

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Overview

Adds `torch.compile` support for the PaddleOCR-VL vision encoder. `SiglipEncoderLayer` gets the `@support_torch_compile` decorator behind `compile_mm_encoder`, following Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and Pixtral ([#57168](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57168)). Nothing changes unless `compile_mm_encoder=True`.

## Claims

- `compile_mm_encoder=True` compiles PaddleOCR-VL's 27 SigLIP encoder layers. The first layer compiles in about 4 s, the other 26 reuse it, and restarts load from the cache.
- With `vllm bench serve` on H100, throughput rises by 1.8–7.3% and mean TTFT falls by 3.3–9.8% at concurrency 1–256. The gain exceeds the trial-to-trial range at concurrency 64–256.
- On the full OmniDocBench recognition set, throughput rises by 1.4% and accuracy is unchanged within BF16 noise.

## Validation

Setup: H100, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 (`c5630ab`) in BF16, base `2631afd3f`. Both versions use `-cc.mode=3 -cc.cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and differ only in `-cc.compile_mm_encoder`.

**OmniDocBench recognition.** 19,251 regions from all 1,651 public pages, concurrency 64, prefix caching off, 32 warmup crops, one measured pass per version. The harness is the same as in [#61458](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61458).

| Metric | Compile off | Compile on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Throughput, crops/s | 76.58 | 77.65  |
| EngineCore CPU time, ms/crop | 13.64 | 13.43 |
| Text NED ↓ | 0.015787 | 0.015652 |
| Formula NED ↓ | 0.062234 | 0.062199 |
| Table TEDS ↑ | 0.952008 | 0.951610 |


**`vllm bench serve` (random-mm).** The serve flags, bench flags, image mix and seeds for c=32–256 match #61458. c=1 and c=8 were added with 128 and 256 prompts. Each configuration ran 3 trials, alternating off and on per trial. Throughput is the mean, with min–max in parentheses; TTFT is the mean of the per-trial means. All 11,520 requests succeeded.

| Concurrency | Off req/s | On req/s | Gain | Mean TTFT off → on |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 7.35 (7.22–7.53) | 7.66 (7.40–7.80) | +4.2% | 50.8 → 45.8 ms (−9.8%) |
| 8 | 29.24 (28.05–30.19) | 29.93 (29.35–30.27) | +2.3% | 139.5 → 128.5 ms (−7.9%) |
| 32 | 49.35 (46.45–51.90) | 50.24 (47.57–52.24) | +1.8% | 312.7 → 299.1 ms (−4.3%) |
| 64 | 52.68 (50.61–55.00) | 56.52 (54.67–58.78) | +7.3% | 598.5 → 565.6 ms (−5.5%) |
| 128 | 56.64 (54.72–57.66) | 59.21 (58.52–60.05) | +4.5% | 1,118 → 1,065 ms (−4.8%) |
| 256 | 55.31 (54.06–56.30) | 58.68 (56.43–61.11) | +6.1% | 2,163 → 2,091 ms (−3.3%) |

P99 TTFT improved at c=1, 8, 32 and 128, and was slightly worse at c=64 (+2.2%) and c=256 (+0.6%). This sweep ran on an H100 shared with other jobs; alternating the variants spreads that interference across both.

**Outputs, TP and sync checks.** 32 text-image prompts, including one with two images, at temperature 0 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Off and on outputs were identical for 32 of 32 prompts at both TP=1 and TP=2, and no syncs were flagged. At TP=2, the all-gather inside the attention layer compiles and runs correctly.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/compile/fullgraph/test_multimodal_compile.py -k paddleocr -v   # new: 2 passed
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest tests/model_executor/test_paddleocr_vl_mrope.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py -k "paddle or mrope"   # 5 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                          # passed
```

The new test checks the number of compiled modules: 2 for the language model when the flag is off, and 29 when it is on (one more per encoder layer). It runs in the `PyTorch Fullgraph` CI step.

## Details

**Scope.** Only `SiglipEncoderLayer` is compiled; the layers account for nearly all encoder time. The patch embedding and projector contain per-image Python loops (position-embedding interpolation and the 2×2 merge `rearrange`), which would cause graph breaks or recompiles. `hidden_states` is `[1, num_patches, hidden]`, so its dynamic dimension is 1.

**Encoder-only speedup.** Measured by timing eager and compiled encoders alternately on the same scheduled batches:

| Batch | Eager | Compiled | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 image, 192 tokens | 15.1 ms | 10.8 ms | 1.40× |
| 1 image, 609 tokens | 15.0 ms | 12.1 ms | 1.24× |
| 1 image, 2,160 tokens | 68.6 ms | 65.2 ms | 1.05× |
| 8 images, 3,794–5,021 tokens | 81.6–119.1 ms | 75.8–112.5 ms | 1.06–1.08× |



**Relation to other PRs.** [#44394](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44394) adds encoder CUDA graphs for PaddleOCR-VL. The two PRs are independent: this one does not touch the code paths #44394 changes, and it applies with or without encoder graphs. Running both together, where the encoder graphs would capture the compiled layers, is not covered here. No open or closed PR adds encoder compilation for PaddleOCR-VL.


<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

Model: `PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6` @ `c5630abae1d940eafe0697512a0325494b02ab42`. Use the same commands for both variants, changing only `-cc.compile_mm_encoder`.

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --served-model-name paddleocr-vl --dtype bfloat16 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18356 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.18 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 8589934592 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 4 --seed 42 \
  -cc.mode=3 -cc.cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY \
  -cc.compile_mm_encoder=true   # or false
```

Synthetic benchmark. Seeds: c=1 → 1042–1044, c=8 → 1142–1144, c=32 → 42–44, c=64 → 142–144, c=128 → 242–244, c=256 → 342–344. Prompts and warmups: c=1 → 128/8, c=8 → 256/16, others → 512/32.

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18356 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model paddleocr-vl \
  --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" --dataset-name random-mm \
  --random-input-len 64 --random-output-len 64 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
  --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config \
  '{(224, 224, 1): 0.25, (448, 896, 1): 0.25, (896, 448, 1): 0.25, (896, 896, 1): 0.25}' \
  --temperature 0 --ignore-eos --request-rate inf \
  --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" --num-warmups "$NUM_WARMUPS" \
  --max-concurrency "$CONCURRENCY" --seed "$SEED"
```

OmniDocBench uses the same dataset, revisions, crop extraction, prompts, token limits and scoring as #61458.

</details>

items.body:
## Overview

ROCm side of Step-5-Preview support. #61727 adds [stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview](https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview) for NVIDIA (SM90/SM103 only). This PR adds the `amd/` implementation under `vllm/models/step5/`, with portable Triton kernels for compressed sparse attention (CSA) and 3-layer MTP. Validated on 8x MI300X.

The `step5` reasoning and tool parsers come from #61727. Until it lands, the existing `step3p5` parsers handle Step-5 output.

## Claims

- Step-5-Preview (FP8, TP8) serves on ROCm with text and image input, with no CUDA-only dependencies.
- CSA runs on the 23 full-attention layers for prefill, chunked prefill and decode. Its state lives in two side caches managed by the existing KV-cache manager, with no scheduler changes and no GPU-to-CPU syncs.
- MTP works with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`: same GSM8K accuracy, about 2.3x faster (earlier revision).
- Step-5's hub `tokenizer_class` is overridden in vLLM, as for Step-3.7.

### Serving command (ROCm, MTP enabled)

<details>
<summary>Serve Step-5-Preview on 8x MI300X</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --reasoning-parser step3p5 \
  --tool-call-parser step3p5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

After #61727 merges, switch to `--reasoning-parser step5 --tool-call-parser step5`.

| Flag | Why |
|---|---|
| `--moe-backend triton` | Required. Every MoE layer clamps SwiGLU at 7, and AITER's block-FP8 MoE does not apply that clamp yet. |
| `--mm-encoder-*`, `--limit-mm-per-prompt` | Image input through the perception-encoder tower. |
| `step3p5` parsers | Step-5 uses Step-3.5's `<think>` and `<tool_call>` format. |
| KV cache dtype | Keep the default (BF16). Sparse layers reject other dtypes. |


</details>

### How this fits with #61727

| | #61727 (NVIDIA) | This PR (ROCm) |
|---|---|---|
| Platforms | SM90, SM103 | ROCm, validated on gfx942 |
| Sparse attention | FlashInfer + Triton | Triton |
| New custom ops | 2 `.cu` ops, CUTLASS RMSNorm | None |
| KV cache / scheduler | Reworked for cached region summaries | Side caches through the existing KV-cache manager |
| Indexer Q/W | Sharded by provider group | Sharded by provider group |
| MTP | Yes | Yes, through the Step-3.5 MTP proposer |
| `step5` parsers | Yes | Uses #61727's |

Whichever PR lands second should turn `vllm/models/step5/__init__.py` into the usual platform switch (`nvidia/` on CUDA, `amd/` on ROCm), and keep one `Step5Config` and one set of tokenizer entries.

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x MI300X (gfx942), TP8, `max-model-len 32768`, vLLM ROCm nightly `3f1bcfd82` with this branch applied.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K, full 1319, 5-shot chat (earlier revision) | 97.2%, and 97.4% with MTP |
| GSM8K, 200-question sample, MTP (final revision) | 96.0% |
| Needle in a haystack, 4k / 16k / 30k, 3 depths, 3 trials | 27/27 |
| Image input: shapes, counting, reading text | 3/3 correct |
| Prefix caching, shared ~22k-token prefix | 66% of prompt tokens from cache, answers correct |
| MTP acceptance, 3 draft tokens (earlier revision) | Mean acceptance length 3.1 to 3.3 |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, long chunked prefill + 15 concurrent decodes | No syncs |
| Prefill, 26k-token prompt | TTFT 2.7 s (3.7 to 5.0 s before K/V was written without dense attention) |
| `step3p5` parsers on Step-5 output, stream and non-stream | Pass |
| `tests/models/test_initialization.py` (Step5ForConditionalGeneration) | Pass |
| Unit tests: paged CSA kernels (6), MTP config override (2, CPU) | Pass |
| MI355X (gfx950) GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 by [@jamesETsmith](https://github.com/jamesETsmith) | 96.97% strict / 97.27% flexible; 96.59% / 97.04% with MTP |
| MI355X (gfx950) GPQA-Diamond, 198-question, zero-shot CoT by [@jamesETsmith](https://github.com/jamesETsmith) | 85.86% (170/198); 85.35% (169/198) with MTP (raw lower bounds, 16k gen budget) |
| MI355X (gfx950) NIAH single-key + multikey-2/3, 40 samples per task and context by [@jamesETsmith](https://github.com/jamesETsmith) | 100% at 32K / 128K / 256K, with and without MTP |

Big thanks to [@jamesETsmith](https://github.com/jamesETsmith) for coming up with the extensive MI355X (gfx950) validation with GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, and RULER-style needle-in-a-haystack up to 256K documented [in this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61837#issuecomment-6206831125).

About 8% of GSM8K items timed out in lm-eval's client at concurrency 64 because of long reasoning traces; they were re-asked with the same settings and scored with lm-eval's strict regex. Raw lm-eval scores were 89.2% (CSA) and 88.7% (CSA + MTP).

The 600B checkpoint does not fit in CI, so end-to-end results come from the MI300X runs. The unit tests run on any GPU runner.

## Details

- **Layout:** `vllm/models/step5/{common,amd}`. Triton kernels with explicit OCP E4M3 rounding, so gfx942 (native FP8 is E4M3FNUZ) selects the same regions as the reference.
- **Side caches:** per-token `[index_k | index_z]` rows and one summary per 8-token region, both through `MLAAttentionSpec`. Paging, prefix caching and freeing come from the KV-cache manager.
- **One custom op:** `vllm::step5_csa_attention` compresses completed regions, scores, picks the top-k and attends over the paged K/V. It is a graph splitting op, so it always sees real per-step metadata.
- **Per-batch metadata:** the index-cache metadata builder computes the token-to-request map, positions and completed-region list once per step from `CommonAttentionMetadata`.
- **K/V write:** `unified_kv_cache_update`, ordered before the CSA op through its dummy dependency.
- **Backend:** the sparse layers pin `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` on their own `Attention` layer through a Step-3.5 hook, as DeepSeek-V3.2 and OpenPangu do.
- **Indexer sharding:** Q and W are `ColumnParallelLinear` sharded by provider group; K and Z stay replicated.
- **Reuse:** small class hooks in `step3p5.py` and `step3p5_mtp.py` with unchanged defaults. No changes to the scheduler, KV-cache manager, model runner or attention backends.

**Footprint:** model code 1,373 lines (11 files), tests 244 (3), registrations 39 (8), Step-3.5 hooks +21 / -11 (2).

### Limitations

| Limitation | Follow-up |
|---|---|
| Piecewise CUDA graphs only; all numbers above used them | Graph-safe CSA metadata for full graphs |
| BF16 KV cache only on sparse layers | FP8 KV |
| `--moe-backend triton` required | Post-SiLU clamp in AITER's block-FP8 MoE |
| Top-k uses a PyTorch sort | Fused radix select |

items.title: [Model] Add LoRA support for PaddleOCR-VL
items.body:
## Purpose

Enable LoRA and multi-LoRA serving for PaddleOCR-VL
(`vllm/model_executor/models/paddleocr_vl.py`). Related to #48019.

Currently `
vllm serve PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL --enable-lora` accepts
PEFT adapters but they silently never affect inference: the model class
does not implement `SupportsLoRA`, and its `hf_to_vllm_mapper` lacks the
prefix rule for adapters trained against the native transformers class
(`PaddleOCRVLModel.language_model`). Such adapters carry keys like
`model.language_model.layers.N.*`, which the existing rule
`"model." -> "language_model.model."` rewrites to the nonexistent
`language_model.model.language_model.*`, so no module is matched and the
request is served by the base model.

Scope: text-LoRA only (the adapter targets the ERNIE-4.5 language model).
Tower/connector LoRA (`--enable-tower-connector-lora`) is out of scope;
the SigLIP vision tower receives no LoRA injection.

## Changes

1. `PaddleOCRVLForConditionalGeneration` now inherits `SupportsLoRA`.
2. Add mapper rule `"model.language_model." -> "language_model.model."`,
   placed before the generic `"model."` rule (prefix rules are applied
   sequentially; the specific rule must win).
3. Add `packed_modules_mapping` for the fused `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj`
   modules (Ernie4.5 follows the Llama layout).
4. Add `embedding_modules` (`embed_tokens` / `lm_head`).
5. Mark LoRA support in `docs/models/supported_models.md`.

## Test Plan

```
vllm serve PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL \
--enable-lora --max-loras 3 --max-lora-rank 32 \
--lora-modules adapter1=<adapter1-path> adapter2=<adapter2-path> adapter3=<adapter3-path>
```

- `/v1/models` lists base + all 3 adapters; routing via the `model` field.
- base / adapter1 / adapter2 / adapter3 requests on the same image,
  interleaved in one batch: base output byte-identical to no-LoRA
  serving; adapter outputs differ from base and match offline HF+PEFT
  inference on sampled cases.
- Server logs show non-null `lora_id` on adapter requests.

## Test Result

Environment: vLLM v0.31.0 (patched with this PR) + torch 2.13.0+cu130,
serving PaddleOCR-VL with 3 LoRA adapters (rank 32) via
`--enable-lora --max-loras 3 --max-lora-rank 32`.

1. **Adapter loading**: startup logs show `Loaded new LoRA adapter` for
   all 3 adapters; the LoRA compute kernels (`_lora_shrink_kernel`,
   `_lora_expand_kernel`) are JIT-compiled and exercised during
   inference, confirming the LoRA path is taken.
2. **Routing**: `GET /v1/models` lists the base model and all 3 adapters;
   requests are routed by the OpenAI-compatible `model` field.
3. **Base non-regression**: with the same image/prompt, the base route of
   the multi-LoRA server produces byte-identical output to a vanilla
   base-only server (no `--enable-lora`).
4. **LoRA effect**: the same image sent to base vs. each LoRA route yields
   distinct outputs — base returns raw OCR text while each adapter
   returns its task-specific structured JSON.
5. **Offline parity**: 15 images per adapter, compared field-by-field
   against offline HF+PEFT inference baselines:
   - adapter1: 15/15 identical (10 fields)
   - adapter2: 14/15 identical; the single mismatch is a one-character OCR
     ambiguity that also varies across runs of the offline baseline
     itself (unrelated to LoRA adapter loading)
   - adapter3: 15/15 identical

Note: This PR was prepared with AI assistance.

items.title: [Model] Support every Decision 3.0 size (d3-flash, d3-mini, d3-nano, d3-lite, d3-edge)

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Overview

Make every Decision 3.0 model work in vLLM: `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-nano` stopped while loading weights, and d3-flash, d3-lite, d3-mini and d3-edge had no published validation on current vLLM. Follow-up to #61565, which added Decision 3.0 and validated d3, d3-mini and d3-edge; its "Follow-ups" section promised this PR.

## Claims

- **d3-nano loads.** Its checkpoint has one `model.safetensors` and no weight index, so the default loader also read `readout.safetensors` as a backbone file and stopped with `ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'weight' in D3ForSequenceClassification`. `D3ForSequenceClassification` now names the readout's only tensor in `is_unused_checkpoint_weight`, so the backbone pass skips that file; the readout still loads as the FP32 `score` head through `secondary_weights`.
- **All five sizes give the checkpoint runtime's decisions** with `vllm serve vllm-sr/<model>` and no flags, on one AMD Instinct MI300X: 0 to 2 of 416 decisions changed per model, all near-ties (the reference's two most likely answers within 0.015 of each other), with a median probability difference of 0.003 (table below).
- **Throughput.** At 8 and 64 closed-loop clients vLLM serves 2.0x to 3.6x the requests per second of the checkpoint's own server on the mixed text / image / video load; one request at a time it is 7 % to 32 % slower (each question is its own engine request).
- The docs list all six models, the GPU test runs d3-nano next to d3-edge, and the test registry lists every size.

## Validation

**Setup**: one AMD Instinct MI300X (ROCm 7.2), a new `rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.2.3-complete` container with empty caches. vLLM is the ROCm nightly wheel `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82` (it contains #61565, and every file on the Decision 3.0 path is identical to `main`) with this PR's `d3.py` copied over the installed one; no kernels were built. The reference is the checkpoint's own runtime, `AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)`, with the versions its `requirements.txt` pins (torch 2.13.0+rocm7.1, transformers 5.17.0, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2), in its own venv on the same GPU. Checkpoints at their current `main`: `vllm-sr/d3-edge` @ cab71e6a, `vllm-sr/d3-lite` @ 9c107031, `vllm-sr/d3-nano` @ aeb70d4d, `vllm-sr/d3-mini` @ 97dd054d, `vllm-sr/d3-flash` @ 8b35c853.

**Reproducer**: in the same container, the unchanged nightly fails on d3-nano and this PR loads it:

```bash
vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-nano
# nightly 0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82:
#   ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'weight' in D3ForSequenceClassification
# with this PR: ready, and the agreement set below
```

**Answers vs the reference**: the same 416 questions as #61565 (3 states x 128 typed questions, 1-, 4- and 16-question text, a 4-question JSON state, a 40-option choice, an image with 1 and 4 questions, and a 10 s 1080p video). The decision is the top choice, `noul >= 0.5`, or a score's most likely level; |dp| is the largest absolute probability difference over a question's options.

| Model | Decisions changed | Median abs dp | p90 | Max | Image / video questions, max abs dp |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| d3-edge (0.59B) | 0 / 416 | 0.0030 | 0.0122 | 0.034 | 0.0071 |
| d3-lite (0.85B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0149) | 0.0031 | 0.0097 | 0.022 | 0.0182 |
| d3-nano (2.21B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0028) | 0.0028 | 0.0094 | 0.030 | 0.0300 |
| d3-mini (4.54B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0042) | 0.0028 | 0.0076 | 0.042 | 0.0192 |
| d3-flash (8.39B) | 2 / 416 (reference margins 0.0128, 0.0077) | 0.0027 | 0.0077 | 0.020 | 0.0104 |

**Throughput**: closed loop, 20 s per level after an 8 s warm-up, over the mix of #61565 (40 % one-question text, 20 % four-question text, 10 % four-question JSON, 10 % 40-option choice, 15 % new 1.6 MP image, 5 % new 10 s 1080p video; every image and video carries new bytes). The checkpoint server is the package's `d3_server.py` (AutoModel behind HTTP). Each cell gives req/s and p50 / p90 latency in ms:

| Model | Side | 1 client | 8 clients | 64 clients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3-edge | checkpoint server | 18.7 (12 / 89) | 36.5 (187 / 341) | 26.9 (2,108 / 2,569) |
| d3-edge | vLLM | 16.1 (17 / 85) | 72.0 (34 / 302) | 61.5 (36 / 4,233) |
| d3-lite | checkpoint server | 15.9 (25 / 102) | 24.6 (285 / 457) | 19.2 (2,863 / 3,104) |
| d3-lite | vLLM | 10.8 (36 / 107) | 59.7 (81 / 229) | 59.5 (94 / 4,213) |
| d3-nano | checkpoint server | 14.2 (26 / 125) | 20.7 (358 / 521) | 16.5 (3,192 / 3,677) |
| d3-nano | vLLM | 11.1 (32 / 113) | 52.8 (94 / 254) | 59.8 (235 / 3,699) |
| d3-mini | checkpoint server | 11.4 (33 / 147) | 16.2 (449 / 671) | 12.7 (3,953 / 4,276) |
| d3-mini | vLLM | 10.4 (32 / 135) | 37.1 (167 / 360) | 35.7 (1,585 / 2,031) |
| d3-flash | checkpoint server | 10.7 (34 / 203) | 11.2 (698 / 934) | 9.3 (5,126 / 5,480) |
| d3-flash | vLLM | 9.9 (32 / 169) | 24.6 (297 / 485) | 20.8 (2,706 / 3,130) |

**Start-up**: vLLM's launch to the first answer from empty caches, the model download included: 132 to 172 s (d3-edge 140 s, d3-lite 136 s, d3-nano 132 s, d3-mini 163 s, d3-flash 172 s).

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py` (MI300X, this PR): `[vllm-sr/d3-edge]` PASSED, `[vllm-sr/d3-nano]` PASSED (2 passed in 270 s). Without this PR, d3-nano fails at load as in the reproducer.
- `pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py tests/models/test_registry.py tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py -k "decision_config or joint_head or D3 or d3 or strategy_selection"` (MI300X, this PR): 13 passed.
- CPU check of `DefaultModelLoader.get_all_weights` on a d3-nano-like layout (`model.safetensors` with backbone tensors plus `readout.safetensors`, no index): on main the backbone pass yields the readout's root `weight`; with this PR it yields only the backbone tensors, and `score.weight` still comes from `secondary_weights`.
- vLLM CI on NVIDIA, Buildkite #95083 (H200, MIG 18 GB, the multimodal pooling step): `test_d3.py` `[vllm-sr/d3-edge]` and `[vllm-sr/d3-nano]` PASSED; the d3-nano run logs `Skipped 1/2 safetensors shard(s) holding no weights the model loads`.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass (actionlint skipped locally; no workflow files changed).

## Details

- **Root cause**: without `model.safetensors.index.json`, `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` keeps every `*.safetensors` file of the repo (`filter_duplicate_safetensors_files` returns them all when the index is missing), so `readout.safetensors` ({`weight`: [255, hidden]}) joins the backbone pass. Its root key `weight` matches no module, and `AutoWeightsLoader` raises. The other five checkpoints ship an index that lists only the backbone shards, so the index filter already drops the readout there. d3-nano is the only Decision 3.0 repo without an index.
- **Fix**: `is_unused_checkpoint_weight` is the existing hook the default loader passes to `filter_safetensors_files_by_weight_name` for the primary weights only; it drops a safetensors file when every tensor in it is unused. The readout file holds a single tensor named `weight`, which no backbone checkpoint has at the root. Its own `secondary_weights` source sets no such rule and keeps loading it under the `score.` prefix. For indexed checkpoints nothing changes beyond reading the shard headers, which the loader already does for pooling models (their protocol default returns False).
- **Alternatives considered**: `allow_patterns_overrides=["model*.safetensors"]` would also skip the index filter and depend on file names; adding an index to the Hub repo fixes only that copy of the checkpoint.
- **CI**: `test_d3.py` runs in the optional "Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling)" step; d3-nano adds a 4.5 GB checkpoint there. d3-lite, d3-mini and d3-flash take the same code path as d3-edge and d3-nano and are covered by the measurements above rather than CI, to keep the step's downloads and run time small.
- **Not measured**: agreement and throughput on NVIDIA GPUs (only the CI test above ran there; no NVIDIA GPU was available to me), tensor parallelism, LoRA.
- **Not a duplicate**: no open or closed PR or issue covers d3-nano or the other sizes (searched for Decision 3.0, `vllm-sr/d3`, d3-nano, `D3ForSequenceClassification`, `decision_config`); #61565 is merged.
- **AI assistance** was used for the code, tests, measurements and this description.

---

labels.name: ready

items.body:
## Overview

Adds native serving for Nemotron Parse 3.5's causal visual-prefix architecture and a one-token auxiliary MTP proposer. This extends the Parse model implementation; related earlier-model speculative work is [#51168](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51168).

## Claims

- Register RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM and process variable-resolution packed RADIO images with content-normalized positional embeddings and visual-prefix placeholder expansion.
- Add ParseAuxMTPModel, loading the checkpoint's integrated auxiliary projections and routing causal-prefix configurations to one speculative token on Model Runner V2.
- Extend HF/vLLM generation coverage to Parse 3.5 and add five MTP configuration/loading/sharing contract tests to Basic Models CI. End-to-end MTP correctness and speedup remain unvalidated.
- Older generations of Nemotron-Parse are still supported.

## Validation

Tests ran locally. The nemotron-3.5-parse (with and without mtp) and nemotron-parse-2.0 accuracy verified on internal benchmarks. Parse 3.5 mtp acceptance rate is verified at various concurrencies. Tested on A100, H100. 

## Details

New nemotron-3.5-parse model uses an updated architecture which the current vllm implementation does not support. To simplify the change, created a new nemotron_parse3_5.py implementation while leaving code for previous versions unchanged. Major differences compared to previous implementation and approaches taken for implementations: 
1. New model uses visual prefix and removes cross-attention. 
add_cross_attention field controls whether to add cross-attention in decoder layer. Parse 3.5 implementation in vllm only supports checkpoints that has it set to False (as official checkpoint). Added a hard fail check that nemotron-3.5-parse models have it set to False. 
2. New model uses GQA vs old model using MHA.
Since WhisperAttention does not support GQA, created a local attention implementation that copies Whisper but adds GQA support. Can instead add GQA support to Whisper, but this increases common-code change. 
3. New model uses dynamic-size vision encoder with packed batching (NaVit-style) vs old model using static resolution. 
New RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM and pre-processing. Parse 3.5 is not using device-side preprocessing for parse 3.5 for simplicity (d1d8e6c). 
4. New model uses a different version of RADIO encoder.
Added RADIOv4-SO400M parameters to RADIO file. Model: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/C-RADIOv4-SO400M

## Known limitations and future work

1. Only V2 runner is supported for mtp-enabled parse 3.5. V1 runner fails because it expects kv-cache in the speculator and parse mtp does not have attention. 
2. RADIO dynamic packing causes a sync on . This code is reused between models, so leaving it as-is for this PR. The torch.tensor constructor should be replaced with async copy in the future. Will submit separate PR. 
3. Nemotron-3.5-Parse is currently not public, so the 3.5-specific tests are disabled. Those tests and additional validation for parse 3.5 was ran locally.

items.title: [XPU] Add Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model architecture support
items.body:
# [XPU] Add Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model architecture support

  Adds the `xpu/` sibling to the existing `amd/` and `nvidia/` implementations under
  `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/`, routed through the existing platform dispatch. It reuses
  `Qwen3NextAttention`, `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` and `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`, so
  it is much smaller than the other two backends.

  **Changes outside the model package**

  - `speculator.py` / `llm_base_proposer.py` - the MTP hidden buffer was widened via
    `hc_mult` (the DeepSeek-V4 spelling). Qwen4Exp calls it `hc_count`, so the `getattr`
    fell back to 1 and the MTP head got an un-widened buffer. Both names now accepted.
  - `inc_wna16_linear.py` - guard the `qzeros` copy, which can be empty or mismatched
    under symmetric group quantization and crashed weight load on the 512 routed experts.

  **`layer_types`** - Transformers v5.18 renames `full_attention` to `indexed_attention`;
  all three spellings map to the dense GQA block here. This does not branch on
  `indexer_n_heads` like `amd/`/`nvidia/` do: on `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16` that field is
  set (`4`) but the checkpoint ships no indexer tensors, so keying off it would pick a QSA
  path the weights cannot feed.

  **Known limitations** - no QSA/indexer path on XPU (such checkpoints fail at weight load
  rather than silently running dense attention); TP=4 needs `--enable-expert-parallel`
  (`moe_intermediate_size=640 / 4 = 160` is not divisible by `group_size=128` - checkpoint
  arithmetic, not an XPU limit); requires `transformers >= 5.16.1`, same as the other
  backends; TP=4 validated with `--enforce-eager` only.
  
**model** - https://huggingface.co/devan-carlin/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16

## Overview

Add precomputed image embedding support to LightOnOCR so callers can reuse projected visual features and skip the vision encoder.

## Claims

- Support a 3D tensor or per-image 2D tensors with different feature lengths.
- Support embedding-only inference with the image limit set to zero.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_lightonocr.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py \
  tests/utils_/test_tensor_schema.py -v
```

- Processor and tensor-schema regressions: 51 passed, 8 GPU-specific skips. Pre-commit passed.
- Local `LightOnOCR-2-1B` validation (BF16, TP=1) passed in eager, default graph and encoder-free modes, including strict sync checking for embedding-only inference. Single- and multi-image embedding outputs match pixel baselines in token IDs and sampled-token logprobs. Chat Completions comparisons and Hugging Face reference checks also passed.

## Details

Use embedding feature counts for placeholders. Override LightOnOCR image input parsing to reuse the inherited embedding processing path, with an explicit input schema supporting variable feature lengths. Pixel inputs reuse existing parsing and token-counting logic.

Duplicate checks found no overlap with [#48316](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48316) (model identifiers) or [#58122](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58122) (encoder graphs).
