items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Support heterogeneous P/D TP for mixed MLA models
items.body:
## Overview Fixes the NIXL KV-transfer crash when a P/D disaggregated deployment uses **heterogeneous TP** (e.g. prefill TP16 + decode TP8) with a **mixed MLA** model — a model that combines a replicated MLA latent cache with head-sharded attention regions (GLM-5.3 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, i.e. MLA + DSA sparse-attention indexer). Extends the per-region classification introduced in #44583 to heterogeneous-TP page geometry. ## Claims - Heterogeneous P/D TP works for mixed MLA models: prefill TP16 + decode TP8 and prefill TP8 + decode TP16 both complete full benchmarks with correct output quality. - Pure-MLA (DeepSeek-class), pure-GQA, and symmetric-TP deployments keep their existing behavior — every change is gated on conditions only hybrid + mixed-TP produce. - Measured on GLM-5.3 785B fp8 (8xH200): `1P×TP16 + 2D×TP8` = 0.81 req/s vs 0.48 req/s for the best symmetric split (**+68%**) — prefill is compute-bound (wider TP wins) while decode is latency-bound (smaller TP group wins); heterogeneous TP lets each role sit at its optimum. ## Validation Live on an 8xH200 cluster, GLM-5.3 785B fp8, full request-load benchmarks per config: - D>P (prefill TP8 + decode TP16): EPP registration 3s, full benchmark, quality ok - D

Failure signature (before the fix) ``` ValueError: Replicated region i=99 local_len=8192 remote_len=16384 (NIXL handshake validation, decode engine, first request) ``` followed, after each layer was fixed in sequence, by descriptor-size mismatches and finally a multi-source read assertion in `pull_worker`. Performance evidence and the full 11-iteration investigation: internal benchmarking on ServeIt Studio (GLM-5.3 asymmetric TP analysis).

items.title: [Model] Support Decision 3.0 decision models (vllm-sr/d3)

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Overview

Serve the Decision 3.0 decision models ([`vllm-sr/d3`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3) and its smaller variants such as `vllm-sr/d3-mini` and `vllm-sr/d3-edge`) from their Hub checkpoints as they are: `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3`, then ask typed questions on `/v1/systemone`. Today these checkpoints do not load in vLLM (`Qwen3_5Model` is not a registered architecture and the readout is a separate file). This builds on vLLM's Qwen3.5 implementation, the structured decisions API (#60465 and its predecessors) and the Clef-Flash detection pattern (#61308).

## Claims

- **The published checkpoints load unchanged** (measured here: d3, d3-mini and d3-edge; see Follow-ups). A bare `Qwen3_5Model` checkpoint that ships a `decision_config.json` is detected and served as `D3ForSequenceClassification`. The 255-row answer-code readout (`readout.safetensors`) becomes the FP32 `score` head. The declared `noncausal_full_attention` makes the full attention layers bidirectional, while the Gated DeltaNet layers stay causal. Tied embeddings need nothing, and per-model `layer_types` are honoured (d3-edge: `llFllFllFFFF`).
- **`/v1/systemone` gives the checkpoint runtime's answers.** For each question, `D3Strategy` writes the prompt the checkpoint's own `d3_format.py` writes (byte-identical on 416 prompts), reads the question's codes from the classify head, and applies the option mask and the checkpoint temperature. It supports choice (up to 255 options), yes / no and score questions, text and JSON states, and images and videos read with the runtime's budgets (1.6 MP images; 2 fps, at most 32 frames of 0.2 MP).
- **Same decisions as the reference runtime on AMD Instinct MI325X.** Against `AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)`: 0 of 416 decisions changed on d3, 1 on d3-mini and 2 on d3-edge, all ties or near-ties. The median probability difference is 0.0024 to 0.0029.
- **Throughput.** On a mixed text / JSON / image / video load at 8 and 64 closed-loop clients, vLLM sustains 1.4x to 2.6x the rate of the checkpoint's own server (AutoModel behind HTTP, one request at a time).

## Validation

Hardware and software: one AMD Instinct MI325X per side. vLLM used the official ROCm nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8f7116b2b4877f66516f4128176cf722a` (PyTorch 2.13, ROCm 7.2), with this branch's Python tree (main `f4b8d43a6` plus this PR) overlaid; no kernels were built. The reference used the same image with the versions the checkpoint pins (transformers 5.17.0, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2). vLLM ran with no flags: `vllm serve vllm-sr/<model>`. Models: `vllm-sr/d3` @ fc2d74bd, `vllm-sr/d3-mini` @ 6d8971f4, `vllm-sr/d3-edge` @ fe71f8e1.

**Answers vs the reference** (`model.system_one(...)` in process): 416 questions per model, namely 3 states (a support ticket, release notes, a JSON account) x 128 typed questions (48 choice, 40 yes / no, 40 score), plus 1-, 4- and 16-question text, a 4-question JSON state, a 40-option choice, an image with 1 and 4 questions, and a 10 s 1080p video. The decision is the top choice, `noul >= 0.5`, or a score's most likely level; |dp| is the largest absolute probability difference over a question's options.

| Model | Decisions changed | Median abs dp | p90 | Max | Image / video questions, max abs dp |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| d3 (27B) | 0 / 416 | 0.0024 | 0.0078 | 0.027 | 0.0049 / 0.021 |
| d3-mini (4B) | 1 / 416 (0.5003 vs 0.4996) | 0.0026 | 0.0078 | 0.032 | 0.018 / 0.032 |
| d3-edge (0.6B) | 2 / 416 (margins 0.0019, 0.0012) | 0.0029 | 0.012 | 0.043 | 0.0050 / 0.0055 |

For scale, two vLLM configurations of d3 (defaults vs `--max-model-len 32768`, so different batch shapes) differ from each other by up to 0.011 and change 2 decisions.

**Throughput and latency**: closed loop, 30 s per level after an 8 s warm-up, over a mix of 40 % one-question text, 20 % four-question text, 10 % four-question JSON state, 10 % 40-option choice, 15 % new 1.6 MP image and 5 % new 10 s 1080p video. Every image and video carries new bytes. Each cell gives req/s and p50 / p90 latency in ms:

| Model | Side | 1 client | 8 clients | 64 clients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | checkpoint server | 6.9 (69 / 290) | 6.1 (1,210 / 1,653) | 4.6 (9,300 / 9,817) |
| d3 | vLLM | 6.7 (74 / 265) | 8.6 (903 / 1,228) | 8.5 (5,907 / 6,552) |
| d3-mini | checkpoint server | 17.0 (23 / 123) | 23.3 (339 / 499) | 18.3 (3,157 / 3,427) |
| d3-mini | vLLM | 15.8 (30 / 103) | 43.0 (166 / 273) | 45.0 (1,357 / 1,606) |
| d3-edge | checkpoint server | 31.6 (7.4 / 66) | 47.3 (141 / 306) | 41.7 (1,463 / 1,724) |
| d3-edge | vLLM | 28.6 (10 / 56) | 102 (23 / 211) | 110 (36 / 2,679) |

One request at a time (p50 ms, AutoModel in process / vLLM):

| Model | 1 text question | 16 text questions | new image, 1 question | new image, 4 questions | new 10 s video |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | 55.9 / 54.9 | 583 / 547 | 293 / 216 | 1,020 / 700 | 519 / 443 |
| d3-mini | 18.1 / 19.4 | 114 / 116 | 111 / 64 | 341 / 158 | 319 / 261 |
| d3-edge | 6.4 / 7.0 | 21.2 / 29.0 | 56 / 33 | 140 / 48 | 266 / 234 |

**Start-up and memory** (launch to the first answer; cold = empty compile caches, model files on local disk):

| Model | AutoModel cold / warm | vLLM cold / warm | GPU memory above idle, steady: AutoModel / vLLM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | 39.9 / 22.0 s | 214.5 / 130.0 s (`--max-model-len 32768`: 139.0 / 67.8 s, same throughput) | 52 / 199 GiB |
| d3-mini | 28.6 / 10.5 s | 136.2 / 61.7 s | 11 / 216 GiB |
| d3-edge | 27.0 / 8.2 s | 129.2 / 37.1 s | 3.5 / 227 GiB |

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py`: d3-edge vs the checkpoint runtime, with text prompts as token ids (including a 40-option choice) and one image prompt processed by vLLM. PASSED on MI325X (134 s).
- `pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k "decision_config or joint_head"`: 8 passed.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/`: 115 passed, including the new d3 strategy tests.
- `pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/test_initialization.py -k D3`: 2 passed.
- `pre-commit run` on the diff: all hooks pass. actionlint was skipped locally because no workflow files changed.

## Details

- **Detection** follows Clef-Flash: `Qwen3_5ModelArchConfigConvertor` maps `architectures: ["Qwen3_5Model"]` plus `decision_config.json` to `D3ForSequenceClassification` and keeps the decision config on `hf_config`. Bare `Qwen3_5Model` checkpoints without that file are unaffected (they stay unsupported, as today).
- **Config hook** `D3ForSequenceClassificationConfig` validates `format_version` 1, `pooling: last` and the attention mode. It sets `is_causal=False` for `noncausal_full_attention`, so chunked prefill and prefix caching turn off by themselves, sets `id2label` to the 255 codes, and makes the classify head return raw code logits by default. Probabilities only exist over a question's own options, so `/classify` and `/pooling` callers mask and normalize themselves.
- **Model** (`d3.py`): `as_seq_cls_model(Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration)`, so no LM head is allocated and the `score` head is FP32. It adds a mapper for the bare-backbone keys, `readout.safetensors` as `score.weight` via `secondary_weights`, and a processing info that applies the runtime's media budgets. The checkpoint's processor config allows 16.7 MP images, while the runtime reads at most 1.6 MP; video frames use transformers' `cap_pixels_per_frame` with the runtime's 200,704-pixel cap.
- **Strategy**: one classify read per question. The media come first, so they are processed once per request and shared by its questions, and the encoder cache deduplicates the vision tower. Videos go through the existing `qwen3_vl` loader, whose sampling rule already matches the runtime's, with `max_frames=32`. A small change to the question builder, `DecisionLimits.labeled`, lets label-free strategies accept more options than the A to Z label set; the defaults of other strategies are unchanged.
- **Why not an example client**: the System One API already has question types on main, so the option mask and temperature belong in the strategy rather than in client code.
- **Tradeoffs and limits**
  - Start-up: with chunked prefill off, the profiling pass runs one `max_model_len`-token sequence. At the config's 262,144 tokens this dominates start-up (71 s of d3's 130 s warm start). `--max-model-len 32768` halves it, with no throughput change on this mix.
  - Memory: vLLM reserves `--gpu-memory-utilization` (0.92) of HBM. The Gated DeltaNet layers still keep per-request state, and the attention layers keep no KV.
  - Media under load: at 64 clients, text stays fast (d3-edge text p90 about 80 ms) while image and video requests queue (image p50 2.65 s), because decoding a new 300-frame 1080p video per request is CPU-bound. `--renderer-num-workers 4` did not change this.
  - Small-model latency: one request at a time, multi-question requests on the small models are slower than in process (d3-edge, 16 questions: 29.0 vs 21.2 ms), since each question is its own engine request.
  - API differences from the runtime: a request with an invalid or too-long question returns 400 instead of per-question errors; at most 64 questions per request (the API's limit); `confidence` and `usage` follow `/v1/systemone`'s definitions; option descriptions, instructions and score levels are rendered as text (non-string values go through `str`, where the runtime writes JSON); the runtime's optional `permutation_average` is not available.
  - Not measured: d3-flash, d3-nano and d3-lite (same layout and code path), CUDA GPUs, tensor parallelism, LoRA.
- **Not a duplicate**: no open or closed PR or issue covers these checkpoints, `decision_config.json` readout checkpoints, or bare `Qwen3_5Model` loading (searched for d3, Decision 3.0, `Qwen3_5Model`, `decision_config.json`, decider, readout). The Laya PR (#58429) adds an unrelated ModernBERT-based model.
- **AI assistance** was used for the code, tests, measurements and this description. The PR stays a draft until the submitter has reviewed every line.

## Follow-ups

- **The other five Decision 3.0 models** (`vllm-sr/d3-flash`, `vllm-sr/d3-mini`, `vllm-sr/d3-nano`, `vllm-sr/d3-lite`, `vllm-sr/d3-edge`) share d3's architecture and take the same code path: each Hub checkpoint is a bare `Qwen3_5Model` with a `d3-code-readout-v1` `decision_config.json` (`noncausal_full_attention`, 255 codes) and a `readout.safetensors`. The variations between them, tied embeddings and d3-edge's layer layout, are exercised by d3-mini and d3-edge.
- **d3-mini and d3-edge** already match the reference in this PR's measurements (1 and 2 of 416 decisions changed, all ties or near-ties; see the agreement and throughput tables under Validation).
- **A follow-up PR** will validate d3-flash, d3-nano and d3-lite, publish agreement and throughput for all five, and add them explicitly to the docs examples and tests where it makes sense.

items.title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Support heterogeneous-vocab draft models (TLI)
items.body:
## Overview

Draft models with a different vocabulary than the target, `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` from #38174, now run on Model Runner V2. Since #59541 they fall back to V1. This is the TLI item listed as TBD in #47172.

## Claims

- `method="draft_model"` with `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` runs on V2, and the V1 fallback is removed.
- On both directions of vocab mismatch, acceptance length on V2 matches V1 and GSM8K accuracy stays within noise of the target alone.
- V2 throughput with TLI is the same as or slightly above V1.

## Validation

Tests I ran on main at 624a5dd with this change. The GPU tests ran on 1x L4.

```bash
pytest tests/test_config.py -k v2_model_runner -q
# 32 passed
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_vocab_mapping.py -q
# 17 passed
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_draft_model.py -k heterogeneous_vocab -v -s
# Using V2 Model Runner
# acceptance_len=1.920
# exact text matches=96/100 (required=61)
# 1 passed
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_draft_model.py -k "correctness or realistic" -v
# 5 passed
```

Without the change, the new e2e test fails with `Model Runner V2 does not yet support: heterogeneous-vocabulary draft models`.

GSM8K, 500 questions, greedy, k=3, all prompts submitted at once, 1x L4. AL is the mean acceptance length from the spec decode metrics. Throughput is output tokens per second over the whole batch.

| Target | Draft | Runner | GSM8K | AL | tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | none | V1 | 0.532 | | 3666 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | none | V2 | 0.532 | | 3724 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | SmolLM2-360M-Instruct | V1 | 0.542 | 2.11 | 1771 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | SmolLM2-360M-Instruct | V2 | 0.524 | 2.11 | 1832 |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | none | V1 | 0.458 | | 1859 |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | none | V2 | 0.458 | | 1816 |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | V1 | 0.448 | 3.13 | 2281 |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | V2 | 0.454 | 3.12 | 2311 |

The first pair has a target vocab larger than the draft's (151,936 vs 49,152), and the second pair is the reverse. These are the two pairs from #59541. The SmolLM2 target ends right away on raw few-shot prompts, so its rows use chat prompts. The standard error at 500 questions is about 2 points. With the 1.5B target at this batch size the draft is extra work, so throughput with drafting is lower than the target alone. That is the same on V1.

<details>
<summary>Greedy outputs vs the target alone</summary>

Greedy outputs with drafting do not match the target alone token for token on either runner, for any draft. Verify computes k+1 rows at once and plain decode computes one, so near-tied logits can flip, see #54506. To check that TLI adds nothing on top of that, the table compares each run with the target alone on the same runner, next to a same-vocab draft as a control, and looks at the first diverging token of every mismatch.

| Target | Draft | Runner | Same as target | First divergence at a top-2 tie or one bf16 step apart |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | SmolLM2-360M-Instruct | V2 | 247/500 | 85% |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | V2 | 242/500 | 80% |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | V2 | 289/500 | 95% |
| SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct | SmolLM2-360M-Instruct | V2 | 296/500 | 96% |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
# Run once with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 and once with =1, from the repo root.
from vllm import LLM
from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import evaluate_gsm8k_offline
from tests.v1.e2e.spec_decode.utils import compute_acceptance_len

llm = LLM(
    "Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct",
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=0,
    disable_log_stats=False,
    speculative_config={
        "method": "draft_model",
        "model": "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
        "use_heterogeneous_vocab": True,
    },
)
print(evaluate_gsm8k_offline(llm, num_questions=500))
print(compute_acceptance_len(llm.get_metrics()))
```

For the SmolLM2 target, pass `use_chat_completions=True` to `evaluate_gsm8k_offline`.

</details>

## Details

The change keeps the draft vocab inside `StandaloneARSpeculator`. Ids cross between vocabularies at two points only:

1. Target ids become draft ids once per step, in the expanded step-0 input buffer. This is done in place so the draft CUDA graph work in #60989 can keep reading that buffer. The dummy-run path reads the target's own input buffer, so it maps into a new tensor instead.
2. `propose()` maps the drafted ids to target ids, into a preallocated buffer, right before returning them.

`compute_draft_logits` masks logits outside the shared vocab, so the drafter only proposes tokens the target also has. Between draft steps the drafter keeps its own ids. V1 maps back and forth every step, but ids in the shared vocab map one to one, so the drafter sees the same inputs on both runners.

Tokenizers are loaded with each model's own path, mode and revision. The draft config inherits the target's tokenizer mode and revision, which #54780 fixes on the V1 side.

`use_local_argmax_reduction` bypasses `compute_draft_logits`, so the mask would be skipped. #51564 already rejects that combination in the config, so it is not repeated here.

Not in this PR: CUDA graphs for the standalone drafter, which #60989 is adding, and probabilistic drafting with a heterogeneous vocab, which needs the draft distribution mapped into the target vocab and is also unsupported on V1.

Duplicate check: #47172 and the open PRs for TLI and heterogeneous vocab on V2. #54780, #51564 and #59012 fix V1 or `VocabMapping`, and #61152 fixes probabilistic rejection sampling for narrower draft vocabularies. None of them ports TLI to V2.

This PR was written with AI assistance from Claude Code. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.

items.title: [Model][DSV4.1] Support MXFP4-packed Engram embedding tables
items.body:
## Overview

Support DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints whose Engram embedding table is stored as MXFP4 (E2M1 nibbles packed two per byte, UE8M0 block-32 scales) instead of FP8. FP8 behavior is unchanged.

## Claims

- A checkpoint with `quantization_config["engram_embed_quant"] = "mxfp4"` now loads: the table is allocated as `[rows, dim // 2]` uint8 and decoded in the lookup kernel.
- The packed table halves the host memory: 12.16 GiB per rank vs 23.60 GiB for FP8 (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP=4).
- GSM8K accuracy of the packed checkpoint matches the FP8 baseline (0.967 vs 0.966), including with `dp_shared_memory`.
- An unknown `engram_embed_quant` value raises instead of being ignored.

## Validation

### End to end (GB300)

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, one GB300 node per run, on `vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev360+g44f0ddfd7` (this PR's base). Compiled ops come from the precompiled wheel for that commit, with this PR's Python overlaid. GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, chat endpoint, `--max-tokens 4096`.

| Run | Engram table | Parallelism | GSM8K acc. | Invalid | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 baseline | 23.60 GiB per rank (host-pinned) | TP=4 | 0.966 | 0.004 | 1275 |
| MXFP4-packed | 12.16 GiB per rank (host-pinned) | TP=4 | 0.967 | 0.005 | 1218 |
| MXFP4-packed, `dp_shared_memory` | 48.64 GiB shared across 4 DP replicas | DP=4, TP=1, EP | 0.967 | 0.003 | 1299 |

- One run per row. A 0.001 accuracy gap is within noise (about ±0.5 points standard error). tok/s is not a clean comparison (single runs, different parallel layouts).
- DP-shared packed storage (`DPSharedEngramStorage`) loads and serves correctly.
- The FP8 baseline is `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-nvfp4-experts-blend`. I did not check that its expert quantization matches the packed checkpoint's, so the accuracy comparison is not isolated to the Engram table.
- Not covered: long-context and other benchmarks, DP=4 with FP8.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
# Packed, TP=4
vllm serve <packed-ckpt> --served-model-name m --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32

# Packed, DP-shared host table
vllm serve <packed-ckpt> --served-model-name m --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --engram-config '{"dp_shared_memory": true}' \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --language-model-only --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32

# Eval, against each server
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
  --max-tokens 4096 --save-results gsm8k.json
```

The checkpoint needs `quantization_config["engram_embed_quant"] = "mxfp4"`.
</details>

### Unit and kernel tests

Run on 4xGB300 before the test trim in 1800929afd (which removed the `EngramBatch` skip test and the FP8/THP allocation matrix); not yet re-run after it:

- `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`: 127 passed, 2 skipped (THP without offload).
- `tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py`: 27 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

### Lookup microbenchmark

24 columns, us per lookup (FP8 / packed): host-pinned 8192 tokens 356 / 365; GPU-resident 8192 tokens 115 / 156 (the nibble decode); no extra peak GPU memory.

## Details

- `ParallelEngramEmbedding` takes `packed_fp4`; the row size is `dim // 2` bytes when packed. `DPSharedEngramStorage` and the offload memory log count the packed row size.
- `_engram_lookup_kernel` gets a `PACKED_FP4` constexpr (even column in the low nibble); the block scales are unchanged.
- `EngramBatch.create` returns `None` for packed tables, because the staged exchange carries FP8 rows only.
- `Engram._create_embedding` reads the format from the HF config (default `"fp8"`).
- Limitations:
  - GPU-resident lookup is about 36% slower for packed tables (nibble decode). The deployed host-pinned mode is within 1-3%.
  - `can_share_engram_tables` still sizes `/dev/shm` from the FP8 row size, so it over-estimates by about 2x for packed tables. This is conservative, and I left it out to keep the diff small.
- Existing tests that build layers through `__new__` need a `model_config` stub, which this PR adds.
- Not a duplicate: #58782 (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 hybrid FP8/MXFP4 quant routing, AMD) changes quant config and weights mapping, not the Engram table path. #60938 also edits `engram.py` and `test_engram.py` (Engram to mHC fusion prototype), so it may conflict textually.

items.title: [Model] Enable LoRA support for tower and connector in MiDashengLM
items.body:
## Overview

Enable LoRA on the Dasheng audio tower and `AudioProjectorSubsample` connector of MiDashengLM, built on the `get_mm_lora_token_counts` interface from #42662. Part of #31479; sibling audio-model PRs: #45697 (Voxtral), #45944 (Qwen2-Audio).

## Claims

- `MiDashengLMModel` now declares `SupportsLoRA` and `supports_tower_connector_lora`, with `get_mm_mapping` (`decoder` / `audio_encoder` / `audio_projector`). Adapters can target the Qwen2 decoder, the Dasheng tower (`qkv`, `proj`, `fc1`, `fc2`), and the projector (`net.0`, `net.2`); no encoder rewrite was needed since the tower already uses vLLM-native linears and the HF checkpoint's fused `qkv` maps to `QKVParallelLinearWithLoRA` without packing.
- With `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, every audio item is padded to a fixed 160000 samples, so the tower always runs 250 patches and the projector 50 rows per item for the 7B config, making the tower/connector punica token mappings exact under encoder batching.
- Covered by a processor-driven unit test (real `mispeech/midashenglm-7b` processor, awkward audio lengths whose patch counts are not multiples of the projector's subsample factor), plus end-to-end GPU validation with a tower+connector adapter on a variable-length multi-audio batch.

## Validation

On an A100 80GB (nightly `vllm==0.31.1rc1.dev376+g5555a2d8f.cu129`, torch 2.13.0+cu129, torchaudio 2.11.0+cu129, transformers 5.19.0, Python 3.12.3; the changed model file overlaid onto site-packages, tests tree shipped alongside):

**Unit test** (real `mispeech/midashenglm-7b` processor, no model weights):

```
tests/models/multimodal/test_midashenglm.py::test_mm_lora_token_counts_match_padded_tower_input[mispeech/midashenglm-7b] PASSED [100%]
======================= 1 passed, 14 warnings in 18.28s ========================
```

**End-to-end smoke** — randomly-initialized small-magnitude PEFT adapter targeting `qkv`/`fc1`/`fc2` (tower blocks 0/15/31), `net.0`/`net.2` (connector), and `q/k/v_proj` (decoder layer 0); batch of 3 prompts mixing audio lengths 0.37s / 3.3s+7.77s (two audios in one prompt) / 10.0s (patch counts 9, 82, 194, 250 — three of them not multiples of 5), `enforce_eager`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.199` (16.7 GiB free on a shared box):

```
(EngineCore) WARNING [model_manager.py:273] LoRA for the tower and connector of multimodal models is experimental and may contain bugs. ...
=== generate WITH tower/connector LoRA ===
[lora 0..2] completed, 16 tokens each
=== generate WITHOUT LoRA (same engine, padded path) ===
[base 0..2] completed, identical ids to the LoRA pass (greedy argmax unchanged by the small random adapter)
=== SMOKE TEST PASSED ===
```

The adapter loads with every target wrapped (no `unexpected modules` error, no unwrapped-module or `does not support` warnings in the full log), and prefill through the LoRA-mapped tower/connector plus 16 decode steps complete without any punica shape/mapping assertion across the variable-length multi-audio batch — the property this PR is responsible for.

**Caveat (pre-existing, unrelated to this PR):** base MiDashengLM on current main emits only the untrained token id 151872 (text-only prompts included, top-1 logprob 0.0 vs −619 for rank 2). Verified pre-existing by rerunning with the pristine nightly `midashenglm.py` (same output), with no LoRA flags at all (byte-identical output, which also confirms the pad path changes nothing for non-LoRA use), and with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` in the same environment (correct output, ruling out the env). Tracked in #61469; adapter-quality validation on this model is blocked on that fix, mapping/plumbing validation above is not.

<details>
<summary>Smoke-test script</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Functional smoke-test for MiDashengLM tower/connector LoRA (A100).

Validates the plumbing the PR touches, not adapter quality: with
`enable_tower_connector_lora` every audio is padded to 160000 samples, so the
tower/connector punica mappings built from `get_mm_lora_token_counts` must
match the rows the Dasheng/projector linears actually receive. A
randomly-initialized small-magnitude adapter targeting tower (qkv/fc1/fc2),
connector (net.0/net.2), and LM (q/k/v_proj) modules is enough: if the counts
or the wrapping were wrong, generation would throw a punica shape/mapping
error or the adapter load would report unexpected modules.

The batch mixes audio lengths whose patch counts are not multiples of the
projector's subsample factor (9, 82, 194 patches) with a full-length audio
(250 patches) across single- and multi-audio prompts.
"""

import faulthandler
import json

faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(2400, exit=True)

import numpy as np
import torch
from safetensors.torch import save_file

import vllm
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

MODEL = "mispeech/midashenglm-7b"
SR = 16000
ADAPTER_DIR = "/tmp/mdsl_lora_val/rand_adapter"

# (in_features, out_features) per targeted module, from the 7B config:
# tower embed_dim=1280, mlp_ratio=4, subsample_factor=5, text hidden 3584,
# 28 heads / 4 kv heads, head_dim 128.
_TOWER_BLOCKS = [0, 15, 31]
_SHAPES: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {
    "audio_projector.net.0": (6400, 3584),
    "audio_projector.net.2": (3584, 3584),
    "decoder.model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj": (3584, 3584),
    "decoder.model.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj": (3584, 512),
    "decoder.model.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj": (3584, 512),
}
for _i in _TOWER_BLOCKS:
    _SHAPES[f"audio_encoder.blocks.{_i}.attn.qkv"] = (1280, 3840)
    _SHAPES[f"audio_encoder.blocks.{_i}.mlp.fc1"] = (1280, 5120)
    _SHAPES[f"audio_encoder.blocks.{_i}.mlp.fc2"] = (5120, 1280)


def make_random_lora(out_dir: str) -> str:
    """Write a PEFT-format adapter with small random A/B matrices directly
    (no HF model load needed on the shared box)."""
    import os

    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    rank = 8
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    tensors = {}
    for name, (fan_in, fan_out) in _SHAPES.items():
        tensors[f"base_model.model.{name}.lora_A.weight"] = torch.from_numpy(
            (rng.standard_normal((rank, fan_in)) * 0.01).astype(np.float16)
        )
        tensors[f"base_model.model.{name}.lora_B.weight"] = torch.from_numpy(
            (rng.standard_normal((fan_out, rank)) * 0.01).astype(np.float16)
        )
    save_file(tensors, f"{out_dir}/adapter_model.safetensors")
    config = {
        "peft_type": "LORA",
        "base_model_name_or_path": MODEL,
        "r": rank,
        "lora_alpha": 16,
        "lora_dropout": 0.0,
        "bias": "none",
        "task_type": "CAUSAL_LM",
        "target_modules": [
            "qkv", "fc1", "fc2", "net.0", "net.2",
            "q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj",
        ],
    }
    with open(f"{out_dir}/adapter_config.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(config, f, indent=2)
    return out_dir


def _audio(seconds: float, rng: np.random.RandomState):
    return ((rng.rand(int(seconds * SR)).astype(np.float32) - 0.5) * 0.1, SR)


def main() -> None:
    lora_path = make_random_lora(ADAPTER_DIR)

    free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
    free_gib = free / 1024**3
    print(f"GPU free: {free_gib:.1f} GiB / total {total / 1024**3:.1f} GiB")
    if free_gib < 15.0:
        raise SystemExit(f"ABORT: only {free_gib:.1f} GiB free (<15 GiB)")
    # Leave ~1 GiB headroom for the resident prod workload. The fp32
    # checkpoint runs as bf16 (~15.4 GiB weights), so this is tight on a
    # busy box; keep batching budgets small.
    gpu_util = round((free - 1.0 * 1024**3) / total, 3)
    print(f"gpu_memory_utilization={gpu_util}")

    llm = vllm.LLM(
        model=MODEL,
        dtype="bfloat16",
        trust_remote_code=True,
        enable_lora=True,
        max_loras=1,
        max_lora_rank=8,
        enable_tower_connector_lora=True,
        mm_processor_cache_gb=0,
        max_model_len=2048,
        max_num_batched_tokens=2048,
        max_num_seqs=4,
        limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 2},
        gpu_memory_utilization=gpu_util,
        enforce_eager=True,
    )

    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    span = "<|audio_bos|><|AUDIO|><|audio_eos|>"
    inputs = [
        {
            "prompt": f"{span}What do you hear?",
            "multi_modal_data": {"audio": [_audio(0.37, rng)]},
        },
        {
            "prompt": f"{span}{span}Compare the two clips.",
            "multi_modal_data": {"audio": [_audio(3.3, rng), _audio(7.77, rng)]},
        },
        {
            "prompt": f"{span}Describe this.",
            "multi_modal_data": {"audio": [_audio(10.0, rng)]},
        },
    ]
    # ignore_eos: the base model may emit EOS immediately on raw (non-chat)
    # prompts; force 8 decode steps so the LoRA-mapped decode path runs too.
    sp = vllm.SamplingParams(
        temperature=0, max_tokens=8, min_tokens=8, ignore_eos=True
    )

    print("=== generate WITH tower/connector LoRA ===")
    out = llm.generate(
        inputs, sp, lora_request=LoRARequest("rand_tower_conn", 1, lora_path)
    )
    assert len(out) == len(inputs)
    for i, o in enumerate(out):
        text = o.outputs[0].text
        assert len(o.outputs[0].token_ids) == 8
        print(f"[lora {i}] {text!r}")

    print("=== generate WITHOUT LoRA (same engine, padded path) ===")
    out = llm.generate(inputs, sp)
    assert len(out) == len(inputs)
    for i, o in enumerate(out):
        print(f"[base {i}] {o.outputs[0].text!r}")

    print("\n=== SMOKE TEST PASSED ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Details

- **Why fixed padding:** scheduled audio items are grouped and batched (`group_and_batch_mm_kwargs`) and `_parse_and_validate_audio_input` pads them to the batch max, so a per-item token count derived from the item's own length can never match the rows the tower linears actually process in a mixed-length batch. Padding every item to `_MAX_AUDIO_LENGTH` (the model's existing `get_max_audio_len`) mirrors Ultravox's `pad_audio_to_max_context` and is gated on `enable_tower_connector_lora` — zero impact when the flag is off.
- **Why this needed #42662:** the pre-#42662 hook (`get_num_mm_encoder_tokens(num_embeds)`) served runtime items and punica wrapper sizing through one formula. For MiDashengLM those must differ: runtime needs the per-item constant, while sizing needs a budget-scaled bound. The `mm_kwargs` parameter disambiguates the two calls.
- **Sizing bound:** placeholder counts are derived from each audio's true length (projector rows are `patches // 5`, floored), so unlike Voxtral's chunk-padded placeholders they cannot bound the number of items within the encoder budget — a batch of many short audios would overflow a full-item-scaled buffer. The sizing path therefore assumes worst-case one-embed items (`num_mm_embeds` items). Cost: tower punica index buffers sized at ~250x the encoder budget in int64 entries (tens of MB at default budgets), only when the flag is on. A follow-up could shrink this by passing the scheduler's max item count through the interface.
- **Limitation:** with the flag on, audio longer than 160000 samples (10s, the profiled max item) is rejected with a clear `ValueError`; without the flag, longer audio behaves as before. The rejection uses the standard `_parse_and_validate_audio_input` error path (like the Ultravox tower's over-long raise); rejecting at input-processing time instead would require LoRA-config visibility in `InputProcessingContext`, which could be a follow-up.
- **Not a duplicate:** as of 2026-10-13, `midashenglm.py` on main has no LoRA support, no open PR touches it for LoRA (searched `midashenglm lora`, `MiDashengLM`, PRs referencing #31479), and MiDashengLM is unclaimed on #31479.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change; the submitter reviewed every line and ran the validation above.

items.body:
## Overview

Add native support for [Cloudflare/clef-flash](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-flash) through `/v1/systemone`, reusing the Qwen3.5 backbone and the joint schema head introduced for Clef-Omni in #61064.

## Claims

- Automatically detect and load the separate joint schema head, scoring `choice`, `noul`, and `score` questions in one pooling request.
- Support text/JSON, images, and videos sampled at 2 fps. Match the release's fixed prompt, media separators, schema spans, and 16K truncation.
- Share the head/pooler between Clef-Flash and Clef-Omni. Flash rejects audio inputs and ignores video soundtracks.

## Validation

Compared the full checkpoint at revision `8b2e5fd17c09fd49bc2880b805d5323ec7ff4ff3` against the release's `joint_schema_model.py` in BF16. Ten model inputs covered invoice decisions, Unicode/empty instructions, a state truncated to 16K, one/two images, video, and image+video. Prompt token IDs and question/option spans matched the reference exactly in all ten cases.

Each mode ran the ten inputs once sequentially and twice at concurrency 4:

| Mode | Requests | Highest-probability option matches | Max absolute probability difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Eager | 30 | 57/57 | 0.001508 |
| Default compile | 30 | 57/57 | 0.000863 |

The four invoice threshold labels were correct in every repetition (12/12 per mode). These are synthetic model correctness checks. Probability normalization and input-token counts also matched; output-token counts were zero.

The reference evaluation used `encode_record`, `collate_records`, and `load_release_model(..., attn_implementation="sdpa")`, comparing each question's softmax probabilities against `/v1/systemone` responses. Serve the model with:

```bash
vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-flash \
  --served-model-name clef-flash --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --max-num-seqs 8
# Add --enforce-eager for the eager comparison.
```

## Details

The checkpoint advertises `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` and supplies `joint_head_config.json` plus `joint_head.safetensors`. Architecture conversion detects that head, and the Flash wrapper uses the output embedding table for lexical option features, matching the reference implementation.

The existing Clef head/pooler is moved unchanged into `clef_joint_schema.py`. Flash shares the joint schema strategy's typed answers and span/truncation logic, with its own media rendering for adjacent placeholders and a single trailing newline.

Duplicate checks found no open Clef-Flash support PR. #61064 supports Clef-Omni; the other open Clef-related PRs concern API/frontend behavior.

Model comparisons cover BF16 with TP=1. Multi-GPU configurations, quantization, and the full Clef checkpoint were not evaluated.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to implement and validate this model support.

items.body:
## Overview

Enable LoRA for `BertForSequenceClassification` cross-encoders, e.g. `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2`. That includes PEFT `SEQ_CLS` adapters that save a trained classification head. Follow-up to #61033 (BERT/RoBERTa embedding models); same pattern as #58884.

## Claims

- `--enable-lora` works instead of failing with `... does not support LoRA yet.`
- PEFT adapters with a saved head (`modules_to_save=["classifier"]`) load and match transformers + PEFT. Backbone-only adapters match too.
- Without LoRA, outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

Tesla T4, main @ e0317b28c. Random PEFT adapters (r=8, `init_lora_weights=False`); saved heads are perturbed so they differ from the base head. Each pair is scored with `LLM.score`, vLLM fp16 vs transformers + PEFT (merged) fp32 on CPU, 4 query/document pairs.

| Model | Adapter | Max abs diff, base | Max abs diff, LoRA vs HF+PEFT | LoRA effect (HF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 (raw logits) | encoder q/k/v/dense + saved head | 0.0022 | 0.0027 | 13.53 |
| ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 (raw logits) | encoder q/k/v/dense only | 0.0022 | 0.0110 | 7.25 |

- **On main:** the model fails at startup with `... does not support LoRA yet.`
- **With only `SupportsLoRA` added (no classifier change):** the saved-head adapter fails with `ValueError: Cannot load full module 'classifier': the model does not expose a unique ClassificationHeadWithLoRA.`
- **Existing tests,** each passing both before and after the change:
  - `tests/models/language/pooling/test_classification.py::test_bert_model_runner_v2`
  - `tests/models/test_registry.py`
  - `tests/models/test_initialization.py -k BertForSequenceClassification`
  - `tests/lora/test_sequence_classification.py`
  - `tests/models/language/pooling_mteb_test/test_cross_encoder.py`

The comparison script (adapter generation + vLLM vs HF+PEFT check) is ~150 lines; happy to share it or turn it into a `tests/lora` case if useful.

## Details

- **`classifier`: `nn.Linear` → `ReplicatedLinear(..., return_bias=False)`.** With the default `target_modules`, `LoRAModelManager` only wraps `LinearBase` modules (`is_supported_lora_module`). A plain `nn.Linear` classifier therefore never becomes a `ClassificationHeadWithLoRA`, and `_validate_modules_to_save` rejects saved heads. This matches how `as_seq_cls_model` builds `score`, and #60211 makes the same change for RoBERTa's head. BERT's head is a single linear, so this stays within the existing single-layer `modules_to_save` contract. Same weights, bias and `head_dtype`, so non-LoRA outputs are identical. The weight names are unchanged.
- **`packed_modules_mapping`:** `qkv_proj ← query/key/value`. BERT's vLLM module names already match HF, so no `hf_to_vllm_mapper` is needed.
- **`self.config`** is needed by the LoRA manager.
- **Limitation: `bert.pooler.dense` is not LoRA-wrapped,** because `BertPooler.dense` is a plain `nn.Linear`. An adapter that targets it loads and the pooler LoRA is dropped: max abs diff 0.42 vs HF on the pooler-targeting adapter. This is the same class of issue as RoBERTa's `classifier.dense` in #60211. Making it a `ReplicatedLinear` would apply token-indexed LoRA in a per-sequence stage, so I left it. Happy to follow the reviewers' preference: reject such adapters, or let BERT opt `bert.pooler.dense` in if `lora_classifier_modules` from #60211 lands.
- **ModernBERT left out on purpose:** #59206 moves `ModernBertForSequenceClassification` to the Transformers modeling backend and removes the native class, so I didn't touch it. The same change does work there (gte-reranker-modernbert-base on the same T4 setup: max abs diff 0.0002 with a saved head, 0.0014 encoder-only), and I'm happy to send it separately if that's useful before #59206 lands.
- **Scope and fallback:** this does not change `modules_to_save` or any shared LoRA code. It only makes this single-linear classifier eligible for the existing saved-head path. If maintainers prefer not to widen saved-head support for now (see the scope discussion on #60211), the `ReplicatedLinear` change can be dropped. That leaves backbone-only LoRA, as in #58884, which the "encoder only" rows above already validate.
- **No file overlap with #60211** (`vllm/lora/*`, `roberta.py`).
- **CI gap:** no new test. LoRA correctness needs a GPU and adapter checkpoints. Happy to add a `tests/lora` case if wanted.

items.title: [Model] Support MTP drafts in the Transformers modeling backend
items.body:
## Overview

Serve the MTP layers of any model that opts into the Transformers MTP standard (huggingface/transformers#46229) as a speculative decoding draft in the Transformers modeling backend.

Draft: depends on huggingface/transformers#49544, which adds the `MtpModel` helpers this uses (`forward_layer`, `get_mtp_weights_regex`, `get_weight_conversions`) so vLLM shares the per-layer logic and weight loading with Transformers instead of duplicating them. The minimum version is set to 5.20.0, assuming that PR lands in it.

## Claims

- `--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", ...}'` works for targets on the Transformers backend whose config sets `num_mtp_layers` (`TransformersForMTP` / `TransformersMoEForMTP`)
- MTP weights are found and renamed by the same `MtpModel` helpers as `MtpModel.from_pretrained`, so new checkpoint layouts only need the Transformers-side mapping
- Multi-module MTP: `spec_step_idx` selects the MTP layer, so `num_speculative_tokens > 1` uses every checkpoint layer
- Covers DeepSeek-V3/R1 and GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7 today, and Mellum with huggingface/transformers#49531

## Validation

items.title: [Model] Support ModernBERT decoder (Ettin) via the Transformers modeling backend
items.body:
## Overview

Supports `ModernBertDecoderForCausalLM` (the [Ettin](https://huggingface.co/collections/jhu-clsp/encoders-vs-decoders-the-ettin-suite-686303e16142257eed8e6aeb) decoders, 17M–1B) through the Transformers modeling backend. To do this, the backend's causal LM head learns to handle output heads that transform the hidden states before the output embeddings.

There is no existing issue or PR for this. I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `ModernBertDecoder`, `ettin`, `modernbert decoder`, and for output-head / `lm_head` changes to the Transformers backend.

## Claims

- `jhu-clsp/ettin-decoder-*` models load and generate with vLLM. Before this change, loading failed with `ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'lm_head.dense' in TransformersForCausalLM`.
- Generic: the Transformers backend now supports any `ForCausalLM` whose output embeddings are not called `lm_head`, plus one module applied to the hidden states before them. For example, `decoder(lm_head(hidden_states))` with a biased, tied `decoder`.
- No cost or behavior change for other models. Only classes that override `get_output_embeddings` are inspected: 31 of the 178 `AutoModelForCausalLM` classes in Transformers 5.19. The other 147 return early without building anything. The inspected ones that already work keep their behavior; for example, GPT-NeoX's `test_common` still passes.

## Validation

H100 80GB, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` editable install on top of `ffec221276`, Transformers 5.19.0, torch 2.13.

**Correctness against Transformers.** Greedy, 32 tokens, the 8 prompts in `tests/prompts/example.txt`, float32 on both sides:

| model | identical generations |
|---|---|
| `jhu-clsp/ettin-decoder-17m` | 8 / 8 (32/32 tokens each) |
| `jhu-clsp/ettin-decoder-150m` | 7 / 8 (the 8th diverges only at its last token, 32/32) |

In bfloat16, `check_logprobs_close` against `HfRunner` fails for both sizes. At each mismatch the two candidate tokens have identical vLLM logprobs (e.g. ` detect` / ` identify` both −3.1181, `performance` / `throughput` both −0.8469). That is a bf16 near-tie in small models, not a model difference, so the end-to-end test runs in float32.

**Tests** (all passing):

```bash
# new: head detection + renaming (meta device, no GPU), and HF-vs-vLLM float32 e2e on ettin-decoder-17m
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py -k test_output_head          # 4 passed
# new registry entry initializes with dummy weights
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k ModernBertDecoder               # 1 passed
# regression: an architecture that overrides get_output_embeddings and already runs on this backend
pytest tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py -k "pythia and not prompt_embeds_True"   # 2 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                        # all hooks pass (incl. mypy)
```

## Details

**Root cause.** The backend builds `AutoModel` (the base model) and adds its own `ParallelLMHead` named `lm_head`. It assumes the Transformers `ForCausalLM` is `lm_head(model(...))`. ModernBERT decoder is instead `decoder(lm_head(model(...)))`:

- its `lm_head` is a prediction head (dense → GELU → LayerNorm);
- `decoder` is the output projection, tied to the input embeddings and with its own bias.

So the checkpoint's `lm_head.dense.*` had nowhere to load, and skipping the prediction head would also produce wrong logits.

**Change** (`transformers/causal.py`, about 90 lines):

- `CausalMixin._output_head` finds the output head:
  - It returns at once unless the `ForCausalLM` class overrides `get_output_embeddings`; only such a class can name its output embeddings differently.
  - Otherwise, it builds that class on `meta`, as `SequenceClassificationMixin` already does for classifiers. It takes the output embeddings' attribute name, plus the one parameterized child that is neither the base model nor the output embeddings, if there is exactly one.
  - With more than one such child, the order of application can't be known. The backend logs a warning and keeps today's behavior.
- `load_weights` renames the output embeddings' weights to `lm_head.*` and the transform's weights to `lm_head_transform.*`. The existing `lm_head.bias` handling then loads `decoder.bias` unchanged.
- `compute_logits` applies `lm_head_transform`, if present, before the logits processor. It runs only on the sampled positions and outside the compiled region. It adds no CPU/GPU synchronization.

The transform stays a plain Transformers module, replicated on every TP rank. It is a hidden×hidden matrix, so this is negligible.

**Why the Transformers backend and not a native model file.** Small dense models are being moved to the backend (#48100, #53615, #59679, #59701). This architecture runs on it once the head is understood: separate q/k/v projections are fused into `QKVParallelLinear`, and per-layer sliding windows are mapped from `layer_types`. A native implementation would be about 300 lines for one architecture. For reference, I wrote one first (out of tree, as a plugin), and it matches this PR's outputs.

**Who else this helps.** These architectures also overrode `get_output_embeddings` with a non-`lm_head` name or a transform head in the scan:

- `BioGpt` (`output_projection`)
- `Electra` (`generator_predictions` + `generator_lm_head`)
- `GPTNeoXJapanese` (`embed_out`)
- `TrOCR` (`output_projection`)

They are not registered here and I did not test them.

**Limitations and untested paths:**

- Single GPU only. I had no multi-GPU machine.
- **TP > 1:** ModernBERT decoder has no TP plan, so it relies on the backend's fallback: QKV and attention are sharded, everything else replicated. `Wi` holds the GLU input and gate halves in one matrix; it is not fused, so it stays replicated, which is correct but not optimal.
- **PP:** the transform is only built on the last rank, next to `lm_head`.
- **Docs:** the LoRA and PP checkmarks in `supported_models.md` follow the backend's general support, like the other backend entries. They were not exercised for this model.
- **Fusion count:** the GLU fusion count in the e2e test is `(0, 1)` because `Wi` is already a single matrix.

**AI assistance.** This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.

items.title: [Model] Add TeleOCR support
items.body:
## Overview

Add built-in support for [TeleOCR](https://github.com/caipeng328/TeleOCR), using the existing Qwen2.5-VL vision stack and a Qwen3 text decoder.

## Claims

- Register `TeleOCRForConditionalGeneration` without replacing the Qwen2.5-VL architecture globally.
- Initialize Qwen3 with `hf_text_config`, including its head dimension and Q/K normalization, while retaining the existing multimodal processor and weight-loading path.
- Add an example to the model initialization test registry and document the required architecture override. The official model-specific plugin is not needed.

## Validation

All applicable staged-file pre-commit hooks passed during `git commit`, including mypy, Ruff, SPDX, Markdown, and test-tethering checks. `git diff --check 3fe917abb13160d60bea5330399f5c09ca282348 HEAD` passed. The squash retains the exact previously validated code tree.

External integration used Ascend 910B, [vLLM 0.30.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607), [vllm-ascend](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/16074608c71ef5adce4e2a4e475848b8fc037297), Torch 2.10.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4, Transformers 5.14.1, and CANN 9.1.0 B243. The model class was identical to this branch; the small base-class hook was equivalently ported to that runtime. This was **not** a full native current-main integration run, and no Ascend repository changes were required.

Checkpoint: [`XingChen-AGI/TeleOCR`, revision `70a19ec6a3b036311af19ae5e762e650f41a5980`](https://huggingface.co/XingChen-AGI/TeleOCR/tree/70a19ec6a3b036311af19ae5e762e650f41a5980).

Actual serving command, with that checkpoint downloaded to `/task/models/TeleOCR`:

```bash
vllm serve /task/models/TeleOCR --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18193 \
  --served-model-name TeleOCR --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 \
  --hf-overrides '{"architectures":["TeleOCRForConditionalGeneration"]}'
```

External validation harness commands and results:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `python /task/probe_document.py` | Synthetic document OCR and layout checks passed; expected text and box/label structure were present. |
| `python /task/load_http.py --kind document --requests 4 --concurrency 2 --output /task/results/load-document.json` | 4/4 requests succeeded. This is a bounded smoke check, not a throughput benchmark. |
| `PYTHONPATH= /task/hf-reference-clean/bin/python /task/validate_reference.py` | Same-image, same-prompt greedy prefix matched the independent official HF model, CPU FP32 versus NPU BF16, up to 24 new tokens. Reference environment used Transformers 4.57.1. |

The harness scripts above are external to this PR. The registry addition is exercised by the existing `tests/models/test_initialization.py` Buildkite job; that full current-main test was not run locally. CUDA/ROCm, full OmniDocBench evaluation, and LoRA/TP/PP remain unverified. An additional all-files check was not clean: aggregate mypy failed, and the non-root wrapper test hit the macOS `/var` versus `/private/var` path mismatch. Changed-file checks passed; no claim of full-suite or CI success is made.

## Details

The published checkpoint advertises Qwen2.5-VL, but its text decoder is Qwen3. Selecting the ordinary Qwen2 decoder therefore gives the wrong attention implementation. Passing the outer multimodal config to Qwen3 also fails because text attributes such as `vocab_size` are nested. A protected decoder-construction hook lets TeleOCR select Qwen3 with the text sub-configuration and reuse the vision implementation. The default Qwen2.5-VL construction is preserved.

Before submission, searches for TeleOCR, NaviDC, and NaviOCR found no existing matching PR. This adds a dedicated built-in architecture instead of the official external vLLM 0.11 plugin's global replacement. AI assistance was used to implement, validate, and prepare this contribution.

## Overview

Implement `SupportsEagle3` for `GraniteMoeForCausalLM` and `GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM` (which also serves `GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM`), so Granite MoE models can serve as targets for aux-hidden-state speculative decoding (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark) and for `extract_hidden_states`. Follow-up to #60855, which did the same for dense `GraniteForCausalLM`.

## Claims

- Granite MoE targets (`GraniteMoeForCausalLM`, `GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM`, `GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM`) can now attach aux-hidden-state drafters and run `extract_hidden_states`. Previously, engine init rejected them because `supports_eagle3` was absent.
- The captured hidden states match HF `output_hidden_states` at the requested layers.
- No behavior change when no aux layers are requested: the models return `hidden_states` exactly as before.

## Validation

Hidden states extracted with `method="extract_hidden_states"` and `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`, compared with HF transformers `output_hidden_states` on the same token ids (3 prompts, up to ~450 tokens, bf16, GB200):

`ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct` (`GraniteMoeForCausalLM`, 24 layers)

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k 'GraniteMoeForCausalLM or GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM or GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM'  # 3 passed
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py  # 9 passed
```

Same pattern as #60855. The inner models inherit `EagleModelMixin` and record hidden states with `_maybe_add_hidden_state` in the layer loop. The outer `*ForCausalLM` classes declare `SupportsEagle3`. `granitemoeshared.py` has its own model class and layer loop (it does not reuse `GraniteMoeModel.forward`), so both files need the change. items.title: [Model] Support Cloudflare/clef-omni on /v1/systemone
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Serve [`Cloudflare/clef-omni`](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-omni) on `/v1/systemone`. Clef-Omni is Qwen3-Omni's thinker with a joint schema head that scores every option of every question in one forward pass; vLLM runs it as a pooling model, `ClefOmniForJointSchema`.

```bash
vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-omni
```

## Claims

- `vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-omni` answers `/v1/systemone` with the same answers as the checkpoint's own `joint_schema_model.py`, for text and JSON states and all three question types.
- One request is one forward pass: the prompt is prefilled once for all its questions.
- `images`, `audio` and `videos` (URLs or data URLs) are accepted on `/v1/systemone` for models that take them; other models return 400.

## Validation

**Prompt parity (CPU).** For 5 records (JSON/text/unicode states, choice/noul/score, empty instructions, state truncation), the prompt token ids and every question/option span equal `encode_record`'s. For image, audio, silent video, video with soundtrack, and image+audio+video, the expanded media tokens equal the reference processor's.

**Head parity (CPU, fp32, random weights).** The batched pooler matches a per-question port of the reference head to 7e-7; this is the CI test.

**Answers against the reference (one GB200, bf16).** Reference: the checkpoint's `load_release_model` + `encode_record` on transformers 5.18. 11 requests, sent once sequentially and 4 times concurrently (55 requests): 0 errors, every pick matches, input token counts identical.

| Request | Max prob. gap |
|---|---|
| Invoice JSON, choice + noul | 0.0004 |
| Ticket text, choice + score + noul | 0.009 |
| JSON state, 4 questions | 0.011 |
| French/Japanese, 4-way language choice (0.51/0.42 split) | 0.047 |
| Arithmetic, choice + noul + 10-level score | 0.017 |
| 39k-token log (chunked prefill) | 0.006 |
| Image, 3 questions | 0.001 |
| Audio, 3 questions | 0.003 |
| Silent video, 2 questions | 0.034 |
| Video with soundtrack, 2 questions | 0.049 |
| Image + audio + video, 3 questions | 0.018 |

Sequential and concurrent answers agree to 7e-4. The largest gaps are on split distributions; the reference itself moves by 0.028 on the language question between bf16 and fp32, and an fp32 run of both sides leaves a 0.03 gap, so it is not only bf16 rounding in vLLM.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_clef_omni.py \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py \
  "tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[ClefOmniForJointSchema]"
```

All pass on GB200 (structured decisions e2e on Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B included). No CI test loads the 30B checkpoint; parity above was run by hand.

## Details

- **Selection.** The checkpoint keeps Qwen3-Omni's `config.json`, so `get_config` switches `Qwen3OmniMoeForConditionalGeneration` to `ClefOmniForJointSchema` when the repo has `joint_head_config.json`. `--hf-overrides` still wins.
- **Model.** The thinker unchanged; the head runs in a `token_classify` pooler on the whole prompt's final hidden states, with `AllPool` for chunked prefill. The schema (question types, question/option spans, option counts) travels in `PoolingParams.extra_kwargs`. Spans count from the end of the prompt, so media expansion before the state does not move them. The head reuses `nn.MultiheadAttention`/`nn.TransformerDecoderLayer` so the checkpoint's weights load as is; `joint_head.safetensors` is outside the shard index and is loaded in `load_weights`. The pooler returns an empty output instead of raising on a missing or malformed schema.
- **Endpoint.** `JointSchemaStrategy` builds the prompt exactly as `encode_record` does (each piece tokenized on its own), sends one pooling request, and maps option probabilities back to request order. `label_mass` is 1 and `usage.input_tokens` counts the prompt once. Read strategies now declare the engine task they run as (`generate`, or `token_classify` for Clef) and `/v1/systemone` is set up once for every server, so a model gets the endpoint exactly when its architecture has a strategy for a task it serves. Strategies may also render the state themselves (Clef uses compact JSON with sorted keys).
- **Media.** Fetched through `MediaConnector` (allowed domains/paths, download cap). Audio and video are decoded as the reference does (PyAV, 16 kHz mono; frames at 2 fps, ≤ 256·32·32 px), with the audio duration/size limits and a 768-frame cap. A video's soundtrack is heard when every video has one.
- **Qwen3-Omni fix.** With `use_audio_in_video`, audio/video tokens were interleaved with `second_per_grid_ts` from the request kwargs (default 2.0) while the processor and the mrope positions used the processed value; with `fps=2` the token order differed from HF. It now uses the processed value. Covered by `test_audio_in_video_follows_requested_fps`.
- **Limitations.** Request-level `instructions` returns 400 (fixed prompt); `chat_template_kwargs` has no effect. Audio clips together with videos that have soundtracks return 400. A choice is capped at 26 options and a score at 10 levels, like other strategies. Validated on MRV2, TP=1.
- **Duplicate check.** Open PR and issue searches for Clef-Omni found nothing.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, validation and this description. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line.

items.body:
## Overview

Enable LoRA adapters for `BertModel`, `RobertaModel` and `XLMRobertaModel` embedding models. All three load through `BertEmbeddingModel`, which `RobertaEmbeddingModel` subclasses. Covered models include `BAAI/bge-*`, `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-*` and `intfloat/multilingual-e5-*`. Follows #57148 (ModernBERT) and #58884 (RobertaForSequenceClassification).

Related: #40581 adds LoRA to `BertWithRope` models and `XLMRobertaModel`, but not `BertModel`. See Details for the overlap.

## Claims

- `--enable-lora` works for these models instead of failing with `BertEmbeddingModel does not support LoRA yet.`
- PEFT adapters trained on the HF backbone apply to the correct modules, and the outputs match HF + PEFT. This holds whether the adapter's weight names have no prefix or start with `bert.` / `roberta.` (e.g. trained on `*ForMaskedLM`).

## Validation

Tesla T4, main @ 2d69083c4.
- **Adapter:** random PEFT adapter (r=8, `init_lora_weights=False`, targets encoder `query|key|value|dense`).
- **Comparison:** vLLM fp16 vs HF + PEFT (merged) in fp32 on CPU, 4 sentences, L2-normalized embeddings.
- **Prefixed adapters:** copies of the plain adapter with the weight names rewritten. They're compared against the same HF reference.

| Model | Arch / pooling | Adapter names | vLLM base vs HF base (min cos) | vLLM+LoRA vs HF+LoRA (min cos) | vLLM+LoRA vs vLLM base (max cos) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 | BERT / MEAN | plain | 0.999999 | 0.999998 | 0.130 |
| sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 | BERT / MEAN | `bert.` | 0.999999 | 0.999998 | 0.130 |
| BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 | BERT / CLS | plain | 0.999999 | 0.999999 | 0.321 |
| sentence-transformers/all-distilroberta-v1 | RoBERTa / MEAN | plain | 0.999999 | 0.999997 | 0.118 |
| sentence-transformers/all-distilroberta-v1 | RoBERTa / MEAN | `roberta.` | 0.999999 | 0.999997 | 0.118 |
| intfloat/multilingual-e5-base | XLM-RoBERTa / MEAN | plain | 0.999999 | 1.000000 | 0.611 |
| intfloat/multilingual-e5-base | XLM-RoBERTa / MEAN | `roberta.` | 0.999999 | 1.000000 | 0.611 |

The last column shows the adapter is actually applied, not silently ignored.

Before this change, the BERT and RoBERTa models fail at startup with `ValueError: BertEmbeddingModel does not support LoRA yet.`

`pytest tests/models/language/pooling/test_embedding.py tests/models/language/pooling/test_truncation_control.py -k 'not mistral and not gemma2 and not Qwen2'`: 11 passed both before and after.

LoRA only runs in fp16 here because the LoRA shrink kernel requires fp16/bf16 and the T4 has no bf16.

<details><summary>Validation script</summary>

```python
"""Check vLLM LoRA embeddings for a BERT-family model against HF + PEFT.

Usage:
  python validate_bert_lora.py make-adapter MODEL OUT_DIR
  python validate_bert_lora.py prefix-adapter SRC_DIR OUT_DIR PREFIX
  python validate_bert_lora.py check MODEL ADAPTER_DIR [--hf-adapter DIR]
                                     [--expect-unsupported]
"""

import json
import sys

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

TEXTS = [
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
    "vLLM serves embedding models with paged attention.",
    "LoRA adds a low-rank update to frozen weights.",
    "Blacksburg is home to Virginia Tech.",
]


def make_adapter(model_name: str, out_dir: str) -> None:
    from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
    from transformers import AutoModel

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    base = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype=torch.float32)
    config = LoraConfig(
        r=8,
        lora_alpha=16,
        # Encoder projections only; HF's unused `pooler.dense` is left out.
        target_modules=r".*encoder.*\.(query|key|value|dense)$",
        init_lora_weights=False,  # random A and B, so the adapter has an effect
    )
    peft_model = get_peft_model(base, config)
    peft_model.save_pretrained(out_dir)
    from safetensors import safe_open

    with safe_open(f"{out_dir}/adapter_model.safetensors", "pt") as f:
        names = sorted(f.keys())
    print(f"saved adapter with {len(names)} tensors, e.g. {names[:2]}")


def prefix_adapter(src: str, out: str, prefix: str) -> None:
    """Copy an adapter, renaming `base_model.model.X` to `base_model.model.<prefix>X`.

    Mimics an adapter trained on e.g. `BertForMaskedLM` (weights under `bert.`).
    """
    import shutil

    from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file

    shutil.copytree(src, out, dirs_exist_ok=True)
    tensors = load_file(f"{src}/adapter_model.safetensors")
    head = "base_model.model."
    renamed = {head + prefix + k[len(head) :]: v for k, v in tensors.items()}
    save_file(renamed, f"{out}/adapter_model.safetensors")
    print(f"prefixed {len(renamed)} tensors, e.g. {sorted(renamed)[0]}")


def hf_embeddings(model_name, adapter_dir, pooling, normalize):
    from peft import PeftModel
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype=torch.float32).eval()
    if adapter_dir:
        model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, adapter_dir).merge_and_unload()
    out = []
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for text in TEXTS:
            enc = tok(text, return_tensors="pt")
            hidden = model(**enc).last_hidden_state[0]
            vec = hidden[0] if pooling == "CLS" else hidden.mean(dim=0)
            out.append(F.normalize(vec, dim=-1) if normalize else vec)
    return torch.stack(out)


def check(model_name, adapter_dir, hf_adapter_dir, expect_unsupported) -> int:
    from vllm import LLM
    from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

    result = {"model": model_name, "adapter": adapter_dir}
    try:
        llm = LLM(
            model=model_name,
            runner="pooling",
            dtype="float16",  # LoRA shrink kernel needs fp16/bf16; T4 has no bf16
            enforce_eager=True,
            max_model_len=256,
            enable_lora=True,
            max_lora_rank=8,
            gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
        )
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        msg = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        result.update(status="lora_rejected", error=msg[:400])
        print("RESULT", json.dumps(result))
        return 0 if expect_unsupported else 1

    if expect_unsupported:
        result["status"] = "unexpectedly_accepted"
        print("RESULT", json.dumps(result))
        return 1

    pooler = llm.llm_engine.vllm_config.model_config.pooler_config
    pooling = pooler.seq_pooling_type
    lora = LoRARequest("random-adapter", 1, adapter_dir)
    v_base = torch.tensor([o.outputs.embedding for o in llm.embed(TEXTS)])
    v_lora = torch.tensor(
        [o.outputs.embedding for o in llm.embed(TEXTS, lora_request=lora)]
    )
    h_base = hf_embeddings(model_name, None, pooling, normalize=True)
    h_lora = hf_embeddings(model_name, hf_adapter_dir, pooling, normalize=True)

    cos = lambda a, b: F.cosine_similarity(a, b, dim=-1)  # noqa: E731
    base_match = cos(v_base, h_base).min().item()
    lora_match = cos(v_lora, h_lora).min().item()
    lora_effect = cos(v_lora, v_base).max().item()
    lora_vs_hf_base = cos(v_lora, h_base).max().item()
    result.update(
        pooling=pooling,
        min_cos_vllm_base_vs_hf_base=round(base_match, 6),
        min_cos_vllm_lora_vs_hf_lora=round(lora_match, 6),
        max_cos_vllm_lora_vs_vllm_base=round(lora_effect, 6),
        max_cos_vllm_lora_vs_hf_base=round(lora_vs_hf_base, 6),
    )
    ok = base_match > 0.995 and lora_match > 0.995 and lora_effect < 0.99
    result["status"] = "pass" if ok else "fail"
    print("RESULT", json.dumps(result))
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cmd = sys.argv[1]
    if cmd == "make-adapter":
        make_adapter(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
    elif cmd == "prefix-adapter":
        prefix_adapter(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4])
    elif cmd == "check":
        args = sys.argv
        hf_dir = args[args.index("--hf-adapter") + 1] if "--hf-adapter" in args else args[3]
        sys.exit(check(args[2], args[3], hf_dir, "--expect-unsupported" in args))
    else:
        raise SystemExit(__doc__)
```

</details>

## Details

- **`packed_modules_mapping`** maps HF's separate `query`/`key`/`value` LoRA weights onto the fused `qkv_proj`. The inner `BertModel` already declares it; the LoRA manager reads it from the top-level model.
- **`hf_to_vllm_mapper`** places adapter weights under vLLM's `model.` backbone prefix. `BertEmbeddingModel` previously did this renaming only inside `load_weights`, which the LoRA loader does not use. `LoRAModel.from_local_checkpoint` validates only the last name component, so without the mapper an adapter loads but is never applied.
- **`self.config`** is required by the LoRA manager, as in #58884.
- **Side effect:** the class-level mapper is also applied to quantization-config ignore lists (`model_loader/utils.py`), mapping them onto the real `model.`-prefixed module names.
- **Not validated:**
  - `BgeM3EmbeddingModel`, which also inherits the change. Its docs row is left unchanged.
  - The rotary `JinaRobertaModel` path used by `jinaai/jina-embeddings-v3`, which merges its own LoRA weights at load time.
- **Overlap with #40581:** it adds the same `SupportsLoRA`/packing to `RobertaEmbeddingModel`. If that PR lands, its class attributes override the inherited ones; the files don't conflict. cc @yuancu
- **CI gap:** no new test. LoRA correctness needs a GPU and an adapter checkpoint. Happy to add a small `tests/lora` test if reviewers want one.

items.title: [Model] Qwen4Exp: support batch-sharded sampling (compute_logits_local)
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let Qwen4Exp take the batch-sharded sampling path (#50465). `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` inherits `compute_logits_local` from `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, which calls `language_model.compute_logits_local`, but `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM` does not define it. This PR adds the method on the NVIDIA and AMD `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM`, the same 3-line pattern as Qwen3.5 and MiniMax M3.

**Draft:** the end-to-end serving validation below is still running. I will mark the PR ready only after it is filled in.

The first serving run reached "Batch-sharded sampling enabled." on all 8 ranks. It then failed in warm-up, with NCCL out of memory at the first all-to-all. That failure is not specific to Qwen4Exp: the profile run never executes the sharded all-to-all. The fix is #61025, and the serving retry runs with both PRs.

**Retry with #61025 (measured):** start-up passes. All 8 ranks log "Batch-sharded sampling enabled.", warm-up is clean, and the server answers requests. The NCCL all-to-all buffers now take about 2.9 GiB per GPU (non-torch memory 17.75 → 20.62 GiB), so the KV cache falls from 2,128,699 to 1,742,619 tokens (−18 %) on 40 GB A100s. That is a real trade-off for capacity-bound serving; the 3 × 60 min result will show whether the sampling saving outweighs it.

**Serving result (measured, MLPerf agentic full set, 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min per arm, same node type, strict per-request SLO TTFT ≤ 2.93 s and TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms):**

| Arm | Joint SLO pass r1/r2/r3 | Goodput (req/s) | TTFT p50 / p95 (s) | TPOT p50 / p95 (ms) | Accuracy score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flag off | 90.0 / 89.2 / 89.5 % | 1.83–1.89 | 0.93–0.98 / 2.22–2.35 | 14.1–14.3 / 23.9–24.5 | 0.540–0.542 |
| Flag on (this PR + #61025) | 75.2 / 77.4 / 75.3 % | 1.35–1.38 | 1.35–1.41 / 3.22–3.35 | 15.8–16.1 / 27.3–29.2 | 0.536–0.543 |

On this memory-tight, KV-capacity-bound workload, the 18 % smaller KV cache costs far more than sampling saves; nsys on the flag-off run puts redundant sampling at about 1.5–2 % of step time. So **I do not claim a speed-up**. This PR only makes the existing option work for Qwen4Exp (today `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` advertises `compute_logits_local` but the language model lacks it). It should pay off where the KV cache is not the limit, for example GPUs with more memory, or after limiting NCCL point-to-point channels; I have not measured those. If reviewers prefer, I will close this PR rather than add an option that does not help on the hardware I can test.

## Claims

- `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` works for Qwen4Exp. Each TP rank computes its vocabulary shard of the logits (`skip_gather=True`), and the existing `BatchSharder` all-to-all gives each rank the full vocabulary for its share of the requests.
- No change when the flag is off: the new method is reached only from the sharded path.
- (Pending) Serving result on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP8 + EP, 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB.

## Validation

**Unit test** (`tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_compute_logits_local.py`, NVIDIA and AMD classes):
- `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.compute_logits_local` calls the logits processor with `skip_gather=True`.
- The VL wrapper `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration.compute_logits_local` reaches it.
- It follows the existing `test_rocm_compute_logits_local_skips_gather` pattern in `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_rocm.py`.
- Status: TODO, a CUDA run in the vLLM 81198e97 image (scheduled). My local macOS environment cannot import the Qwen4Exp model, because its transformers lacks `Qwen4ExpConfig`.

**End to end** (TODO, running):
- Setup: `vllm serve` Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP8 + EP, MTP 3, prefix caching, FP8 KV, `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, against the same command without the flag. Same node.
- Load: MLPerf agentic dataset (full set), 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min per arm.
- Checks:
  - the start-up log says "Batch-sharded sampling enabled.";
  - no errors;
  - TTFT/TPOT p50/p90/p95/p99 and goodput against the control.
- Correctness: greedy and seeded requests should give the same tokens with and without the flag, because the Gumbel path draws its noise from (seed, position, token id). I will report a seeded comparison.

## Details

- **Root cause:** models opt in to batch-sharded sampling by implementing `compute_logits_local` (`ParallelConfig.enable_batch_sharded_sampling` docstring). The Qwen3.5 VL base class delegates the call to its language model. `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` reuses that base class, but its language model class did not implement the method.
- **Expected effect (estimate from an nsys trace of this model at 16 concurrent sessions):** top-k/top-p and the logits all-gather run redundantly on all 8 ranks, about 0.6–0.8 ms of a 42 ms average step (1.5–2 %). That trace also counted the Triton top-k/top-p kernel at 6.8 % of the eager kernel time.
- **Size:** +14 lines of model code; +57 lines of test.
- **Limitations:**
  - I have not checked whether the MTP drafter's logits take the sharded path; the drafter code is unchanged.
  - LoRA is rejected by the flag itself (#56074).

items.title: [RL] Support model-native rank-local destinations for NCCL M2N
