items.body:
## Summary

This PR is stacked on [#62853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62853),
which adds partitioned trainer source groups directly on main. Merged
[#60934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60934) provides the
per-parameter source layout contract. This PR lets a model module expose a
validated rank-local shard target for a logical checkpoint parameter. NCCL M2N
can then transfer the shard owned by each inference worker instead of
reconstructing a complete logical tensor on every worker.

Fixes #59835.

Before this PR, each parameter was either written into an exact live tensor or
received in full and passed through `load_weights`:

```text
logical parameter -> exact live tensor OR full tensor on every worker
```

After this PR, the destination planner selects and collectively agrees one of
three modes:

```text
logical parameter -> exact live tensor
                  OR rank-local staging target + model callback
                  OR explicitly permitted full tensor on every worker
```

The destination contract is generic. Model integrations define how a logical
checkpoint parameter maps to local storage and how the local shard is consumed.
Unquantized `RoutedExperts` is the first production integration; fused MoE
`w13`/`w2` tensors provide the concrete example below.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    W[Logical checkpoint parameter] --> P{Collectively agreed destination}
    P --> E[Exact live tensor]
    P --> S[Rank-local staging target]
    P --> F[Explicit full fallback]
    S --> C[Model callback]
```

### Relationship to #60934, #62853, and PR boundary

#60934 adds per-parameter trainer-side source layouts. #62853 builds on main,
adds partitioned source groups, and retains the existing receiver behavior.
This PR preserves those source groups and changes destination selection and
loading; it does not reimplement trainer ownership or multi-route execution.

| Behavior | #62853, built on main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Source mesh | Each parameter declares its source mesh and placements | Unchanged |
| Participating trainers | Each parameter selects one canonical source group | Unchanged |
| Destination mesh | One mesh shared by every parameter | Unchanged |
| Destination selection | Exact-name in-place target or full-tensor fallback | Adds validated rank-local staging targets |
| Receiver loading | Exact live tensor or complete logical tensor through `load_weights` | Exact live tensor, rank-local model callback, or explicitly permitted full fallback |

This PR does not introduce per-parameter destination meshes. It adds
per-parameter destination targets over the existing session-wide destination
mesh.

## Problem

#59835 describes the missing model-native loading path for sharded NCCL M2N
destinations. When a logical checkpoint tensor does not exactly match a live
vLLM parameter, the existing fallback reconstructs the complete tensor on every
generator worker, even when that worker consumes only one rank-local shard.

## Implementation

This PR expands the NCCL M2N control plane so every participant agrees on the
complete destination plan before entering the ordered data-plane collectives.

### Model-native sharded targets

`ShardedWeightRequest`, `ShardedWeightSpec`, and `ShardedWeightTarget` define a
model-loader contract independent of NCCL M2N implementation types. A target
declares its local shape, shard dimension/index/count, consumer callback,
atomic group, and retention requirements.

The API is model-independent and has a synthetic non-MoE consumer test. It does
not classify parameters by name inside the transport engine.

### Whole-plan destination agreement

The planner resolves every logical parameter before NCCL4Py transfer-communicator
initialization:

1. prefer a validated semantic rank-local target;
2. otherwise use a validated exact-name in-place target; or
3. use full fallback only when the producer explicitly permits it.

All worker plans are gathered and validated for parameter order, destination
mode, shard ownership, geometry, atomic staging groups, and fallback policy. A
deterministic destination digest and commit token bind that plan to the source
manifest, source-group ownership, and transfer routes before data transfer
begins.

The wire schema advances from #62853's version 3 to version 4 because source
records gain `allow_full_fallback` and destination agreement includes semantic
target metadata. Mixed versions fail during metadata initialization.

`plan_summary()` reports source and destination digests, mode counts, logical
global bytes, and planned aggregate receiver bytes. Receiver bytes describe the
destination volume implied by the plan, not measured fabric traffic.

### Module-scoped in-place demotion

A later layerwise load can overwrite direct writes in the same module. The
planner retains main's module-scoped in-place demotion and applies it to the
expanded destination plan, rejecting demotion when the producer forbids full
fallback. Unrelated modules remain in-place, and semantic targets remain sharded.

### Bounded staging and update lifecycle

Rank-local shards use reusable bounded staging buffers. An atomic group stays
live until its consumer explicitly releases it or layerwise finalization
completes. A callback returning without releasing the group is not enough.
Transfer streams wait for consumer reads before reusing released buffers.
Bindings are recreated for every update so stale model pointers do not survive
repeated updates.

Failure recovery follows #62853's separation of transport and loader state.
Failures known before the first M2N launch reset update-local state and preserve
communicators. Failures while transfer may be in flight abort all joined
transfer communicators and require reinitialization. A loader/finalizer failure
after transfer completion preserves transport, resets loader and staging state,
and allows the trainer's coordinated complete-update replay.

### Fused routed experts

`RoutedExperts` maps unquantized, uniformly and contiguously EP-sharded logical
weights to the experts owned by the local worker:

- the stacked gate/up shard uses the existing loading path into `w13_weight`;
- down shards use the existing loading path into `w2_weight`; and
- paired shards remain retained until native layer loading finalizes.

For compatibility with current main, ownership is checked against
`ExpertMapManager.expert_map` rather than the removed
`get_local_expert_ids()` helper. The check still rejects a target when actual
and declared ownership differ, including after the map is reconfigured.

### Qwen3-235B-A22B example

Qwen3-235B-A22B provides a concrete example of the generic contract. The model
has 128 routed experts, while the measured generator uses EP16. Generator EP
rank 5 therefore owns experts 40 through 47.

For this integration, the producer exports a stacked logical
`gate_up_proj.weight` tensor containing both gate and up projections, plus a
logical `down_proj.weight` tensor. For EP rank 5, their local expert slices
load into the runtime's `w13_weight` and `w2_weight`:

| Logical transfer tensor | Rank-local data received by EP rank 5 | Runtime target |
|---|---|---|
| Stacked gate/up (`gate_up_proj.weight`) | Experts 40–47, both projections | `w13_weight` |
| Down (`down_proj.weight`) | Experts 40–47 | `w2_weight` |

The destination is derived from `RoutedExperts` ownership and loading metadata,
not from model-name checks in the transport layer. These two shards remain
staged as one atomic pair until the existing model loading path releases them.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph L[Qwen3-235B-A22B logical weights owned by EP rank 5]
        GU[Stacked gate/up shard]
        D[Down projection shards]
    end
    GU --> S[Retained two-tensor staging group]
    D --> S
    S --> W13[Fused w13_weight]
    S --> W2[w2_weight]
```

Qwen is the first production integration and the end-to-end validation example;
it is not a constraint on the transport contract.

## Supported scope

The generic source and destination contracts are independent of model type,
world size, and the measured 16-to-16 topology. Semantic destination selection
currently requires an unquantized generator deployment with PP1. The first
`RoutedExperts` consumer additionally supports:

- unquantized FP16 or BF16 weights;
- generator TP1 and PP1 with expert parallelism enabled;
- uniform contiguous linear expert ownership; and
- recognized logical gate/up and down projections.

Recognized malformed logical tensors and explicitly rejected reload paths fail
closed. When a model declines a target capability, explicitly permitted full
fallback remains available; initialization fails if the producer forbids it.
Other parameters may use exact in-place destinations.

All parameters still share one configured destination mesh. Per-parameter
destination meshes are future work and are not implemented here.

## Validation

Coverage includes:

- destination disagreement before NCCL4Py communicator construction;
- worker-specific shard-index validation;
- direct, staged, and full-fallback entries in one plan;
- module-scoped demotion;
- complete staging-group retention and bounded reuse;
- update-scoped callback rebinding;
- callback failure cleanup and inherited transport-abort behavior;
- explicit owner-local receiver-byte accounting;
- a non-Qwen semantic consumer; and
- routed-expert ownership and `w13`/`w2` fusion.

Focused validation ran on an AArch64 compute node with four NVIDIA GB200 GPUs:

| Component | Version or setting |
|---|---|
| Python | 3.12.13 |
| PyTorch | 2.14.0+cu130 |
| CUDA | 13.0 |
| NCCL | 2.30.7 |
| NCCL extensions | 0.1.0 |
| nccl4py | 0.5.0 |
| `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` | `1` |

Current-restack validation used the official AArch64 native wheel for
`224b2f54f19d`. Its compiled sources and dependency pins match the main base,
`a0544b13f2ee`; the affected source and test files match this PR head.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -P -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer_m2n.py \
  tests/distributed/test_utils.py::test_stateless_process_group_many_to_one_objects_do_not_collide \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_sharded_weight.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::test_abort_layerwise_reload_restores_tensors_for_retry \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py \
  -v -ra --maxfail=20
```

| Current-restack gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Complete M2N, sharded-target, control, loader-abort, and worker-lifecycle selection | 236 passed, no failures or skips |
| CUDA expert-ownership regression | Failed on the removed helper before the compatibility fix; passed with the fix |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks on AArch64 | Passed, including mypy, Ruff, markdownlint, and test tethering |

The suite includes real TCP and pre-shared UID transfers, TP2 destination
resharding, mixed source meshes, disjoint source groups, and a generic
owner-local semantic consumer in addition to the routed-expert integration.

The broader reload suite also encountered 20 unavailable Hugging Face config or
checkpoint failures in the offline cache. Unmodified exact main reproduced the
same 20 failures; the focused loader-abort and worker tests above passed.

## End-to-end performance

These are the original trainer-PP1 measurements, collected before the current
restack. They evaluate rank-local destinations without partitioned PP source
groups; they are not the PP2 experiment reported in #62853. Full-model
generation and RL performance have not been rerun on this restacked head.

We compared the existing SkyRL NCCL broadcast backend with NCCL M2N using the
same eight-node allocation, immutable software environment, model, training
workload, and generator configuration. The only experimental variable was
`weight_sync_backend`.

This experiment used no LoRA and performed full-parameter BF16 fine-tuning.

| Configuration | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | Qwen3-235B-A22B |
| Hardware | 8 nodes, 4 GB200 GPUs per node |
| Trainer | 4 nodes / 16 GPUs |
| Generator | 4 nodes / 16 GPUs |
| Trainer parallelism | TP4 / PP1 / CP1 / EP16 / ETP1 / EDP1 |
| Generator parallelism | TP1 / PP1 / DP16 / EP16 / EDP1 |
| Training | Full-parameter BF16; no LoRA |
| Workload | GSM8K GRPO |
| Batch | 16 prompts; 4 generations per prompt |
| Sequence limits | 512 prompt tokens; 1,024 generated tokens |
| Generator attention | FlashInfer |
| Generator MoE | FlashInfer TRTLLM unquantized monolithic MoE |
| CUDA graphs | Enabled |
| NCCL | `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`; unchanged debug settings |
| Topology | NVLink/MNNVL within each 16-GPU role; InfiniBand/GDRDMA between roles |
| Sampling | 1 cold synchronization excluded; 10 warm synchronizations retained |
| Synchronization point | Each retained synchronization followed a completed optimizer step |

Both methods ran back-to-back on the same nodes. The trainer and generator
software environments, model state, optimizer configuration, MoE backend,
attention backend, CUDA-graph policy, and NCCL settings were identical.

### Results

| Timing boundary | NCCL broadcast | NCCL M2N | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Weight-sync E2E mean | 13.869 s | 3.044 s | 4.557×; 78.05% lower |
| Total unavailable mean | 13.924 s | 3.099 s | 4.494×; 77.75% lower |
| Pause/resume and outer wrapper mean | 0.0547 s | 0.0549 s | Unchanged |

![Qwen3-235B-A22B: mean weight-sync E2E, NCCL broadcast 13.869 seconds versus NCCL M2N 3.044 seconds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pkousha/vllm/c2ed488a331f566689971b1fa561c0422b6154c1/pr-assets/m2n-qwen3-235b-weight-sync.png)

Figure: the original PP1, no-LoRA, full-parameter BF16 experiment. Each mean
retains 10 warm synchronizations after excluding one cold synchronization;
these are not new measurements of the restacked head.

The mean is the primary result and retains every warm sample. The E2E medians
were 13.741 seconds for NCCL broadcast and 2.850 seconds for NCCL M2N.

### Timing boundaries

The weight-sync E2E timer starts before Megatron weight extraction and
conversion. It includes required trainer collectives, trainer-to-generator
transfer, and vLLM receive/load processing, and ends after the generator update
finishes.

`update_weights` is a concurrent wall-clock interval. Megatron extraction,
required collectives, NCCL M2N reshard operations, and receiver loading can
overlap inside it. Its components therefore cannot be interpreted as
independent or additive network-transfer measurements.

| NCCL M2N interval | Warm mean | Included work |
|---|---:|---|
| Start-session fanout | 0.068 s | Starts and validates the update across receivers |
| `update_weights` | 2.926 s | Extraction, collectives, M2N transfer, and receiver loading |
| Finish/commit fanout | 0.030 s | Finalizes staged consumers and commits the update |
| Inner dispatch residual | 0.020 s | Remaining synchronization and dispatch overhead |
| Weight-sync E2E | 3.044 s | Complete inner synchronization boundary |
| Pause/resume and outer wrapper | 0.055 s | Generator availability control outside the inner boundary |
| Total unavailable | 3.099 s | Complete interval during which generation is unavailable |

### Agreed destination plan

The destination plan selected the transfer mode independently for each logical
parameter while preserving one collective order across all participating
ranks.

| Destination mode | Parameters | Logical global size | Planned aggregate receiver size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Exact in-place | 94 | 0.099 GB | 1.577 GB |
| Rank-local staged | 188 | 454.193 GB | 454.193 GB |
| Explicit full fallback | 755 | 15.896 GB | 254.335 GB |
| **Total** | **1,037** | **470.187 GB** | **710.104 GB** |

Reconstructing the complete 470.187-GB checkpoint on all 16 generator workers
would produce 7.523 TB of aggregate receiver payload. The agreed M2N plan
reduces that planned volume to 0.710 TB: a 10.59× reduction, or 90.56% less
receiver payload.

These values describe destination-buffer volume derived from the agreed plan.
They are not physical InfiniBand byte counters and should not be compared
directly with the 4.557× end-to-end latency improvement.

Qwen3-235B-A22B is the measured example. The source-layout, destination-target,
and collective-agreement contracts are not specific to this model, world size,
or parallelism configuration.

## Stack

The merge order is now:

1. [#60934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60934) (merged) adds the
   general per-parameter source-layout contract.
2. [#62853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62853) builds directly on
   main and adds partitioned trainer source groups and multi-route execution.
3. This PR adds collectively agreed rank-local destination targets, bounded
   staging, and consumer callbacks, with unquantized `RoutedExperts` as the
   first production integration.

Review and merge #62853 first. While both PRs target upstream main, this
branch contains #62853 as its ancestor.
[Review the destination-only diff](https://github.com/pkousha/vllm/compare/98feec2308eec34973fa1a4e3e625860da66c1c0...c2ed488a331f566689971b1fa561c0422b6154c1).

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests, validation automation,
benchmark analysis, figures, and drafting. The human submitter reviewed every
changed line before submission.

items.body:
## Overview

Implement `SupportsEagle3` for `GraniteForCausalLM`, so dense Granite models can serve as targets for EAGLE3/DFlash speculative decoding.

## Claims

- Granite targets can now attach aux-hidden-state drafters (EAGLE3, DFlash). Previously, engine init rejected them because `supports_eagle3` was absent.
- Accuracy is unchanged with speculation, and drafts are accepted.

## Validation

Target `ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b` with an internal DFlash drafter (`num_speculative_tokens=15`), on an Intel Xeon 6972P:

```python
LLM(model="ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b",
    speculative_config={"method": "dflash", "model": "<draft>", "num_speculative_tokens": 15})
```

| GSM8K (100 questions, greedy, no-think) | Accuracy | Mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|
| No draft | 75% | — |
| + DFlash | 75% | 3.74 |

Aux hidden states also match HF `output_hidden_states` at the requested layers (fp32, rel. err ~1e-6).

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k 'GraniteForCausalLM or GraniteSWAForCausalLM or Granite4Vision' # 3 passed
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py # 9 passed
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/granite.py # passed
```

## Details

- Follows the existing aux-hidden-state pattern in `minicpm.py` and `apertus.py`. Pipeline parallelism is not supported: MRV2 rejects PP > 1 for this model.
- No public Granite drafter exists yet, so no e2e test is added.
- No existing PR covers this.

items.body: # Context Continuing the effort from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58463 to remove unnecessary attention metadata rebuilds before FULL cudagraph replays for draft model-based speculators. I found an opportunity to use the same `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` flag to gate updating the metadata within the captured decode step for DFlash/DSpark, reducing GPU kernel launch overhead. # This PR Adds support for skipping the full attention metadata rebuild before replaying the uniform decode cudagraph. Previously, only the `TargetDependentARSpeculator` was leveraging the `update_draft_decode_metadata` operations for its attention backends to update the attention metadata in a cudagraph-safe way. In this PR, I move that logic for deciding draft model eligibility (`supports_update_decode_metadata`) for this optimization to the base class `DraftModelSpeculator`, and then i have both `TargetDependentARSpeculator` and `DFlashSpeculator` check this eligibility. If True, capture the `_update_draft_decode_metadata` op in the graph before the draft model forward. Otherwise, rebuild the attention metadata eagerly via `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` before replaying the graph. This optimization has been enabled for DeepSeek V4.1 + DSpark, as verified below. ## Profile Captured while serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on 4xGB200: **Before** **After** ## Benchmarks / Evals **Setup (both subsections).** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=5`, 4x GB200 (TP4), `--max-model-len 102400 --max-num-seqs 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'`, adaptive verification off, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Speed-Bench is 2K/2K (`throughput_16k`, `low_entropy`), with prompts scaled 8x concurrency (min 16), seed 0, and a fresh server per arm. In both subsections the PR server logged no "cannot update draft decode metadata" warning, so the in-graph metadata update was active. ### Greedy draft sampling Baseline is `main` at `b6d8e8afd9`; PR is `1abc890148`. **Speed-Bench, temperature 0.** Each value is the mean of repeated runs: 3 runs at concurrency 1, 2 runs at 16 and 64. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.96 | 6.94 | -0.3% | 1.91 | 1.90 | 521.2 | 520.7 | -0.1% | 3.760 | 3.747 | | 16 | 16.11 | 16.04 | -0.4% | 4.92 | 4.91 | 3144.3 | 3113.5 | -1.0% | 3.775 | 3.755 | | 64 | 30.37 | 30.36 | 0.0% | 9.88 | 9.94 | 6249.0 | 6250.2 | 0.0% | 3.795 | 3.795 | Step time is unchanged at every concurrency. As with MTP in #58463, the host work this removes is not on the critical path for this model at TP4. Acceptance length differs between arms by at most 0.02, while runs of the same arm vary by up to 0.16 at concurrency 1. **AIME25** (MQA, 2 epochs x 30 problems, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max 98304 tokens, 64 concurrent): | Arm | Exact match | pass@2 | Samples | Request errors | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | base | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 60 | 0 | | PR | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 60 | 0 | Accuracy is identical. Every sample includes reasoning, with median completion lengths of 5.3k tokens (base) and 4.9k (PR). ### Probabilistic draft sampling `--speculative-config` adds `"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"`. Baseline is `main` at `240785b82c`; PR is `6065f7c37c` (this branch rebased onto that baseline). **Speed-Bench, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0.** Each value is the mean of 2 runs. Individual acceptance lengths are in brackets. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.89 | 6.86 | -0.4% | 1.95 | 1.86 | 505.1 | 514.8 | +1.9% | 3.60 [3.68, 3.52] | 3.66 [3.71, 3.61] | | 16 | 16.05 | 16.02 | -0.2% | 5.01 | 5.06 | 3051.8 | 3046.9 | -0.2% | 3.64 [3.65, 3.62] | 3.65 [3.65, 3.65] | | 64 | 30.51 | 30.50 | 0.0% | 10.28 | 10.43 | 6061.4 | 5972.4 | -1.5% | 3.66 [3.65, 3.67] | 3.67 [3.66, 3.68] | Median ITL matches within 0.03 ms. The -1.5% throughput at concurrency 64 comes from a single PR run (5930 vs 6015 tok/s for the other); output lengths vary between runs at temperature 1.0. Acceptance length is equal or higher for the PR at every concurrency, and the largest gap (+0.06 at concurrency 1) is smaller than the baseline's own run-to-run spread (0.16). **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot `/v1/completions`, temperature 1.0, max 512 tokens, 64 concurrent). Acceptance is computed from the server's spec-decode counters over the eval: | Arm | Accuracy | Invalid | Accept. len | Per-position acceptance (0-4) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | base | 0.838 | 1.1% | 3.296 | 0.779 / 0.605 / 0.423 / 0.298 / 0.190 | | PR | 0.835 | 1.1% | 3.299 | 0.782 / 0.603 / 0.421 / 0.298 / 0.195 | Accuracy is within 4 questions, and per-position acceptance shows no drop at later draft positions, which is where a stale non-causal window would show up first.

items.title: [Model][LoRA] Support LoRA for EmbeddingGemma2Model
items.body:
## Overview

Enable LoRA for `EmbeddingGemma2Model` (`google/embeddinggemma-2`), added in #60254. Adapters attach to the language model only, so a single engine can serve LoRA-adapted text queries and base-weight image queries in the same batch.

## Claims

- `--enable-lora` works with `EmbeddingGemma2Model`. Before this change, startup fails with `EmbeddingGemma2Model does not support LoRA yet.`
- `get_mm_mapping()` routes LoRA to `language_model`. The vision and audio towers and their connectors keep base weights, and tower/connector LoRA stays disabled.
- Per-request adapters: in one `LLM.embed` call, a request with a `LoRARequest` gets the adapted embedding. Requests without one, including image inputs, return the base embedding.

## Validation

All runs on 1× H200 (Hugging Face Jobs), PR head `0d2f76b` installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` on the wheel for `194da61`, transformers 5.19.0.

**Model tests.** `EG2_MODEL_PATH=google/embeddinggemma-2 pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py`: 14 passed, 5 failed, 3 skipped.

- The new `test_lora_applies_only_to_its_request` passes.
- None of the failures enable LoRA:
    - `test_video_parity_uniform_overflow`, `test_video_parity_portrait`, `test_video_loader_duplicate_expansion_e2e` and `test_video_loader_real_video` fail because torchcodec cannot load FFmpeg in the job container. `test_video_loader_real_video` also needs the local asset `/projects/gemma4-vllm/videos/test_intel.mp4`.
    - `test_instance_attribute_access` fails in `LLM.apply_model`, which needs `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1`. The test does not use the `enable_pickle` fixture.
- The 3 skips need local assets under `/projects/gemma4-vllm`.

**Real adapter, offline.** A rank-32 PEFT adapter over q/k/v/o/gate/up/down of the language model, trained with Unsloth on Nordic query translations. One shuffled `LLM.embed` call with 1,152 requests: 512 texts with the adapter, the same 512 texts without it, and 128 images without it. Cosine similarity to sentence-transformers:

| Requests | Reference | n | min | mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Text + adapter | merged-adapter checkpoint | 512 | 0.99912 | 0.99996 |
| Text, no adapter | base model | 512 | 0.99949 | 0.99994 |
| Image, no adapter | base model | 128 | 0.99966 | 0.99991 |

The adapter changes the vectors: on the 428 non-English queries, adapter vs base cosine is 0.926 mean, 0.765 min.

**Throughput** (4,096 texts, 256 images):

| Engine | Requests | texts/s | images/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no `--enable-lora` | base | 4,281 | 55.4 |
| `--enable-lora` | base | 3,951 | 57.2 |
| `--enable-lora` | adapter | 3,367 | — |

**Online.** `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=True vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 --runner pooling --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 32 --max-loras 1`, then `POST /v1/load_lora_adapter` and `POST /v1/embeddings` with 64 texts:

- with `"model": "nordic"`: min cosine 0.99988 to the merged-adapter checkpoint;
- with the base model name: min cosine 0.99990 to the base model.

**Lint.** `pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` on the branch merged with `main` (`6a70913`, head `04497da`): all 31 hooks pass, including mypy, ruff, markdownlint and test tethering.

CI coverage: the new test uses the same `EG2_MODEL_PATH` gate as the existing EmbeddingGemma2 tests, so Buildkite skips it. The results above come from runs outside CI.

## Details

- The change mirrors `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`: `SupportsLoRA` plus `get_mm_mapping()`. `packed_modules_mapping` (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`) was already declared, and the text model already uses vLLM parallel linear layers, so no layer changes are needed.
- `supports_tower_connector_lora` is left at its default (`False`). Embedding adapters for this model target the text decoder, and enabling tower LoRA would need `get_mm_lora_token_counts()`.
- Image tokens pass through the language model, so a LoRA request with an image input applies the adapter to those tokens as well, the same as Gemma 4. Serving base image embeddings means sending image requests without a `LoRARequest`.
- Adds the missing `EmbeddingGemma2Model` row to the multimodal embedding models table, with LoRA marked.
- Not a duplicate: before starting, I searched open and closed PRs and issues for EmbeddingGemma2, `embedding_gemma2` and LoRA on embedding/multimodal pooling models. #60254, #60289, #60280 and #60295 added and stabilised the model without LoRA. Open PRs #60631 (Triton prefill tiles) and #60009 (tensor registration) are unrelated.

Usage:

```python
from vllm import LLM
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

llm = LLM("google/embeddinggemma-2", runner="pooling", enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=32)
adapter = LoRARequest("nordic", 1, "/path/to/adapter")
out = llm.embed(
    ["task: search result | query: rød cykel",
     {"prompt": "<|image|>", "multi_modal_data": {"image": image}}],
    lora_request=[adapter, None],
)
```

AI assistance: Claude (Claude Code) was used to write the change, the test and this description. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer. The submitter reviews every changed line and the validation results before this leaves draft.

items.title: [Model] Add native TR-HASH support
items.body:
## Overview

Add native support for the public TR-HASH checkpoint, which currently fails architecture resolution. Closes #53286.

## Claims

- Load checkpoint-defined token routes and transposed, stacked expert weights without rebuilding the routing tables.
- Reuse vLLM attention, shared SwiGLU and fused MoE layers for prefill and decode, including tensor parallelism.
- Add checkpoint routing/generation coverage and document serving and future AutoRound export requirements.

## Validation

Public checkpoint revision: `0c6d56faae27e29eda9b7bd55e20297e2c0d0abe`. CPU, FP32, Transformers 5.18.0. Before this change, `LLM(..., trust_remote_code=True)` rejects `TRHashForCausalLM`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Six prompts × 12 greedy tokens, TP=1 | 72/72 tokens match Transformers; full-vocabulary logits max absolute error `7.20e-5` |
| Same panel, TP=2 | 72/72 tokens match; logits max absolute error `6.34e-5` |
| Batch of all six prompts, TP=1 and TP=2 | 72/72 tokens match in each run |
| Persisted routing | All 16 tables match exactly on each rank; regression checks routes and weights across all vocabulary IDs |
| OpenAI server | Model listing, completion, streaming completion and chat passed; completion text matches the reference |

Raw logits were collected from `compute_logits` and compared against cached Transformers decode at every step with `atol=rtol=1e-4`. Prompts: `Hello`, `The capital of France is`, `def add(a, b):\n    return`, `Explain gravity in one sentence.`, `1 + 1 =`, and `A short story about a cat:`. Generation used temperature 0 and ignored EOS for the 12-token panel.

Commands run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k TRHash -q
# 1 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/language/generation/test_tr_hash.py -v -s
# 1 passed; default compilation enabled
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/tr_hash.py vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py \
  tests/models/registry.py tests/models/language/generation/test_tr_hash.py \
  docs/models/supported_models.md
# All applicable hooks passed, also checked by commit hooks
```

The regression uses existing HF/vLLM fixtures and runs in the existing generation and CPU model jobs. CUDA/ROCm were not tested: this environment has no GPU. Remote pre-commit is gated by the repository's contributor check (0 merged PRs and no maintainer verification label); local hooks passed.

## Details

Each MLP receives the original token IDs and looks up its saved route table. A custom MoE router supplies those expert IDs and the configured route weights. The loader splits and transposes the stacked expert tensors, merges QKV/shared gate-up projections, and loads the integer route tables unchanged. Derived fused routing encodings are unused; no hashes are regenerated.

The implementation composes existing vLLM layers; no reference implementation source was copied. Quantization, prompt embeddings, expert parallelism and pipeline parallelism are explicitly unsupported in this first implementation. LoRA is not advertised. AutoRound W4A16 needs a compatible quantized expert export and must preserve the integer routing tables.

Checked the issue and comments, open PRs mentioning `53286` in their body, and open PRs matching `TR-HASH`; none cover this integration. AI assistance was used to implement and validate this change.

items.title: [Model] Add Jina v2 embedding support

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests

items.body:
## Overview

Add native embedding support for `jinaai/jina-embeddings-v2-small-en`. Fixes #48127.

## Claims

- Load `JinaBertForMaskedLM` checkpoints for mean-pooled embeddings without remote code.
- Support Jina's ALiBi attention and GeGLU layers using existing BERT and parallel layers.
- Correct CPU bidirectional ALiBi to penalize absolute distance; preserve causal attention.

## Validation

Built all three CPU extension variants from source. On CPU with eager execution, compared six texts (including empty input, Chinese and 602 tokens) against the upstream HF model under Transformers 4.57.6. Native inference used Transformers 5.18.0. The HF reference also matched Sentence Transformers exactly.

| Configuration | Minimum cosine similarity | Maximum absolute error |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FP32, TP=1 | 0.9999998 | 1.13e-6 |
| FP32, TP=2 | 0.9999999 | 8.94e-7 |
| BF16, TP=1 | 0.9999808 | 0.01104 |

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py -k bidirectional_alibi -q`: 6 passed. The bidirectional case failed before the kernel fix.
- `pytest tests/models/language/pooling/test_embedding.py -k jina_embedding_batching -q`: 1 passed; single and mixed-length batch outputs agree.
- `pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k JinaBert -q`: 1 passed.
- Full pre-commit passed for all changed files. Remote CI and docs are blocked by the contributor authorization gate.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the embedding comparison</summary>

Use the source checkout's `.venv/bin/python`. Keep the old HF dependency isolated, since upstream Jina remote code imports `transformers.onnx`, which was removed in Transformers 5.

```bash
uv pip install --target /tmp/jina-hf4 'transformers==4.57.6'
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/jina-hf4 .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
name = 'jinaai/jina-embeddings-v2-small-en'
revision = '44e7d1d6caec8c883c2d4b207588504d519788d0'
texts = ['The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.', 'A small sentence.',
         '', '你好，世界。', 'Embedding models turn text into vectors.', 'hello ' * 600]
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(name, revision=revision, trust_remote_code=True,
    code_revision='f3ec4cf7de7e561007f27c9efc7148b0bd713f81',
    max_position_embeddings=1024).eval()
inputs = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name, revision=revision)(
    texts, padding=True, return_tensors='pt')
with torch.inference_mode():
    hidden = model(**inputs).last_hidden_state
    mask = inputs['attention_mask'].unsqueeze(-1)
    embeddings = (hidden * mask).sum(1) / mask.sum(1)
torch.save({'texts': texts, 'embeddings': embeddings}, '/tmp/jina-reference.pt')
PY
cat > /tmp/check-jina.py <<'PY'
import os
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from vllm import LLM

def main():
    ref = torch.load('/tmp/jina-reference.pt', weights_only=True)
    llm = LLM(model='jinaai/jina-embeddings-v2-small-en',
        revision='44e7d1d6caec8c883c2d4b207588504d519788d0',
        runner='pooling', trust_remote_code=False, enforce_eager=True,
        dtype=os.getenv('JINA_DTYPE', 'float32'),
        tensor_parallel_size=int(os.getenv('JINA_TP', '1')),
        max_model_len=1024, max_num_seqs=6, max_num_batched_tokens=1024)
    actual = torch.tensor([out.outputs.embedding for out in llm.embed(ref['texts'])])
    print(F.cosine_similarity(actual, ref['embeddings']).min().item())
    print((actual - ref['embeddings']).abs().max().item())

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
PY
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 .venv/bin/python /tmp/check-jina.py
# Repeat with JINA_DTYPE=bfloat16 or JINA_TP=2, binding CPU threads per rank.
```

</details>

## Details

Jina uses no absolute position embeddings and has a bias-free fused gate projection followed by a biased output projection and residual layer norm. The new model reuses BERT attention/weight loading and the existing embedding pooler. CPU attention previously applied signed ALiBi distance to noncausal sequences, producing cosine similarities of only 0.93–0.97 on two short texts.

Checked issue comments, issue-number PR searches and Jina-v2/CPU-ALiBi searches; no matching open PR was found. Existing CPU PRs concern GEMM tiling or Zen decoder dispatch.

GPU execution and quantization were not tested. The HF comparison runs outside CI because its remote implementation requires Transformers 4; native registration, batching and kernel regressions run in existing CI suites. AI assistance was used.

items.body:
# [Model] Support EmbeddingGemma 2 (Omni-Modal Embeddings)

## Overview

This PR adds support for **EmbeddingGemma 2** (`google/embeddinggemma-2`), Google's bidirectional omni-modal embedding model. EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, image, audio, video, and interleaved multimodal inputs into a unified 768-dimensional L2-normalized vector space for cross-modal and multi-modal semantic search, retrieval, and classification.

## Claims

- **Omni-Modal Embedding Architecture**: Supports single-modal and joint/interleaved inputs across Text, Image, Audio, and Video producing unit-normalized 768-dim embeddings in a single forward pass.
- **Bidirectional Attention & RoPE**: Implements bidirectional attention (`ENCODER_ONLY`) with an inclusive sliding window of 513 tokens (`config.sliding_window + 1`) and 512-dim rotary embeddings (RoPE) across all layers, matching Hugging Face / SentenceTransformers semantics.
- **Upfront Dynamic Modality Loading**: Supports bypassing unused modality encoders at engine startup via `--limit-mm-per-prompt` (e.g., `image=0,audio=0,video=0`). Omitting vision (167.8M params) and audio (305.6M params) loads a lightweight 271.0M param text-only model (~517 MiB VRAM), saving up to 64% VRAM with zero post-load deletion.
- **Dedicated Video Sampling Backend**: Adds `EmbeddingGemma2VideoBackend` to `vllm/multimodal/video.py`, providing 1 fps uniform sampling up to 32 frames with duplicate-frame expansion for short clips (< 1s), exactly matching `EmbeddingGemma2VideoProcessor`.
- **Zero Generative Regressions**: Implemented cleanly as a standalone model in `vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py` without mutating existing generative Gemma 4 model classes (`gemma4.py`, `gemma4_mm.py`).
- **Validated Numerical Parity**: Achieves >= 0.999 cosine similarity against Hugging Face / SentenceTransformers across all 16 multimodal evaluation cases (text, image, audio, video, and mixed inputs).

## Validation

### Unit and Parity Tests

All 20 unit and numerical parity tests pass on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB:

```bash
# Run standalone unit and parity test suite
pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py -v

# Verify model registry loading
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "EmbeddingGemma2"
```

### CLI Serving Examples

```bash
# 1. Full Multimodal Serving (Text + Image + Audio + Video)
vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 \
    --runner pooling \
    --max-model-len 8192

# 2. Text-Only Deployment (Lightweight, ~517 MiB VRAM)
vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 \
    --runner pooling \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt image=0,audio=0,video=0 \
    --max-model-len 8192

# 3. Vision + Text Deployment (No Audio Tower)
vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 \
    --runner pooling \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt audio=0 \
    --max-model-len 8192
```

### Python API Example

```python
from vllm import LLM
from PIL import Image

# Initialize pooling model
llm = LLM(
    model="google/embeddinggemma-2",
    runner="pooling",
    max_model_len=8192,
)

# Text embedding
text_outputs = llm.embed(["Retrieve relevant documents for machine learning research"])
print("Text embedding shape:", len(text_outputs[0].outputs.embedding))  # 768

# Multimodal text + image embedding
image = Image.new("RGB", (224, 224), color=(73, 109, 137))
mm_outputs = llm.embed([{
    "prompt": "What is depicted in this image? <|image|>",
    "multi_modal_data": {"image": image},
}])
print("Multimodal embedding norm:", sum(x**2 for x in mm_outputs[0].outputs.embedding) ** 0.5)  # 1.0
```

### Numerical Parity Test Results

#### 1. Text Embeddings
```text
TEST: Text Embedding (Shape & Norm)
  Prompt:    "Hello world"
  Embedding: [-0.0598, +0.0352, +0.0593, -0.0393, -0.0352, ... +0.0396] (dim=768)
  Norm:      1.0000 (unit L2 norm)
✅ PASSED: Shape (768,) and unit norm

TEST: Text Semantic Similarity
  Cosine Sim (A vs B): 0.8914  [Semantically similar: high]
  Cosine Sim (A vs C): 0.6065  [Different topic: low]
✅ PASSED: Similar > dissimilar (0.8914 > 0.6065)

TEST: Batch vs Individual Consistency
  Min Cosine Similarity: 0.999967
✅ PASSED: Batch matches individual encodings (cosine sim > 0.9999)
```

#### 2. Image Embeddings
```text
TEST: Image Embedding (Shape & Norm)
  Norm:      1.0000 (unit L2-normalized)
✅ PASSED: Valid 768-dim image embedding

TEST: Image Discrimination
  Cosine Sim: 0.6324  [Distinct images]
✅ PASSED: Different images have distinct embeddings (0.6324 < 0.99)

TEST: Text + Image Joint Embedding
  Norm:      1.0000
✅ PASSED: Valid joint text+image embedding
```

#### 3. Audio Embeddings
```text
TEST: Audio Embedding (Shape & Norm)
  Norm:      1.0000 (unit L2-normalized)
✅ PASSED: Valid 768-dim audio embedding

TEST: Audio Discrimination
  Cosine Sim: 0.7116  [Distinct audio signals]
✅ PASSED: Different audio inputs have distinct embeddings (0.7116 < 0.99)

TEST: Text + Audio Joint Embedding
  Norm:      1.0000
✅ PASSED: Valid joint text+audio embedding
```

#### 4. Video Embeddings
```text
TEST: Video Embedding (Shape & Norm)
  Video Clip: synthetic_clip.mp4 (4.0s clip -> 4 sampled frames at fps=1)
  Norm:       1.0000 (unit L2-normalized)
✅ PASSED: Valid 768-dim video embedding

TEST: Text + Video Joint Embedding
  Text:       "A video clip showing conveyor belt operations"
  Norm:       1.0000
✅ PASSED: Valid joint text+video embedding

TEST: Video File Loader Input (MediaConnector / VideoMediaIO)
  Video File: file://synthetic_clip.mp4 (32 sampled frames, 3906 tokens)
  Norm:       1.0000
✅ PASSED: Valid video embedding via MediaConnector file loader
```

#### 5. HuggingFace / SentenceTransformer vs vLLM Parity (16/16 Passed)
```text
=========================================================================================================
Test Case                      | HF Norm  | vLLM Norm | HF Tok  | vLLM Tok | Cosine Sim  | Status
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Short text                     | 1.0028   | 1.0000    | 4       | 4        | 0.999946    | PASS
Sentence                       | 1.0000   | 1.0000    | 12      | 12       | 0.999836    | PASS
Technical paragraph            | 1.0037   | 1.0000    | 12      | 12       | 0.999955    | PASS
Task prompt (inlined)          | 1.0012   | 1.0000    | 15      | 15       | 0.999960    | PASS
Named prompt query             | 1.0012   | 1.0000    | 15      | 15       | 0.999960    | PASS
Long text > 512 tok            | 1.0015   | 1.0000    | 710     | 710      | 0.999883    | PASS
Long text > 1024 tok           | 1.0030   | 1.0000    | 1810    | 1810     | 0.999931    | PASS
Single image                   | 0.9991   | 1.0000    | 260     | 260      | 0.999985    | PASS
Text + Image                   | 0.9996   | 1.0000    | 265     | 265      | 0.999915    | PASS
Prompt + Image                 | 1.0016   | 1.0000    | 267     | 267      | 0.999944    | PASS
Prompt + Text + Image          | 1.0021   | 1.0000    | 273     | 273      | 0.999974    | PASS
Audio                          | 1.0023   | 1.0000    | 22      | 22       | 0.999933    | PASS
Text + Audio                   | 1.0027   | 1.0000    | 27      | 27       | 0.999907    | PASS
Video (frames + metadata)      | 1.0027   | 1.0000    | 368     | 368      | 0.999825    | PASS
Video (file loader)            | 1.0001   | 1.0000    | 3906    | 3906     | 0.999931    | PASS
Text + Image + Audio           | 1.0002   | 1.0000    | 284     | 284      | 0.999907    | PASS
=========================================================================================================
ALL 16 TEST CASES PASSED (token parity + cosine similarity >= 0.999)
```

## Details

### Architecture & Key Components

1. **Standalone Model Architecture (`vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py`)**:
   - `EmbeddingGemma2Model`: Inherits from `nn.Module`, `SupportsMultiModal`, and `VllmModelForPooling`. Integrates vision and audio modality encoders via `_mark_tower_model`, language model backbone (`EmbeddingGemma2TextModel`), and a `DispatchPooler.for_embedding` pooling head with `MEAN` pooling and L2 normalization.
   - `EmbeddingGemma2Attention`: Implements bidirectional attention across all layers using `ENCODER_ONLY` attention. For sliding-window layers, sets sliding window size to `config.sliding_window + 1` (513) to reconcile Hugging Face's `|q - k| <= W` condition with vLLM's `|q - k| < W` encoder attention kernel. Applies full 512-dim RoPE on global attention layers.
   - `EmbeddingGemma2TextPLE` & `EmbeddingGemma2PLEBlock`: Per-layer embedding projections matching the checkpoint weight schema.

2. **Multimodal Processing & Tokenization**:
   - `EmbeddingGemma2ProcessingInfo`: Retains standard `<bos>` and `<eos>` special tokens without applying chat templates, matching SentenceTransformers.
   - `EmbeddingGemma2MultiModalProcessor`: Dynamically budgets soft tokens (`max_soft_tokens=140` per video frame) and suppresses unconditional timestamp prefixing (`exclude_timestamps=True`). Safely masks multimodal placeholder tokens exceeding `vocab_size` before embedding lookups.

3. **Video Backend (`vllm/multimodal/video.py`)**:
   - Registers `EmbeddingGemma2VideoBackend` in `VIDEO_LOADER_REGISTRY` (`embedding_gemma2`).
   - Implements frame index computation mirroring `EmbeddingGemma2VideoProcessor.sample_frames`, with support for uniform overflow capping at 32 frames and duplicate frame expansion for short clips (< 1s).

4. **Configuration & Attention Capping (`vllm/model_executor/models/config.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py`)**:
   - `EmbeddingGemma2ModelConfig`: Automatically caps default `max_model_len` to 8192 (down from the 262k theoretical context) and syncs scheduler token limits while respecting explicit user limits.
   - Triton Prefill Attention: Limits block size to 32 for head dimensions >= 512 to avoid shared memory exhaustion during bidirectional prefill attention.

5. **Upfront Dynamic Modality Loading**:
   - Integrated with vLLM's `SupportsMultiModal` lifecycle: when a modality is disabled via `limit_mm_per_prompt` (e.g., `image=0,video=0` or `audio=0`), the corresponding encoder tower is created on `torch.device("meta")` and skipped during weight loading. Only active weights are loaded into VRAM.

items.title: [Model] Welcome Kolibri; add support for Kolibri-1
items.body:
## Overview
This change introduces [Kolibri](https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1). 

Kolibri is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model (78B total / 3.46B active parameters), focused on German and English, with selectable reasoning effort and tool calling. Until now it has been served through an out-of-tree [plugin](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/aleph-alpha-inference); this PR adds native support.

`Kolibri1ForCausalLM` reuses the Qwen3-MoE model, decoder layer and MoE block,
with these differences:
- 4:1 sliding-window (513 tokens) to full attention with RoPE only on sliding-window layers, no positional encoding on full-attention layers.
- Sandwich norms after attention and after the MoE.
- 384 routed experts (top-6) plus one shared expert without a shared-expert gate.
- Router: fp32 logits, top-k selection on `logits + bias` and the weights are `sigmoid(logits)`. This differs from the built-in `scoring_func="sigmoid"`, which selects on `sigmoid(logits) + bias`.

The attention, MoE block and `ForCausalLM` constructors are re-implemented, because the Qwen3-MoE versions always apply RoPE, only support a gated shared expert, and hard-code the model class.

The `kolibri1` reasoning parser is based on the Qwen3 grammar, with the starting state taken from the Kolibri 1 chat template, where `reasoning_effort` takes precedence over `enable_thinking`.
Also adds the `kolibri1` tool parser name, which maps to `Hermes2ProToolParser`, `Kolibri1Config`, and updates `supported_models.md`, `reasoning_outputs.md` and `tool_calling.md`.

For model accuracy in FP8 checkpoints, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM` and `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0` default to 0, since E8M0 would round the checkpoint's fp32 block scales to powers of two, and DeepGEMM on Blackwell only accepts UE8M0 scales. These are process-wide switches, so this follows the existing `scale_fmt: ue8m0` handling in `get_config`. User-set values win, and the model refuses to load if `E8M0` is still in use or DeepGEMM is re-enabled on Blackwell.

There are no PRs or issues mentioning Kolibri.

## Test Plan
```
# Custom MoE router 
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k kolibri1

# Custom reasoning parser
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_kolibri1.py

# Registry and initialization
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Kolibri1

# Serving
vllm serve Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 \
    --reasoning-parser kolibri1 --tool-call-parser kolibri1 --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

## Test Result

- Routing: 5 passed. Parser: 13 passed. Registry and initialization: 2 passed (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell).
- The two non-streaming starting-state tests, fail with the stock `qwen3` reasoning parser, since qwen3 reads enable_thinking alone.
- Against the server above: JSON-schema and regex structured outputs (thinking on and off) and tool calls (streaming and non-streaming).
- CI has no end-to-end correctness test, since the model is 78B and Transformers has no `kolibri1` implementation to compare against. Instead we report a benchmark score comparison below.

## Validation

AIME2026 avg@16 with [eval-framework](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha-Research/eval-framework) on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, with the [tech report](https://aleph-alpha.com/downloads/tech-report.pdf)'s settings: 256k-token window, reasoning effort high, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.97, top_k 128.
(Note AIME was chosen as a benchmark due to the very long rollouts used. Long rollouts tend to be much more sensitive on changes)

| Checkpoint | Setup | AIME2026 avg@16 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tech report |  | 96.0 |
| `Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1-BF16` | TP2 | 96.5 |
| `Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1` (FP8) | TP1 | 96.7 |

with a standard error of ±3.1 across the 30 problems.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 --served-model-name kolibri \
    --max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser kolibri1 \
    --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort": "high"}'

eval_framework --llm-name eval_framework.llm.openai.OpenAIModel \
    --llm-args model_name=kolibri base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1 api_key=EMPTY \
    --task-suite aime_suite.py --output-dir results
```

```python
# aime_suite.py
from eval_framework.suite import TaskSuite

suite = TaskSuite(
    name="aime2026-kolibri",
    temperature=1.0,
    top_p=0.97,
    max_tokens=261000,
    repeats=16,
    tasks=[TaskSuite(tasks="AIME2026")],
)
```

Note: the openai client's timeout was extended.
</details>

items.body:
## Overview


Adds complete-audio transcription support for `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b`.

Related to #47455. Native cache-aware realtime streaming is intentionally out of scope for this PR; the required persistent streaming-state and lifecycle support is being explored separately in the vLLM-Omni RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5212.

## Claims



- Supports transcription through `/v1/audio/transcriptions`.
- Reuses Transformers encoder, RNN-T predictor, and joint-network components with model-local vLLM processing and execution adapters.
- Supports batched greedy RNN-T decoding with isolated per-request state.
- Does not modify dependency versions or generic serving/scheduler logic.

## Validation



Local environment: RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Transformers 5.16.1.

**Commands run**:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron3_5_asr.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/test_nemotron3_5_asr.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_nemotron3_5_asr.py -q

python -m pre_commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD
```

**Results**:

- 31 focused tests passed.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
- Real-checkpoint transcription completed for 26.3-second, 30-second, and five-minute WAV inputs.
- The 26.3-second transcript matched Transformers exactly.
- The 30-second and five-minute inputs completed successfully but produced empty transcripts, so these were treated as execution smoke tests rather than accuracy checks.

## Details



The implementation targets Model Runner V2 with eager execution and currently supports TP=1 / PP=1. It performs greedy RNN-T decoding with isolated per-request acoustic and predictor state.

Because RNN-T token selection happens inside the model-specific decoding loop, the adapter exposes synthetic selected-token logprobs to vLLM’s sampler. These values preserve the selected token but must not be interpreted as model confidence. Unsupported execution and sampling features are documented in the model notes.

Native cache-aware realtime streaming is outside the scope of this PR and is being explored separately in the linked vLLM-Omni RFC.

AI assistance was used during implementation and review. The resulting code and changes were manually reviewed, tested, and validated locally before submission.

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Check draft model support for FlashInfer large pages
[Model][DCP] Support Qwen4Exp QSA
items.body:
## Purpose Enable decode context parallelism (DCP) for Qwen4Exp QSA. Each rank reads its own shard of the main KV cache. The QSA selector and its side caches stay replicated on every rank. The ranks then combine their partial results with the base-2 log-sum-exp convention that QSA uses. Five further changes make this work: - The selector and the main KV cache share one block table. In separate groups the selector takes most of the blocks that a request needs, and DCP loses capacity instead of gaining it. - A packed compressed cache binds one whole manager block. Its kernel blocks are mapped afterwards through the stride between manager blocks. Without this the server stops at startup, because a packed block cannot be cut into evenly spaced kernel blocks. - The QSA side caches skip their stores when the block table points at the null block. - Every attention metadata builder in a group takes the block table row width that the runner allocated. A replicated layer in a DCP-sharded group has a larger block than the group, so a builder that derives the width from its own layer spec sizes its kernel block table too small. The mapping now rejects a row that does not fit instead of writing past it. - QSA marks its compression work inactive while CUDA graphs are captured. A capture batch has no real history behind its blocks, so an active work item reads positions that were never written. Without this, full graph capture fails when DCP and speculative decoding are both on. An empty DCP batch now returns both an output tensor and a log-sum-exp tensor. Draft #61242 covers the same feature with a sharded selector. This PR keeps the selector replicated, so selection stays identical to DCP=1. ## Test commands Focused suites: ```bash pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_dcp_localize.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_selector_write_mask.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py ``` Serving command. Set `--decode-context-parallel-size` to 1 or 2. Only the MTP runs pass `--speculative-config`: ```bash VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --decode-context-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 256 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Load, AIPerf 0.12.0, started with `aiperf profile -f agentx.yaml`. In this scenario `concurrency: 128` is the number of multi-turn conversations that stay open at the same time. A conversation pauses between its turns, so it does not hold one request in flight at all times. The measured number of requests in flight is in the results table. ```yaml schemaVersion: "2.0" randomSeed: 42 benchmark: scenario: inferencex-agentx-mvp model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 tokenizer: name: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 trustRemoteCode: true endpoint: url: http://127.0.0.1:8000 path: /v1/chat/completions type: chat streaming: true useServerTokenCount: true extra: ignore_eos: true dataset: type: public dataset: semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k entries: 393 maxContextLength: 262144 cacheBust: target: first_turn_prefix phases: type: concurrency concurrency: 128 duration: 900 trajectoryStartMinRatio: 0.0 trajectoryStartMaxRatio: 1.0 systemIdleGapCapSeconds: 10 gpuTelemetry: enabled: false serverMetrics: http://127.0.0.1:8000/metrics artifacts: sliceDuration: 1.0 ``` GSM8K, EvalScope 1.12.0, three repeats with a fresh server each time. The generation config comes from the file in this repository: ```bash for run in 1 2 3; do RUN="$run" python - <<'PYTHON' import os from pathlib import Path import yaml from evalscope.run import run_task c = yaml.safe_load( Path("tests/evals/qwen4_exp/configs/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8.yaml").read_text() ) reports = run_task({ "model": c["model_name"], "api_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", "api_key": "EMPTY_TOKEN", "datasets": ["gsm8k"], "eval_batch_size": 64, "generation_config": c["generation_config"], "work_dir": f"gsm8k-run-{os.environ['RUN']}", "no_timestamp": True, "limit": None, }) r = reports["gsm8k"] s = r.execution_summary assert s is not None and not s.incomplete assert (s.requested, s.succeeded, s.errored, r.num) == (1319, 1319, 0, 1319) print(f"GSM8K run {os.environ['RUN']}: {r.score:.4f}") PYTHON done ``` MRCR, one warmup and five scored repeats. The seed fixes the 24 samples, so every run scored the same items: ```bash for run in 0 1 2 3 4 5; do python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py \ --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \ --num-samples 24 --needles 2 4 8 \ --max-prompt-tokens 259840 --max-tokens 2048 \ --seed 42 --concurrency 24 \ --save-results "mrcr-run-$run.json" done ``` ## Unit test results The suites in the commands above ran together on four B200 GPUs: 207 passed, no skips. Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` passed. ## Serving results All four runs used four B200 GPUs in one node, with the same source commit and checkpoint. Each run used a fresh server and a prefix-cache reset. Every scored workload had zero request errors. The table gives the mean and the peak number of requests in flight that each run measured. Output tokens per second per GPU divides the measured output rate by the four GPUs. Output tokens per second per user is the mean rate of one request stream. Time to first token is given at the median and at the 95th percentile, because the median alone can hide a slow tail. | DCP | MTP | KV tokens | Requests/s | Completions | Requests in flight, mean / peak | Output tokens/s per GPU | Output tokens/s per user | TTFT p50 | TTFT p95 | | ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | off | 9,764,101 | 1.642852 | 1,495 | 58.4 / 95 | 343.3 | 31.7 | 874.5 ms | 5,389.1 ms | | 2 | off | 17,585,863 | 2.330763 | 2,121 | 51.8 / 79 | 485.4 | 42.3 | 553.4 ms | 2,363.0 ms | | 1 | on | 8,396,119 | 0.981313 | 893 | 53.1 / 69 | 185.7 | 25.2 | 4,996.9 ms | 22,640.1 ms | | 2 | on | 14,565,287 | 2.142851 | 1,950 | 51.9 / 85 | 443.0 | 44.1 | 733.9 ms | 5,059.2 ms | DCP=2 lowered time to first token at both MTP settings, and at the same time raised throughput. items.title: [Attention][MLA] Support fp8_ds_mla KV cache for NoPE-512 models on SM90

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Purpose

This supersedes #55543 by @Leoyzen, who is kept as co-author. It enables the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM90 for rope-free sparse-MLA models with head_size 512, such as GLM-5.3-Flash, through `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`.

On H100, plain `fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (with the fix from #55222) holds more tokens. FlashMLA is still clearly faster at long-context decode: up to +31% output throughput and −29% TPOT at 16k input (see the benchmarks below). The PR adds FlashMLA as an opt-in with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`. Default backend selection doesn't change.

The idea is the same as in #55543: keep the DeepSeek 656B row and leave the RoPE slot at zero. This version keeps all of the logic inside the backend.

**How it works**
- **Cache write:** nothing changes. `concat_and_cache_mla` already zero-fills the RoPE slot when `pe_dim == 0` .
- **Query:** `FlashMLASparseImpl` sets `q_head_size = kv_lora_rank + 64` for NoPE on `fp8_ds_mla`.
  - Its q workspaces are sized from `q_head_size`.
  - `forward_mqa` zero-pads the query to that width, so q_pe · 0 = 0.
  - This covers the tuple path, the mixed and prefill paths, and DCP, where the gathered query arrives unpadded.
- **Dense-MHA prefill:** the impl sets `supports_dense_mha_prefill = False` for this layout, because the dense prefill workspace is `kv_lora_rank` wide and cannot hold the 576-wide rows. The SM120 FlashInfer impl does the same.
  - #55543 left this path on, where the FA prefill backend would see a 320-wide head.
  - `AttentionImpl.supports_dense_mha_prefill` drops `ClassVar` so it can be set per instance.
- **Backend selection:**
  - `FLASHMLA_SPARSE.supports_combination` now accepts `fp8_ds_mla` for SM90 NoPE-512.

**Compared with #55543**
- Removed:
  - the global zero buffer
  - the string check on the backend name
  - the model and wrapper hooks in `mla_attention.py`, `sparse_mla_attention.py`, `mla.py` and the glm5next attention
  - the hard-coded insert index in `cuda.py`
- The test fixtures compute the fp8_ds_mla row size as `kv_lora_rank + 16 + 128`, since the RoPE slot is always present.

## Duplicate check

- #55543 is the original PR and is superseded by this one.
- #58892 changes the SM90 backend priority for bf16 NoPE; this PR is orthogonal to it.
- #55222 fixes plain `fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`. It is a different cache format and backend, and the two PRs complement each other.
- #58305 and #53969 are SM120-only.

## Benchmarks (H100, GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8)

- **FI** is `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`, with the #55222 plan-dtype fix applied.
- **FlashMLA** is `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` (this PR).
- Both use the same code and differ only in that flag.
- MTP is off. The workload is `vllm bench serve` with random data and `--ignore-eos`.
- Prompts per run: 16 at C=1, 32 at C=8, 128 at C=32.

**Long context: 16k in / 256 out**

| C | out tok/s FI → FlashMLA | TPOT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA | TTFT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 95 → 102 (+7%) | 6.11 → 5.94 | 1128 → 1001 |
| 8 | 257 → 337 (**+31%**) | 20.5 → 14.6 (**−29%**) | 2717 → 2340 |
| 32 | 347 → 414 (**+19%**) | 74.4 → 62.4 (−16%) | 4552 → 3782 |

**Short context: 1k in / 128 out**

| C | out tok/s FI → FlashMLA | TPOT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA | TTFT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 144 → 146 | 6.05 → 5.92 | 123 → 122 |
| 8 | 685 → 706 (+3%) | 9.09 → 8.67 | 340 → 349 |
| 32 | 1241 → 973 (−22%) | 21.8 → 24.9 | 518 → 1039 |

**KV capacity:** 3.63M tokens with FI vs 2.83M with FlashMLA. The ratio is 1.28, which is the 512B vs 656B row size.

**Trade-off:**
- FlashMLA wins long-context decode.
- FI holds 28% more tokens and does better on short prompts at high concurrency. The C=32 short-prompt gap is most likely prefill; it is not profiled yet.
- The numbers above are single runs.

## Test Plan / Results (H100)

- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashmla_nope_sm90_backend_selection.py`: 34 passed.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k decode_correctness`: 168 passed, 1176 skipped. This includes the new `glm53_flash_nope` case on `fp8_ds_mla` and the DeepSeek regression cases.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k ds_mla`: 3 passed, 5 skipped. The skips are for other architectures or nvfp4.
- `pre-commit` passes, including mypy.
- **Accuracy:** GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8, MTP with 5 spec tokens, GSM8K 5-shot on all 1319 questions.

  | kv cache | backend | GSM8K |
  |---|---|---|
  | fp8_ds_mla (this PR) | FLASHMLA_SPARSE | 0.918 |
  | fp8 (+ #55222 fix) | FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 | 0.913 |

**Not covered:** HiSparse, and DCP end to end. The DCP padding path is checked only by reading the code.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to rework the original PR, write the tests and run the benchmarks and evaluations. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

items.title: [Model][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support DCP for the kpool sparse indexer
items.body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot run with decode context parallelism. Its kpool sparse indexer compresses the indexer KV (`index_kpool=4`), and the indexer metadata builder rejects DCP whenever `compress_ratio > 1`. This check does not depend on the platform or the attention backend:

```
NotImplementedError: DCP is not supported with sparse indexer KV compression (compress_ratio=4)
```

This PR shards the kpool indexer across DCP ranks by pool:

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` must be a multiple of `index_kpool` (e.g. 4), so each compressed pool lives entirely on one rank. The builder now raises a clear error when this does not hold.
- `CompressedSlotMappingKernel` is DCP-aware. Each rank writes only the compressed states it owns, at rank-local positions. Prefill chunk metadata uses the interleave measured in compressed units.
- Each rank scores its local pools, takes a local top-k, and merges it across ranks with the existing DSA DCP global top-k merge (`_merge_dcp_topk_global`), using the interleave in pool units. The result is global token ids, which the sparse MLA backend already filters and localizes under DCP.
- The CuteDSL DCP merge warmup keys use pool-level top-k and interleave for kpool models.
- The raw kpool tail ring (`KpoolTailSpec`) stays replicated on every DCP rank, like Mamba state. Its pages are self-addressed (`uses_slot_mapping=False`), so `resolve_kv_cache_layout` no longer treats it as a replicated draft group that requires a block-outer layout.
- Unchanged: DeepSeek-V4 compressed KV stays unsupported under DCP, and ROCm kpool raises explicitly.

## Repro

On `main`, this fails at engine startup with the error above. On Blackwell, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` supports DCP; the indexer builder check applies on any platform.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8
```

With this PR, set the interleave to a multiple of `index_kpool`:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4
```

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
    tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

New tests:
- `test_compressed_slot_mapping_dcp_uses_rank_local_state_positions`: each DCP rank writes only its own compressed states, at rank-local slots.
- `test_dcp_replicated_kpool_tail_keeps_block_interior_layout`: a replicated kpool tail does not force a block-outer layout.

E2E: GSM8K (1319 questions) at 5, 25, 50 and 100 shots with `vllm serve` at TP8 + DCP8 + `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`, compared with TP8 alone (bf16 KV, no MTP).

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 309 passed on 1×H100. The 2 failures are `test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_*`, which need more than 1 GPU for their PP config and are unrelated to this change.
- E2E was run on 8×H100 together with a separate local SM90 attention-backend change that Hopper needs for DCP at head_dim 512 (out of scope here). I did not have Blackwell hardware to run this PR on its own.

| Config | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.911 – 0.922 |
| TP8 + DCP8 (interleave 4) | 0.916 |

5-shot GSM8K prompts are shorter than `index_topk` (2048 tokens), so that eval only lightly exercises the cross-rank top-k selection. To cover longer contexts, I raised the shot count. Both configs ran on the same build:

| Shots | Prompt tokens | TP8 | TP8 + DCP8 (interleave 4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | ~650 | 0.916 | 0.913 |
| 25 | ~4.3k | 0.909 | 0.917 |
| 50 | ~8.5k | 0.920 | 0.920 |
| 100 | ~16.9k | 0.926 | 0.922 |

Accuracy matches TP8 at every length, including 100 shots (about 8× `index_topk`). Prefix caching was on, so the shared few-shot prefix is mostly a cache hit, while decode and the question chunks run the top-k selection over the full context.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs and issues for GLM-5.3-Flash / kpool / sparse-indexer DCP and found none that enables DCP for compressed indexer KV. #57161 reworks kpool compression and scheduling but does not touch DCP.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed the changes and ran the tests above.

items.title: [Feat] Support PP with PCP in GPU Model Runner V2
items.body:
## Purpose

Enable pipeline parallelism (PP) together with Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) in GPU Model Runner V2 for MLA models.

The last PP stage restores PCP-local hidden states to global request order before sampling. Earlier PP stages use the global request batch when receiving sampled tokens and updating request state, while model forward continues on the PCP-local batch.

Related to #25749 and #50853. Open PRs #33403, #49109, #49246, and #53948 address other PCP or PP paths; none covers this Model Runner V2 request mapping for PP feedback.

AI assistance was used to prepare the implementation, tests, and validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- PP2+PCP2 initializes and completes generation for an MLA model in Model Runner V2.
- Sampled-token feedback on earlier PP stages updates the correct global requests. Hidden-state restoration occurs on the last PP stage before sampling.
- Mixed-length requests, including chunked prefill, preserve generated tokens and logprob counts relative to PCP2 in the functional topology check.
- A full real-model dataset evaluation in FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graph mode completes every request and reports accuracy alongside a PCP2 control.

## Test Plan

~~~bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_non_last_pp_rank_uses_global_batch_for_sample_feedback
~~~

Run Ruff check and format on the three changed files. Compare PCP2 and PP2+PCP2 using a two-layer, randomly initialized DeepSeek-V3.2 FP8 model with one 607-token and one 7-token prompt, eight output tokens each, and prompt/output logprobs.

Evaluate DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat on all 1,319 GSM8K test questions with the same five-shot chat prompts, greedy decoding, and 256-token output limit in PCP2 and PP2+PCP2. Both runs use BF16, expert parallelism, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs, and VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0 on NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPUs.

## Test Result

items.title: [Model][LoRA] Add tower/connector LoRA support for Nemotron Nano/Omni VL (vision + audio)
items.body:
## Purpose

Adds LoRA support for the vision tower (RADIO ViT), audio tower (Parakeet
conformer encoder), and their respective connectors on
`NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2` / `NemotronH_Nano_Omni_Reasoning_V3`, using the
existing `enable_tower_connector_lora` mechanism. Language-model-only LoRA
for this model already works today; this PR extends it to the multimodal
towers and connectors.

- Swaps `nn.Linear` → `ReplicatedLinear` in the vision/audio connectors
  (`mlp1`, `ParakeetProjection`) and the Parakeet encoder's non-shared
  linears, so they can receive LoRA deltas.
- Adds `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` so the multimodal LoRA runtime can
  size its per-modality tower/connector token budgets for image, video,
  and audio inputs (fixed-resolution, dynamic-resolution, and precomputed
  embeddings paths).
- Adds `hf_to_vllm_mapper` rename rules so PEFT-style LoRA checkpoint keys
  for the RADIO vision tower (`vision_model.radio_model.model.blocks.*`)
  and the audio projection (`sound_projection.*`) resolve to the correct
  vLLM module paths.

## Bugfix included in this PR

`get_mm_lora_token_counts()`'s single-image fast path only recognized a
flat `(height, width)` pair when it arrived as a `tuple`:

```python
if (
    isinstance(sizes_data, tuple)
    and len(sizes_data) == 2
    and all(isinstance(dim, int) for dim in sizes_data)
):
    image_sizes = [sizes_data]
else:
    image_sizes = list(sizes_data)
```

In practice, `MultiModalKwargsItem` stores this as a plain `list` (e.g.
`[448, 640]`) for a single image, not a `tuple`. That falls through to the
multi-image branch, which then tries to unpack the bare `int` `448` as
`(height, width)`:

```
TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable int object
```

This crashed the **entire engine core** on any real single-image request
once `--enable-tower-connector-lora` was set — including requests with no
LoRA adapter attached at all, since the flag makes vLLM call this path
unconditionally for every image request. Fixed by also accepting `list`.

## Test Plan

Unit tests (`tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py`, all
mocked, no GPU/weights required):

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py -q
# 16 passed
```

End-to-end validation on real hardware against
`nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16` (4x A6000,
`vllm serve --enable-lora --enable-tower-connector-lora`):

1. **Vision**: built a zero-init LoRA adapter (`lora_B = 0`) targeting all
   32 RADIO ViT blocks' `attn.qkv/proj`, `mlp.fc1/fc2`, plus the `mlp1`
   connector (130 modules). Compared greedy-decoded output on a real image
   with/without the adapter attached: **identical text, bit-exact
   logprobs** (`max abs diff = 0.0`), confirming the no-op composition is
   correct.
2. Built a second, non-zero-init adapter on the same 130 modules. Compared
   against the zero-init adapter and base: **materially different
   output** (hallucinated an unrelated scene), confirming the LoRA path
   is genuinely applied, not silently skipped.
3. **Audio**: repeated the same zero-init vs. non-zero-init vs. base
   protocol on the Parakeet encoder + `sound_projection` connector (195
   modules: 24 conformer layers' `q/k/v/o_proj`, both feed-forward
   linears, `subsampling.linear`, plus the connector) using a real audio
   clip. Same result: zero-init is bit-exact vs. base, non-zero-init
   meaningfully changes the transcription/description.
4. **Combined**: built adapters spanning vision (130) + audio (195) + the
   LLM's 6 full-attention layers' `q/k/v/o_proj` (24, via the standard
   `packed_modules_mapping` fusion into `qkv_proj` — unrelated to this
   PR's tower/connector mechanism, included to confirm the two paths
   compose correctly) — 349 modules total. Sent a single request with an
   image, audio, and text prompt together: zero-init adapter reproduced
   the base model's output exactly; non-zero-init adapter caused
   incoherent generation, confirming end-to-end composition across both
   modalities and the LLM.
5. Loaded a real, separately-trained LoRA adapter (rank 32, rsLoRA,
   trained on the vision tower) and verified it produces coherent,
   on-distribution generations through this code path.

All adapters, test images/audio, and scripts used above are available on
request if reviewers want to reproduce.

## Notes for reviewers

- `enable_tower_connector_lora` remains opt-in and is logged as
  experimental; this PR doesn't change that.
- LLM-side LoRA in the "combined" test above uses the existing, unrelated
  `packed_modules_mapping` mechanism (already supported for this model's
  language model) — it's exercised only to confirm composition, not
  something this PR adds.
- MoE and Mamba mixer layers in the language model are out of scope for
  LoRA in this PR (as before) — only the vision/audio towers and
  connectors are new here.
